News.title: Shocking moment migrant boat ploughs into swimmer, 17, leaving her seriously injured as men on board refuse to stop
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a migrant boat ploughs into a teenage swimmer leaving her seriously injured.

Astonishing footage showed a vessel striking the tourist, 17, before it continued to make a beeline for the coast without stopping to help her.



The small boat was carrying 14 migrants when it collided with the teenager about 200m off Su Giudeu Beach in Sardinia, Italy.

In the clip of the smash, which took place on August 16, the vessel can be seen speeding towards the coast.



Moments later, it crashes into a girl who appears to be swimming in the clear blue sea.

The teen, who was on holiday, suffered several fractures as a result of the collision.

She was also knocked out and left unconscious – which put her at risk of drowning in the water.

Bystanders on the beach rushed to help her before emergency services were called.



She was airlifted to a hospital in Cagliari and put in intensive care in serious condition.

The victim’s state is understood to have improved in the days following the crash.

She has since been moved out of the intensive care unit, according to local media.

The alleged driver of the boat, a 28-year-old Algerian man, has been arrested on suspicion of facilitating illegal immigration and causing extremely serious bodily injuries.

A boy, 16, who was swimming with the girl at the time of the horror said he managed to dodge the vessel at the last second.



He told local media: “I was with her, I moved out of the way and saved myself.

“After the impact, they stopped, looked at us and ran away.”

He also claimed the men on the boat definitely knew their vessel had just struck the girl.

He said: “It’s not true that they didn’t realise what had happened.”

The boat – a fibreglass vessel powered by an 85-horsepower outboard motor – appeared to continue towards Tuerredda Beach following the smash.

Those on board allegedly disembarked the vessel after it reached the coast and tried to get away on foot.

Police later tracked down all of the passengers, who are understood to be a group of Algerian men.

News.title: Nappies, dummies & a web of lies… how did a 38-year-old woman convince couple she was girl, 11 & get adopted for a YEAR?
News.content:
CHILD HOODWINKED Nappies, dummies & a web of lies… how did a 38-year-old woman convince couple she was girl, 11 & get adopted for a YEAR?

AS police officers led the little girl away, the woman who had taken her in and cared for her pleaded with them to let her fetch a sweater because ‘She might be cold.’

It was the last heartbreaking moment in a con that had stretched for more than a year.



The shivering little girl was no vulnerable child but a 38-year-old career conwoman with a long history of deception.

To fool her latest victims she had sucked a dummy, drunk from a baby bottle, carried a comfort blanket, and talked to her adopted family in a baby voice.



But just moments before she was taken away, as police swooped, the mask had fallen.

“The charade is over,” said police chief Rodrigo Gusso, as he confronted 38-year-old Amanda Maria Souza de Oliveira, on a bed strewn with dolls and kids toys.



She looked up from her lunch, smoothed down her heart-print shorts, stared the chief in the eye and said, in her normal deep voice: “Should I come with you?”

The con had been running for 14 months, when Amanda, calling herself Gabriele, spotted her latest victims – a middle-aged couple in the southern city of Joinville.



She had first got to know them at the evangelical church they attended.

Later, Amanda walked into the little bakery they own, claiming she was 18 and an experienced baker.

She pleaded for work and a place to stay, saying she was in trouble with money and her health, and the kind-hearted couple took her in.

She had chosen her latest targets well. The mother, investigators said, was heartbroken and vulnerable after her son had left home.

When she had won their trust her story changed – and her age.



And her elaborate backstory unfolded. Amanda claimed to be an 11-year-old runaway, fleeing a monstrous, abusive father.

The couple showered her with love. She was given her own bedroom, filled with toys and dolls.

When some raised concerns about her grown-up appearance, she claimed to have been force fed hormones during a period of abuse when she was younger.

Everywhere she went she worked to the same script. She kept a hood up, rarely met an adult’s eye and shrank from being seen in person.



She panicked whenever anyone mentioned the authorities, always pleading that her father would track her down. She talked the couple out of enrolling her in school and out of formalising any adoption, warning that any paper trail might alert the father she had fled.

Sources close to the case said that for more than a year, she took cash from them to carry out simple tasks – £28 to brush her teeth, £140 to stop wearing nappies.

She spent the money on shopping trips, although her lawyers said her con was more about being cared for than cash.

She even invented a fellow character to back up her story. ‘Pastor Barbara’ vouched she had sheltered Amanda before and had tried to win custody of her.



Barbara only ever messaged by text, never a call or a voice note, and made exactly the same spelling mistakes Amanda did.

The account fell silent the instant Amanda was arrested.

Other messages, later pulled from her mobile, show her throwing a crisis whenever the family paid attention to their own nephews and nieces.

She sulked over photographs of them and complained that they were prettier children than her.

The fewer people around, police concluded, the fewer there were to grow suspicious.



For her 12th birthday, the doting couple printed invitations and threw her a party.

But earlier this year a desperate relative began digging online, found reports of Amanda’s near-identical scams in other parts of Brazil and alerted the family.

On June 2, officers arrived at the house. She insisted she had never been after money. Asked what she had actually taken from the family, she replied: “Only food, clothes, a place to sleep, those things.”

Asked by the defence’s own psychiatrists whether she had set out to con anyone, she said: “Of course I deceived them, I lied, but not with that intention.”

What she wanted, she said, was simpler and stranger than greed. “I just want to be cared for in a way that doesn’t match my age.”



Her case has gripped Brazil, splashed across national newspapers, prime-time news and call-in shows.

On Instagram alone her story has generated almost 200 million views.

“This is a huge number, on par with the biggest political news stories in Brazil,” said Pablo Ortellado, a professor of public policy and management at the University of São Paulo. He said the story drew so much attention “because it’s so unusual.”



“She is a woman who did not look 25, let alone 12, yet managed to deceive a family,” he said.

“That unusual and implausible nature sparks immense interest and curiosity.”

Amanda, from Ceará, Brazil, had spent well over a decade posing as a vulnerable girl and living off the kindness of anyone soft-hearted enough to take her in.

The country now knows the serial scammer as Pequena Amanda, Little Amanda.

Back in the late 2000s, in her twenties, she is said to have walked into a police station claiming to be 12, accusing her own parents of abusing her and forcing her into sex work.



Police have linked her to the same con across at least seven states, always closing in on families through churches and shelters.

She has a conviction behind her in Goiás, faces further cases in two more states, and once spent six months in prison in Porto Alegre.

Down the years she has been Julia, Emily, Duda and more.

As “Emily,” a 13-year-old supposedly dying of leukaemia during the pandemic, she moved one woman so deeply that she had the fake child’s name tattooed on her wrist.



Posing as an autistic abuse victim called Duda in Rio de Janeiro, she was later found to have used her phone to search “how does an autistic person behave” and “how to draw as if you were a victim of abuse.”

One woman she fooled said Amanda “puts on a character like a coat.”

In 2020, she walked into a children’s shelter as Julia, a 12-year-old who said she was running from a father who dabbled in the occult and had forced her into prostitution.

Staff swallowed every word until a medical exam a week later found she was a grown woman.

She simply walked out, and disappeared, ready to begin again somewhere new.



An older file, drawn up when she was in her twenties, recorded psychiatric admissions, self-harm and the same lifelong habit of shrinking herself into a child under a borrowed name.

During her latest trial, the official psychiatric report found she had antisocial personality disorder but understood exactly what she was doing, with one examiner noting her manipulation and total absence of remorse.

Her own experts said she was a broken woman who needed treatment, not a cell.

Judge Rogerio Manke was unmoved, ruling she knew right from wrong and chose wrong regardless.

Her lawyers insist to this day that she is a survivor, not a swindler. Her lawyer Lúcio Sousa said “all the evidence” showed she had cost her latest victims nothing.



“She admits that she invented an identity,” he said. “It was the way she found to survive. But she has been a vulnerable person for more than 20 years.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But Judge Manke pushed the sentence well above the minimum, describing what he called “a genuine way of life built on taking on false identities to live at other people’s expense.”

She was found guilty of fraud and false identity and sentenced to one year, 10 months and 28 days. In an adult prison.

News.title: Mystery as US military plane lands at Moscow airport as Kremlin ‘has no information on aircraft’
News.content:
AN American plane has touched down at Moscow airport on an unexplained flight from Latvia.

The US transport plane landed at Vnukovo International Airport, located west of the Russian capital, at around 7am this morning, flight tracking data showed.



The plane had arrived in Latvia’s capital Riga on August 23 after flying from the US Camp Springs airbase near Washington DC.

Two days later the US Air Force Boeing C-17 flew two hours to Moscow.



What or who was on the plane remains a mystery.

The US government did not release any information on the plane.

And the Kremlin claimed to have no knowledge of the flight.

Putin’s spokesman said when asked about the flight: “No, I don’t have that information.”

The last direct flight by a US jet to Russia was in January, when special envoys Steven Witkoff and Jared Kushner visited the country for peace talks with Vladimir Putin.

Russia’s government last week said they had no information on another visit from Kushner and Witkoff.

News.title: Man, 34, arrested after 14-year-old girl ‘raped by stranger in broad daylight’ at woodland
News.content:
'RAPE' PROBE Man, 34, arrested after 14-year-old girl ‘raped by stranger in broad daylight’ at woodland

A 34-YEAR-OLD man has been arrested after a teenage girl was allegedly raped by a stranger in a woodland.

Cops scrambled to the scene after reports that a 14-year-old girl was raped in a horror broad daylight attack on Sunday in Southampton.



The alleged rape is thought to have taken place in an area of trees near a roundabout in Swaythling.

Officers launched a probe and have since arrested a man on suspicion of rape, and he remains in police custody.



The force said they are supporting the girl and her family, and they urge anyone with information that could help their probe to come forward.

A spokesperson for Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary said: “Detectives investigating a report of rape in Swaythling have arrested a 34-year-old man in connection with the incident.

“We received a report at 3.09pm on Sunday 23 August that a 14-year-old girl had been raped by a male unknown to her in an area of trees off the Wide Lane roundabout, near Mansbridge Road.

“Officers launched an investigation and are supporting the girl and her family as our enquiries continue.

“As part of our investigation, officers have today (25 August) arrested a 34-year-old man from Southampton on suspicion of rape.

“He remains in custody at this time.



“As the investigation progresses, officers are still keen to hear from any witnesses who may have key information.”

News.title: Mum and daughter, 4, killed as they walked to nursery by ‘two drivers racing at 90mph’
News.content:
SCHOOL RUN HORROR Mum and daughter, 4, killed as they walked to nursery by ‘two drivers racing at 90mph’

A MUM and daughter were killed as they walked to nursery by two drivers racing at at 90mph, a court heard.

Justyna Hulboj, 27, and four-year-old Lena Czepczor were on the pavement in Leeds when they were struck by an Audi TT.



The driver, Hardeep Bachu, has pleaded guilty to causing their deaths by dangerous driving.

Jasskamal Riyat, 37, is currently on trial at Leeds Crown Court after denying the same offences.



Jurors heard he was allegedly racing Bachu in a BMW 1 series before the horror crash in June 2023.

Prosecutor Carmel Pearson said the men, who were not known to each other, had been “egging each other on” during the morning rush hour.



Their driving was described as “competitive” and “aggressive” – with Riyat pulling up alongside Bachu at a set of traffic lights.

Witnesses reported seeing the pair weaving between other cars as the pair reached high speeds on the 40mph road.

Although Riyat’s speed was not recorded, jurors heard he was “right behind” Bachu when he was measured travelling at 89mph 60 metres away from the point of collision.

He was also allegedly holding his phone and recording Bachu as he pulled away from traffic lights, saying: “Watch this guy let it off.”



Footage also showed him and Bachu communicating through their windows as they waited at traffic lights appearing to congratulate each other on the power of their cars, it was said.

Justyna and Lena had been walking along Scott Hall Road at around 8.30am on their way to nursery.

The white Audi TT then hit a kerb and lost control – mounting the pavement and hitting the mum and daughter.



Riyat continued to film the crashed car as he passed by but left the scene and went to work, jurors were told.

Ms Pearson said: “Just because he [Riyat] did not crash, this does not mean he escapes responsibility for these deaths.

“He was also driving dangerously on that road. It’s the prosecution’s case that they both drove dangerously at speeds that outstripped other road users, weaving in and out of traffic close to each other and other cars.

“Neither driver showed regard to other road users and those more vulnerable – pedestrians.

“They were racing and competitive.”

She continued: “This was not just an unspeakable tragedy, but an entirely foreseeable event.”

The trial continues.

News.title: The ‘ghost’ plate crime wave linked to A66 crash turning roads into ‘Wild West’ – as gangs exploit gaping £40 loophole
News.content:
MOST drivers wouldn’t spare a second thought for their car number plate.

So it will surprise many to learn that illegal plates have been blamed for fuelling a “Wild West” of law-breaking on Britain’s roads – ranging from antisocial behaviour up to the highest levels of organised crime.



Two types of banned plates – “ghost” and “cloned” – have enabled toll dodgers to thwart congestion charges and have even been linked to murder.

Now, illegal plates are said to be involved in the horrific head-on crash deaths of two police officers in the early hours of Saturday morning.

Police watchdog the Independent Office for Police Conduct has confirmed cloned plates are believed to have been used on the Volkswagen Passat being driven by joyriders on the A66 in Middlesbrough.



That car struck and killed “devoted father” PC Matthew Blades, 37, and “hero” PC Tom Clough, 38, who were travelling in the opposite direction.

The occupants of the Passat, Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Theo Rae, 17, Cole Robert Worthy, 17, Jacob Matusiak, 23, and Makai Saddington, 18, all also died.

Cloned plates are fakes that use the real reg numbers of other cars owned by unwitting drivers.



Meanwhile, illegal ghost plates are manipulated or specially coated with reflected sprays, films, modified fonts or non-standard spacing.

They are difficult to detect as they often go unnoticed to the untrained eye and are not picked up by Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras.

These cameras, which automatically read vehicle registration marks, help police track stolen or uninsured vehicles and monitor criminal activity.

The horrific A66 smash is not the only recent tragedy involving cloned or ghost plates.

Kyron Lee, 21, was hacked to death by the Chalvey Boyz machete gang in his hometown of Slough, Berks, in October 2022.



He had been knocked off his bike by the attackers in a stolen car with cloned plates.

That slowed down Thames Valley Police in its investigation – although they eventually managed to trace his killers.

According to the DVLA, there were 11,394 reports of cloned plates between January and December 2025, and a bill is currently going through Parliament to crack down on illegal plates.



Estimates from 2023 reveal that in London alone there was a 64 per cent increase in fines being cancelled after many had been sent to innocent car owners whose plates had been cloned.

And it emerged last year that official suppliers of vehicle number plates in the UK are willing to sell illegal cloned versions.

More than 130 of these suppliers could be willing to provide the banned plates, it has been claimed.

And anyone can become a DVLA-registered number plate scheme (RNPS) member for as little as a £40 payment – leaving the system wide open to abuse, critics say.

The Vehicle Identification Group, a group of academics advising the government on the issue, said in a letter last year: “There is no vetting, no trading history requirement and no monitoring of members’ practices.



“We found 10 who were prepared to make cloned plates mapped around West Bromwich alone.

“To date we have identified over 135 DVLA registered RNPS members nationally who were prepared to make cloned plates and there will undoubtedly be more.”

One West Midlands crook was found to have allegedly supplied more than 7,000 illegal number plates to the criminal underworld.



The group, based at Cranfield University in Beds, added in the letter: “The UK’s ANPR system quietly enables mission critical activities across government departments, from the safe transport of nuclear materials to the enforcement of customs tariffs and vehicle excise duty; tackling fraudulent benefit claims and rogue traders; from ensuring roadworthiness, driver safety and standards in food delivery, schools and wider passenger and goods transport management to the support of health emergencies and pandemics, major incidents, civil contingencies, criminal intelligence and national security.

“It is no exaggeration to say that ANPR has become part of the country’s critical national infrastructure – and that system is entirely dependent on vehicle registration plates.

“While members of our group have publicly highlighted the absurdity of relying on a piece of plastic displayed on the exterior of a vehicle in an AI-ambitious digital economy, nevertheless, number plates are all we currently have, so we should take much more care with them.”



It went on to say that the response of the bodies responsible for number plate recognition was “lamentable”.

Labour MP Sarah Coombes, who represents West Bromwich in the West Midlands, took the fight to Parliament to get the punishment for having an illegal plate increased from a £100 fine to a £1,000 fine and six penalty points.

Last year she said: “Everything from low-level antisocial behaviour to organised crime is being fuelled by these number plates; using a ghost plate is not the victimless crime it’s made out to be.”

Meanwhile, Surrey Heath Liberal Democrat MP Dr Al Pinkerton, who is pushing for a Parliamentary bill related to illegal number plate cloning, asked in March this year then-Secretary of State for Transport Lilian Greenwood how she planned to address illegal plates links to organised crime.

Ms Greenwood said: “The Department and the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA) are considering options to ensure a more robust and auditable Register of Number Plate Supplier (RNPS) process, which would enable more stringent checks on suppliers.



“This includes consideration of the relevant legislation, fees, structure, resources and funding to help ensure sufficient auditing capability.

“The DVLA is also working with the National Police Chiefs’ Council, the Home Office and other government departments to improve the identification and enforcement of number plate crime.

“This includes options for making number plates more secure.

“The Department and the DVLA acknowledge the impact illegal number plates have on law enforcement and the effectiveness of automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) systems.

“The Home Office is responsible for the national ANPR service and issues guidance on its use as part of the national ANPR standards for policing and law enforcement.



“Therefore, the Department for Transport has not made an assessment of the impacts on ANPR operations.”

At the time of going to press, Ms Coombes had not responded to The Sun’s request for a comment.

But she previously said: “It’s clear to MPs of all parties that the DVLA is presiding over a failing system that has enabled widespread criminality and led to the absurd situation that we have thousands of number plate suppliers operating out of garages, backrooms and sheds.

“Cloned and ghost number plates are being used in everything from racing to drug-dealing to murder. The DVLA must take control of this number plate wild west. We as MPs cannot stand by and watch as the situation gets worse, putting ordinary drivers and members of the public in danger.”

A Department for Transport spokeswoman told The Sun: “Our thoughts are with all those affected by this tragic incident, especially the friends and family of PC Matthew Blades and PC Tom Clough. This is a live investigation and it’s important not to speculate on the circumstances. More generally, our Road Safety Strategy – the first in more than a decade – is taking direct action to crack down on illegal plates that help criminals evade detection.”



Cleveland Police have also been contacted for a comment.

News.title: Fury as TikTok ‘promoting joyriding yobs being chased by cops as “thrilling & exciting”‘… after wrong-way crash killed 7
News.content:
TIKTOK is allegedly promoting joyriding and police chase videos as “thrilling and exciting” after a wrong-way crash killed seven people.

The fatal collision on the A66 in Middlesbrough in the early hours of Saturday morning claimed the lives of PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38.



Five young men in a Volkswagen Passat also died in the devastating collision when the vehicle they were in ploughed into a patrol car.

They have since been identified as Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Theo Rae, 17, Cole Robert Worthy, 17, Jacob Matusiak, 23, and Makai Saddington, 18.



TikTok footage has since emerged showing Jacob Matusiak, who died in the fatal collision on Saturday, driving dangerously in the months leading up to the tragedy.

Saddington had also shared clips to social media showing him driving dangerously.

It has now emerged that social media giant TikTok is promoting similar videos as “exciting.”

AI generated summaries of footage of police chases and dangerous driving described the scenes as “thrilling”, the Telegraph reports.



This is despite the videos breaching the social media platforms rules on banned content.

TikTok has said its policies strictly prohibit content that could cause significant physical harm, including dangerous driving, and that it actively removes any videos and accounts that break its rules.

However, joyriding content is still found on the social media platform with the Prime Minister branding the sharing of dangerous driving videos was “truly reprehensible.”

The Telegraph reports one TikTok video, showing a motorist avoiding a police car with blue lights flashing, was promoted with an AI summary reading: “Watch the thrilling police chase in Bradford on the M606.”

It was later described by generative AI as an “exciting police chase video” under a keywords section.



Similar dangerous driving footage can be found on Youtube, Instagram and Snapchat with the platforms removing the content when they become aware of it.

The Sun found a slew of disturbing videos on TikTok showing drivers clocking speeds of up to 148mph, driving on the wrong side of the motorway and recklessly weaving across lanes.

Videos depicting incredibly hazardous driving were still being uploaded on to the site yesterday morning, with one user posting a video of a car’s speedometer clocking 125mph.



Some of the dangerous content has been available to watch on TikTok for almost two months, viewed by hundreds of thousands of people, and still has not been taken down.

Users can receive payments ranging from a few pounds to hundreds if their views and follower counts are high enough.

Yesterday, Cleveland Police crime commissioner Matt Storey branded dangerous driving trends “absolutely idiotic” when asked about one of the five young men involved in the wrong-way collision on Saturday.

Hearing reports that one of the young men involved in the fatal wrong-way collision on Saturday had been filming such content, he told BBC Radio 4: “Yeah, there has been speculation around that.

“Without being able to say whether that was anything like involved in this case, it’s absolutely idiotic for anybody to be doing anything other than being completely 100% focused on the road when they’re behind the wheel of a vehicle.”



After the deadly smash on the A66 on Saturday, the government ordered social media platforms to remove content showing dangerous driving.

Speaking on BBC Radio 5 Live Defence Minister Luke Pollard called on social media platforms to act to remove posts showing dangerous driving.

He told the station: “We’ve communicated to those social media platforms that have been hosting content that celebrates this type of dangerous behaviour on our roads to take down that content.

“I think we all need to give the police time, but there’s also things we can be doing in the meantime to make sure that the internet is a safer place for everyone, that doesn’t celebrate and load views and therefore financial incentives on people to generate such awful content.”

Twelve people were yesterday arrested in connection with the horror A66 collision.



A fundraiser launched for the families of the two police officers killed in the horror A66 crash has now raised more than £800,000. PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38, lost their lives alongside five “joyriders” who smashed their Volkswagen Passat into a cop car while driving in the wrong direction. A fundraiser, launched by Cleveland Police, said the two police officers “paid the ultimate sacrifice in the line of duty.” It read: “PC Matt Blades and PC Tom Clough were both dedicated and committed Police Officers who left their families and went to work to serve their community and protect the public. “They did not return home to their families. They leave behind heartbroken loved ones who will struggle to come to terms with the loss of their loved one. The force added they are “supporting and will continue to support” their families at this “unfathomable moment”. Launched on Sunday, the appeal has now raised more than £800,000 from over 27,000 donations. The funds will be split between both officers’ families “to assist them in any way as they try to navigate this traumatic time.” The fundraiser can be found HERE

Some of the 12 are suspected of “participating in the activities of an organised crime group.”

It has also since emerged that four of the five joyriders killed in the wrong-way smash had previous convictions.

Cleveland Police confirmed yesterday that Worthy, Matusiak, Saddington and Rae all had previous police convictions.

All four had appeared in court charged with a variety of offences.

Saddington pleaded guilty to possession of a Class C drug and a knife in May 2025 and months later admitted three offences of assaulting a police officer.



Meanwhile, Worthy admitted using threatening and abusive language to cause harassment, alarm and distress in October 2024.

He also pleaded guilty to common assault of a police officer in April last year and failing to surrender to custody a month later.

In March, Matusiak admitted using a vehicle without insurance and driving without a licence.

Rae was convicted of assaulting a police officer, shoplifting, stealing cars, theft, drug possession and breaching a youth rehabilitation order.

Cops have also confirmed yesterday that nine men and three women aged between 19 and 61, were arrested on suspicion of several offences.



The alleged offences include possession of a firearm and participating in the activities of an organised crime group.

Cops are continuing to investigate the moments leading up to the fatal smash on Saturday.

Police initially received several reports of two vehicles being driven dangerously.



The first vehicle, which is believed to be a Volvo XC60, was witnessed to be ramming properties in the Middlesbrough area.

The second vehicle, a Volkswagen Passat, is believed to have been associated with the activities of the Volvo XC60.

The Volvo XC60 involved in the initial reports has been traced and recovered in Middlesbrough as part of the criminal investigation.

Cleveland Police believes the Passat was being driven with cloned number plates and had been linked to several suspicious incidents.

And just moments before the horrifying fatal smash, officers had been chasing the car in a highspeed pursuit for seven minutes through residential streets.



Cops called off the pursuit when the Passat went on to the A66 because it had begun travelling the wrong way down the road.

But just ten seconds later, the car slammed into a different marked police vehicle travelling correctly on the A66.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Cleveland police have also said there is no evidence to indicate that filming of the activities that took place on Friday night and Saturday morning has taken place for the purposes of TikTok.

The Sun has contacted TikTok for comment.

News.title: Man dies in crash after police pursuit
News.content:
A man has died and two women have been injured in a crash that followed a police pursuit near Stratford-upon-Avon.

Officers tried to stop a black Audi on Birmingham Road shortly before 17:30 BST on Monday but the driver failed to pull over, Warwickshire Police said.

A pursuit began and 15 minutes later the Audi crashed into a white Ford Puma, the force said, with the Audi's male driver confirmed dead at the scene by paramedics.

The driver of the Ford, a woman, was seriously injured and remains in hospital in critical condition, while injuries to a second woman -her passanger - were serious but not believed to be life-threatening. An investigation by the police watchdog is under way.

Officers said after failing to stop, the Audi made off in the direction of the A46 before travelling back towards Stratford on the A439 Warwick Road where the crash occured.

A number of other cars were damaged during the pursuit, police said.

A spokesperson for West Midlands Ambulance Service said paramedics found four patients at the scene.

They treated a man who was in a critical condition, giving him advanced life support.

"Despite their best efforts, it became clear that nothing more could be done to save him and he was confirmed deceased by ambulance staff at the scene," the spokesperson said.

The woman who was driving the second car suffered life-threatening injuries, the ambulance service confirmed, and was taken to hospital.

A female passenger was seriously hurt and was also taken to hospital, along with another patient whose injuries were not believed to be serious.

News.title: Yellow weather warnings issued as thunderstorms and flooding forecast
News.content:
Yellow weather warnings have been issued by the Met Office as heavy rain and thunderstorms are forecast to break out over parts of the UK later this week.

The warnings span Wednesday and Thursday and include parts of east Wales, the Midlands, northern England, East Anglia and southern England - including London.

It is likely to be the one of the most widespread outbreaks of heavy rain across southern and central parts of the UK this summer.

While good news for regions plagued by drought, significant accumulations could lead to flash flooding where the ground is too dry and hard to absorb the downpours. Lightning, large hail and gusty winds are also possible.

News.title: Young care leavers dying early a 'national tragedy'
News.content:
Young adults who have left care have a death rate around four times higher than the general population, a new review, external shows.

Often left alone "with no safety net," the report says the consequences can be catastrophic.

On turning 18, people leaving care in England often lose "significant levers of support", the Government-commissioned report concluded, as it warned the so-called "care cliff" must be addressed.

Speaking to BBC Radio 4 Today, report co-author and broadcaster Ashley John-Baptiste, who grew up in care, called the deaths a national tragedy.

There were 112 deaths of care leavers aged 18 to 24 notified in 2025, which the review said equalled about 130 deaths per 100,000 care leavers.

John-Baptiste recalled his own experience of turning 18 and moving out of the last of four foster homes he'd lived in.

"I was made to live alone and work out how to be an adult," he said.

Unable to afford a bed frame, he says he slept on a mattress on the floor of his council flat and felt a deep sense of abandonment and isolation.

News.title: Moment tornado tears through southern France
News.content:
A destructive tornado has torn through villages in southern France, injuring more than 40 people.

An eyewitness from the village of Verzeille recorded the tornado forming beneath a thunderstorm. Winds of more than 100km/h (62mph) ripped the roofs off homes in Pomas.

Local authorities say about 2,800 households were still without electricity on Monday evening, while several roads were blocked.

More on this story.

News.title: Boy, 3, injured in crocodile attack returns home
News.content:
A three-year-old boy who was seriously injured in a crocodile enclosure has been discharged from hospital and is settling back in at home, his family has said.

The child returned home "a few weeks ago" and is "happy to be home, playing with his toys, sleeping in his own bed and being a big brother", his parents said in an update posted online.

The boy was visiting Johnsons of Old Hurst near Huntingdon, Cambridgeshire, with his family on 18 June when he was attacked by at least one of the animals.

In an update shared on a fundraising page on Monday, the boy's family said it was "nice to have us all back together in the comfort of our own home".

Cambridgeshire Police arrested and bailed a 30-year-old man from Norfolk on suspicion of attempted murder after the incident.

News.title: Russian stadium says it won't host Kanye West gigs
News.content:
The Russian stadium that was scheduled to host two shows by Ye, the rapper also known as Kanye West, has said the events will no longer take place.

In a social media post, external, St Petersburg's Gazprom Arena said no rental agreement had been signed with the concert promoters. "Accordingly, the concert cannot take place on our site."

West would have been the first major Western performer to play Russia since it invaded Ukraine in 2022. The rapper is trying to rehabilitate his image after years of antisemitic remarks, for which he recently apologised.

Gazprom Arena acknowledged it had received complaints about West's planned appearance and stressed that it "was not and is not" responsible for his booking.

The stadium said in its statement that the sold-out concerts, scheduled for 10 and 11 October, had been organised by the Moscow-based Say Agency.

Posting on its Telegram channel, Say Agency said the stadium's announcement had come as a surprise.

"We learned about [it] at the same time as you did, through the media," the agency wrote. "As of now, the Ye concert has not been canceled," it added in a follow-up message.

"We are trying to contact the venue to find out the reason for the post and resolve the issue. We will keep you updated."

The BBC has contacted West's publicist for a comment on the uncertainty over his Russian shows.

In its statement, Say Agency said it announced the concerts earlier this month based "on an official letter that was approved by" Gazprom Arena.

The stadium subsequently sent a rental agreement, Say Agency claimed, and the agency acknowledged the contract had not yet been signed but said the deadline to do so did not expire until later this week.

Last week, Gazprom Arena had posted enthusiastically about the concerts on social media, calling Ye "the most influential musical artist of our time".

Fans reacted to its latest announcement with disappointment.

"This was the shortest concert of my life," responded one, under Say Agency's Telegram post. "It's a shame that the government is putting obstacles in your way," added another.

There is no indication that authorities intervened in the shows, but there has been opposition to West's booking from some Russian politicians.

Vitaly Milonov, a notorious conservative lawmaker, suggested the star should perform traditional Russian songs instead of his planned setlist, reflecting the anti-Western views of many nationalists.

"Maybe after this he'll stop his disgusting antics and become a normal person," Milonov added in a video statement.

News.title: Beyond China's humanoid robots, a quieter machine revolution is unfolding
News.content:
"I take a nap and the world changes," says Chen Tianyu.

His world certainly does. The 28-year-old keeps up with the latest technology by spending his spare time in factories that are switching to automation. That way he knows what to prioritise when teaching his class about artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics.

In front of him, around 30 college students are studying code. One of them is typing furiously as his eyes dart from the screen to the robot: "The idea is it will grab that cylindrical piece and move it over there."

A line of industrial robots are waiting to be programmed, and in another part of the classroom, students are trying to develop robotic medical instruments. As he guides them, Chen declares: "If you are not needed by the world of AI and robotics, then you'll definitely be among those eliminated".

For the people in this room, this is a step - or rather a leap - towards a future that China is meticulously building: Xi Jinping's $20bn (Â£14.7bn) plan to put his country at the forefront of innovation and in direct competition with the US.

The evidence is all around them. They are in the Hangzhou Technician Institute, one of several huge, purpose-built vocational schools that want to churn out the next generation of tech-savvy engineers. The campus sits on the outskirts of Hangzhou, a former imperial capital whose futuristic skyline is just the first hint of its role as a global tech hub.

Across the country, there are more than two million robots working in China's factories - which is more than anywhere else - and they are continuing to scale up at extraordinary speed.

News.title: OnlyFans owner was paid over $700m before his death
News.content:
The late owner of streaming platform OnlyFans was paid more than $700m (Â£513m) in dividends before his death from cancer earlier this year.

Fenix International Ltd, the British company that owns OnlyFans, made $714m in profit before tax last year, it said in its annual report. This is an increase of 5% from 2024.

The site hosts a range of subscription-based content from cooking to fitness videos, but it is best known for pornography and is credited with transforming online adult content by encouraging personal connection between sex workers and subscribers.

Its owner Leonid Radvinsky, who died earlier this year aged 43, bought the site from its British founders in 2018.

OnlyFans employs just 47 people. Companies with such high profits rarely have such small staff - for example, British retail giant Marks and Spencer, which employs over 65,000 people, made Â£671m in profit last year.

Fenix International's company results show that it paid dividends of $535m for the year ending 30 November 2025, with further dividends payments totalling $174m between then and 26 March 2026.

Radvinsky, who was born in Ukraine and raised in the US, died on 23 March. The company is now owned by his widow, Yekaterina 'Katie' Chudnovsky.

OnlyFans surged in popularity during the Covid-19 pandemic, landing Radvinsky on Forbes' annual list of billionaires just three years later.

The site is known for the way it encourages creators and fans to connect through livestreams, personalised messages, and direct requests for custom-made photos and videos.

In return for hosting the material, OnlyFans takes a 20% share of all payments.

The site had 132 million paying subscribers and 2.5 million active creators in 2025.

The boom in size and popularity under Radvinsky's ownership also brought scrutiny from lawmakers and regulators over its adult content â a recent BBC Three documentary uncovered allegations of exploitation, coercion and violence committed against OnlyFans creators.

In 2024, British regulators launched an investigation into whether children were accessing porn, an issue that the company at the time blamed on a technical issue.

Ofcom ultimately dropped that probe, but it fined the firm about Â£1m, external for failing to respond accurately to its requests for information about the measures it had in place to check the age of its users, who in theory must be 18 or over.

Creators have also debunked the narrative that making explicit videos on the site is a get-rich-quick scheme.

Keily Blair, the chief executive of OnlyFans, said on Tuesday that the company had paid over $30bn to creators since launching a decade ago.

"OnlyFans provides real opportunities to real people by creating a safe, regulated space where people can monetise their content with a global fan base," she said.

"As a UK-based business we have also made a significant contribution to the UK economy, paying over Â£600 million in corporate taxes from 2016 to date."

News.title: More than 70,000 social and affordable homes to be built across England over 10 years
News.content:
Ministers have announced where more than 70,000 social and affordable homes will be built in England over the next 10 years as part of an initial allocation of almost Â£10bn, in a bid to address the housing crisis.

Funding has been granted to Greater Manchester, the West Midlands, West Yorkshire, South Yorkshire, North East England, and Liverpool. An additional Â£6bn was previously announced for London.

It is the first part of a wider plan to build 300,000 social and affordable homes across the nation, under the government's Â£39bn social housebuilding programme.

Earlier this year, before he became prime minister, Andy Burnham had called for the entire 10-year Â£39bn affordable housing budget for England to be spent on homes for social rent - which means the cost of the unit is about half that of market rents, and there are strict criteria for who can apply for it.

"I would actually devote all of it to social housing," Burnham told The Social Housing Podcast in May.

But of the new homes announced on Monday, 60% would be for social rent.

Housing minister Matthew Pennycook told BBC Breakfast he did not accept Burnham had failed to meet his previous commitment, saying the government had taken a "pragmatic approach" and wants to "get money out the door".

He said the next tranche of funding would be more focused on council houses - which are usually also classed as homes for social rent.

It is understood ministers decided against giving councils more of the funding announced in the first tranche because they did not believe councils would be in a position to build the required number of social homes.

News.title: Burnham refuses to rule out tax rises in autumn Budget
News.content:
Andy Burnham has refused to rule out tax rises in the upcoming autumn Budget, saying he "won't be unrealistic" about the "challenging" state of public finances.

The prime minister said he would take a "careful approach" to the economy, and defended his previously announced cost of living pledges as funded spending commitments.

Burnham became prime minister in July promising to give people breathing space and help with the cost of living, but questions remain over how major policies such as social care reforms will be funded.

Experts have previously warned that he and Chancellor John Healey will have little financial room to manoeuvre in their first Budget on 28 October.

Speaking during his first visit to Ukraine, Burnham said the policies announced so far including capping bus fares at Â£2 and cutting VAT on household electricity bills were "the first steps that I've felt able to make", and were doable because he was able to reprioritise funding from elsewhere.

"I took the decision early on that digital ID wasn't the top priority for now. And so we've reprioritised funding to other priorities," he said in an interview with ITV.

Asked if the public needed to accept some of the new policies would have to be paid for in tax rises, Burnham said they wouldn't necessarily have to accept that.

Pushed on whether he would need to raise taxes to cover spending gaps, he said: "I will always take a careful approach to things. I ran Greater Manchester for 10 years and we ran a very tight ship with rock solid finances.

"Nothing will change as I come into this role as prime minister. I won't take risks with people's jobs or their livelihoods or their family finances.

"I will try to help them in whatever way I can, I have already done some things that will help them."

Burnham previously told the BBC he accepts his earlier announcements aimed at tackling the cost of living are not enough on their own and hinted at further support.

Speaking during his first official overseas visit on Monday, he said while he would do what he could, "I won't be unrealistic and people really need to understand that.

"We are in a challenging position, whatever I do will be carefully thought through, it will be funded and there will be more to come as we go into the autumn."

Last week official figures showed the the government borrowed more than expected in July, despite a record month for income tax receipts.

Inflation also reached a four-month high of 2.9% in July and is expected to rise further due to the ongoing impact of the Iran war, which has hit energy prices and fuel costs.

Experts have warned Burnham and Healey that they need to either raise taxes or cut spending elsewhere as pressure on the public finances has left no room for extra borrowing.

Both the prime minister and chancellor have vowed to stick to the fiscal rules set by former chancellor Rachel Reeves.

The rules are designed to ensure day-to-day spending is funded through tax revenue by the end of the Parliament, and to reduce debt as a proportion of GDP.

Rain Newton-Smith, chief executive of the Confederation of British Industry, said business owners wanted to create opportunities for young people but "the cost of employing people has gone up so much".

"The business leaders I speak to say that the cost of doing business has gone up so much that it's holding them back from creating opportunities," she told the Today programme.

She said targeted support for businesses would create "more growth and more opportunities that saves money for the government and ultimately leads to higher tax receipts".

News.title: Legendary rugby league winger Boston dies aged 92
News.content:
Rugby league legend Sir Billy Boston has died aged 92.

Last year, he became the first player in rugby league's 130-year history to receive a knighthood.

Born in Cardiff in 1934, Boston grew up playing union but - overlooked by his home club - came to the attention of rugby league scouts while on national service in the north of England, signing for Wigan in 1953 as a 19-year-old.

Despite having played just a handful of games in league, the young winger's talent was quickly evident and Boston was picked for the 1954 Great Britain side that went to Australia and New Zealand - becoming the first black British player to tour down under.

He reached the 100-try milestone in just 68 matches after his switch from union.

Boston's scoring ratio is extraordinary, claiming 478 tries in 488 games for Wigan and helping them win three Challenge Cups and the Championship.

News.title: 'Historic' first as two osprey chicks born on Anglesey, experts say
News.content:
Two osprey chicks have been born on Anglesey for the first time, according to conservationists.

The baby birds were hatched earlier this summer, and have since successfully left the nest, with hopes they may return.

Friends of the Ospreys, the conservation group who monitor the private site, said they were "over the moon" at the news, and hoped it pointed to a bright future for the species on the island.

The adult ospreys responsible for these chicks are one of about 300 breeding pairs in the UK, with about 20 in Wales.

News.title: New 10p coin enters circulation - will you spot one?
News.content:
Something new might appear in your change when you pay in cash from now on: a 10p coin featuring the portrait of King Charles and the world's largest grouse.

Sufficient demand for the coins mean newly-minted 10p pieces are entering circulation for the first time for about four years, this time with a new design.

The Royal Mint says shoppers and collectors should discover the coins, which were minted and dated in 2023 and 2026, across the country.

The reverse side of the coin depicts an image of the capercaillie which is found in a small part of Scotland and threatened with extinction.

The redesigned suite of coins to celebrate the King's love of the natural world were unveiled in October 2023 by The Royal Mint.

The tails side of every newly-minted coin from the 1p to the Â£2 now features the country's flora and fauna - from bees to an oak tree leaf.

Coins in circulation in the UK carrying the portrait of King Charles have so far been limited to the 5p, 50p and Â£1.

Old coins with the image of the late Queen Elizabeth II can still be used, so the new coins are only struck in response to demand.

That is why, with 1.4 billion 10p coins in circulation, there has been no need for the new 10p to be released until now by The Royal Mint.

Now. 600,000 of these coins, dated 2023, and 6.5 million dated 2026 have been released to banks and post offices nationwide.

However, King Charles III coins still only represent about 1% of the 24.1 billion coins in circulation across the UK, making any new ones highly sought after by seasoned numismatists and new coin collectors.

News.title: Organised crime arrests in A66 crash investigation
News.content:
Twelve people have been arrested as part of the investigation into the A66 crash that killed seven people, including two police officers.

Nine men and three women, aged between 19 and 61, have been arrested across Teesside on suspicion of a range of offences including possession of a firearm and being part of an organised crime group. One has since been charged.

In the early hours of Saturday, a Volkswagen Passat that had been pursued by police travelled the wrong way down the A66 near Middlesbrough and crashed into an oncoming police car - two PCs and all five Passat occupants died.

Cleveland Police said it was investigating "serious criminal activity that resulted in this fatal incident".

PC Tom Clough, 38, and PC Matthew Blades, 37, died in the crash, as did Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Jacob Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18, Theo Rae, 17, and 17-year-old Cole Robert Worthy.

Earlier, Cleveland Police released more details of its investigation into the lead-up to the crash and information about the 12 people it had arrested.

The force said:

It received several reports of two vehicles "being driven dangerously" on Saturday morning

The first vehicle, believed to be a Volvo XC60, was seen "ramming properties" in the Middlesbrough area

The second vehicle, a Passat, is believed to have been associated with this activity

Both vehicles were operating with cloned number plates but were picked up by automated number plate recognition technology

The Volvo has been recovered in Middlesbrough

Four of the five people in the Passat had previous convictions

Assistant Chief Constable Wayne Fox said the investigation had been "fast moving and complex".

He said: "The events of that tragic night will have a lasting and profound impact on the Cleveland area and the communities we seek to protect.

"We have a duty to respond to, and thoroughly investigate, the serious criminal activity that resulted in this fatal incident and to bring all those responsible to justice."

News.title: UK drone factories may face attacks from 'unknown sources', says former Russian minister
News.content:
A Russian former deputy foreign minister has said there might be a "semi-military" response against UK drone factories by "unknown sources" over the sharing of blueprints for British-made cruise missile components.

Andrei Fedorov's comments on BBC Newsnight come as UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced plans to travel to the US next month with European leaders to lobby President Donald Trump on Ukraine's defence needs.

Burnham's trip, should it go ahead, would be his first to the US since becoming prime minister.

"Leaving today, I'm quite clear what I need to do in the next few weeks," he said following his visit to Ukraine on Monday, during which he promised to continue pressuring Russia.

The UK has agreed to hand over blueprints for British-made components for the Scalp missile, a French version of the UK's Storm Shadow cruise missile. The blueprints will allow Ukraine to produce the long-range weapon domestically.

Fedorov, a pro-Kremlin commentator who frequently appears on Russian television, said Putin was facing "serious" pressure "to undertake certain measures against UK". Asked on BBC Newsnight where the pressure was coming from, Fedorov responded "public opinion polls, it's coming from journalists, from mass media".

Asked what a "semi-military" response might look like, Fedorov said: "It could take the form of something might happen with enterprises, with factories which are producing drones for Ukraine.

"They could be attacked not by Russia, but by from unknown sources."

The comments are in line with those made by Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov on Monday, when he criticised the UK's decision to share the missile blueprints. Peskov said it prevented "even the slightest progress" towards achieving peace.

He told reporters on Monday that the Russian military was already gathering data to locate any missile production sites to destroy them.

"Britain is involved in this war on the side of the Kyiv regime. Britain methodically and regularly adds fuel to the fire," he added.

In response, Burnham said: "Who started the fire? That's the question, isn't it?"

Burnham's visit to Ukraine was his first official international trip. He met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Kyiv and chaired his first meeting of the "coalition of the willing", set up by the UK and France under his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer.

Burnham has been reaffirming the UK's support for Ukraine in the wake of escalating Russian strikes in recent weeks - including one last week on a shopping centre that killed at least 16 people.

Ukraine has been relying on American supplies of the Patriot interceptor missiles, which are used to combat Russia's ballistic missiles, but stockpiles are running low due to the war in Iran, leaving Ukraine vulnerable to Russian attacks.

Zelensky has said he is hoping to secure 300 patriot missiles ahead of winter, when Russia is likely to increase its attacks on energy infrastructure, as it has done in past years.

In the interview with Bloomberg, Burnham said he felt "really confident" that the issue was "fixable". But he pointed out that it wasn't only the US who could supply Ukraine with Patriots.

"There are other players who could help in the mix who we have influence with," he said. "It's probably going to be a solution that involves a lot of layers and a lot of negotiation."

In July this year, three weeks after offering Ukraine the right to produce Patriots itself, Trump backtracked, saying: "We have not agreed to that. We're talking about it. But it's a hard thing to give away, that kind of technology."

"These weapons are incredible. We have to be very careful about letting somebody build them," Trump told a cabinet meeting.

In a joint statement after the meeting in Ukraine, Burnham and co-chairs French President Emmanuel Macron and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the group would aim to strength Kyiv's air defences "as a matter or urgent priority".

They also condemned Moscow's "systemic and escalating strikes against Ukraine's cities, critical infrastructure and civilians" and pledged to "constrain Russia's war chest through sanctions and actions against the shadow fleet".

In a statement ahead of the visit, Burnham said: "On Ukraine's 35th anniversary of independence, the Ukrainian people should be in no doubt: the UK is behind you today and for as long as it takes.

"I am proud of the contribution our country has made to Ukraine and I want the Ukrainian people to hear it directly from me that our support will not waver. After all, Ukraine's security is our security."

He said the friendship Ukraine shared with the UK would "long outlast Russia's illegal war", adding: "Russia should be in no doubt of our resolve. We will not back down until there is a just and lasting peace."

News.title: Letting agent accused of not returning deposits to more than 100 tenants
News.content:
Raman Kaur and her family rented a house through Morgan, Payne & Knightly (MPK) until September 2025 when they bought their own home.

They are still waiting for their Â£900 deposit to be returned and have discovered the money was not put in a registered deposit scheme.

"It's not right, he shouldn't be doing that with our money," she said. "That's our sweat, our hard work.

"It's very stressful having a young family and with the financial crisis that we're all going through.

"We've saved that money, we've budgeted and we've had to tell the kids they can't have things.

"I think he should be ashamed of what he's done. It's not his money, he didn't earn it."

Kaur says the family visited the West Bromwich branch of MPK to resolve the matter, but found it had closed, leaving them to try phoning Singh and his staff every day.

The home the family rented is owned by an individual who did not want to be named in this article. We will refer to him as Vikram.

"I'm owed Â£700 and MPK are falsely saying they're registered in a deposit protection scheme, but they're not," he said.

"I've spent months trying to get hold of Tony Singh but the offices have shut down, and nobody answers the phone or emails.

"It feels like nobody can help us, so we contacted the BBC."

Our investigation has since found that individual sums that are owed range from Â£700 to Â£16,000.

Vikram reported his experience to Trading Standards.

Sandwell Council, which covers West Bromwich, said both Singh and MPK were no longer operating in the borough.

Singh and MPK continue, however, to operate elsewhere in the West Midlands, the BBC can confirm.

Andrew Tate’s lawyer has said the social media “influencer” rented supercars to appear wealthier than he is and generate more online engagement.

Legal representatives for the former kickboxer and his brother Tristan Tate have claimed the pair deliberately portray themselves as “uberwealthy” because their “business model depends on online attention”.

The submissions come after British police sought the brothers’ extradition from the US over an investigation into alleged sexual offences, which they deny.

The Tate brothers, who hold dual US and British citizenship, were arrested by US marshals in Miami in July after new charges were brought against them.

In a court filing, their lawyers said: “Andrew and Tristan are social media personalities.

“Their business model depends on online attention.

“The outrageousness of the posts by them and about them is the point.

“The more hyperbolic and outlandish the post, the more likely it will generate views and likes, which in turn generates income.

“In short, they are playing a role.”

open image in gallery A car at The Hustlers University’ site belonging to Andrew Tate and his brother in Bucharest on 14 January 2023 ( AFP/Getty )

The brothers’ legal representatives said images of luxury yachts, supercars and expensive watches shared by the brothers online should not be taken as evidence of their wealth.

Their submissions continued: “A promotional video filmed aboard a yacht is not evidence of title to the yacht.

“The ‘superyacht’ does not belong to the Tates.

“They received payment to promote the ship on social media.

“Further, the Tates are engaged in several businesses ‘teaching’ men how to earn money.

“It is in their interest to portray themselves on social media as uberwealthy.

“For example, the 2.1 million dollar Aston Martin and five million dollar and seven million dollar Bugattis featured in Tristan’s videos were rented.

“The valuation of Andrew’s watch collection is based on a third-party enthusiast publication.”

Separately, Andrew Tate is being sued in England by four women over allegations of sexual violence, with the former professional kickboxer’s lawyers previously telling the High Court there was a “total denial of wrongdoing”.

Three of the women bringing the civil case reported allegations of rape and sexual assault against Tate to Hertfordshire Constabulary in 2014 and 2015, with the case concluded in 2019.

The civil trial was adjourned in May after the force said it would reinvestigate the alleged offences.

After the brothers’ arrests on July 18, the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said it was bringing further charges against them.

Andrew Tate, 39, was charged with seven further counts of rape, three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation, three counts of assault occasioning actual bodily harm and 19 additional charges relating to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.

Tristan Tate, 38, was charged with one count of sexual assault, two counts of rape and three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation.

The CPS said the 38 additional charges, in addition to 21 existing charges, relate to alleged offences between July 2010 and August 2017.

The brothers are also facing legal proceedings in Romania and were due to be extradited to the UK after those proceedings concluded, after Bedfordshire Police secured European arrest warrants for the pair in 2024.

The pair have previously “unequivocally” denied wrongdoing, with Andrew Tate describing himself and his brother as “very innocent men”.

Lewis Hamilton has admitted that his sharp radio exchanges with Ferrari during the Dutch Grand Prix were "not the best version of him", following a tense afternoon at Zandvoort.

The 41-year-old came home in fourth place as Formula One returned from its summer break, eager to kickstart his pursuit of an eighth world championship.

However, his race was marked by frustration over Ferrari’s failure to move team-mate Charles Leclerc aside quickly enough, a delay Hamilton suggested prevented him from overtaking George Russell for the final podium spot.

Having shown stronger pace during the middle of the race, Ferrari asked Leclerc to pit, but the Monegasque driver questioned the instruction and stayed out for an extra lap.

"Great way of wasting time guys, good job," Hamilton sarcastically said.

After stating post-race that he had lost "several seconds" which proved costly at the finish, the seven-time world champion reflected on his "heat of the moment" remarks on Instagram on Monday evening.

"I’ve listened back to some of my radio and TV comments. In the heat of the moment frustration can come out, especially when you care as deeply as I do," he wrote.

"But that wasn’t the best version of me. I take responsibility for that, and I’ll be better.

"That passion comes from believing in this team, the people in it, and what we’re building together. The direction is clear. The belief is there. And the fight is absolutely still on.

"Thank you for sticking with us and with me. We’ll keep building, keep pushing and keep fighting."

Hamilton leaves Zandvoort level with Russell in second place in the championship standings, sitting 59 points behind leader Kimi Antonelli. He mounted a late chase against Russell, but his progress was hampered by a late virtual safety car.

open image in gallery Hamilton has vowed to learn from the incident ( PA Wire )

With his lone victory of the season coming in Barcelona in June, Hamilton maintains that he remains firmly in the title hunt after spending the summer break conditioning himself for the remainder of the year.

"A tough weekend, but we leave with valuable points for the team and signs that we’re moving in the right direction," he added.

"I’m incredibly proud of everyone back at the factory who continues to bring updates, find performance and push us forward.

"To the team at the track, thank you. The commitment and effort never go unnoticed."

Thunderstorm warnings have been issued across parts of the country as the Met Office warns of flooding and disruption.

Yellow warnings for storms will be in place across the West and East Midlands, as well as the North West, South East, South West and east of England, and parts of Wales.

The alerts will be in force in England and Wales from 3am until 10pm on Wednesday, and 6am until 10pm on Thursday.

The Met Office warned there is a “small risk of flooding and disruption from thunderstorms” with the potential for power cuts after a summer of record-breaking dry conditions.

open image in gallery A thunderstorm warning is in place across England and Wales ( Met Office )

A band of heavy showers and thunderstorms is expected to move northwards on Wednesday morning, the forecaster warned, adding an intense downpour of 20 to 30mm of rain could fall in less than an hour.

Some spots could see 40 to 50mm in two to three hours, leading to some surface water flooding, with the possibility of large hail and frequent lightning.

These showers and thunderstorms are expected to drift northwards and ease during the evening.

On Thursday, another band of thunderstorms and heavy rain is expected to move slowly across England and Wales. The Met Office said that 20 to 30mm of rainfall is expected to accumulate in three hours across the affected areas, and up to 50mm in 12 hours can be expected in places.

open image in gallery Thunderstorms will return on Thursday ( Met Office )

There is a small chance that some places may see more than 50mm in three hours and more than 75mm through 12 hours, especially over east-facing high ground. Lightning and hail of 1-2cm will also be hazardous, the forecaster warned.

The Met Office warned of a slight chance that power cuts could occur, impacting homes and businesses which could be flooded quickly. Buildings could face damage from floodwater, lightning strikes or hail. Flooding and lightning could cause delays and cancellations to train and bus services.

The risk of spray and sudden flooding could also lead to road closures and difficult driving conditions.

Met Office deputy chief forecaster Mark Sidaway attributed the unsettled weather to warmer and more humid air moving north across the UK.

open image in gallery Rain is expected across parts of the country on Wednesday ( Met Office )

“While many areas will see dry and increasingly warm conditions at the start of the week, attention is turning to the potential for heavy rain and thunderstorms from Wednesday onwards,” he said.

“As warmer and more humid air moves north across the UK, there is an increasing likelihood of some heavy rain developing. Some places could see 20 to 30mm of rain in just a few hours, while there is also the potential for higher totals where thunderstorms repeatedly affect the same locations.

“The detail of which areas will see the heaviest rainfall is still uncertain, so stay up to date with the forecast this week to keep updated on the increasing risk of impactful weather during the latter part of the week.”

By Thursday, a band of heavy and thundery rain is expected to move northwards through England and Wales slowly, which could lead to substantial rainfall totals.

open image in gallery People under an umbrella in the rain on Sunny Sands Beach in Folkestone last week ( Getty )

The incoming downpour comes as England and Wales are expected to record one of the driest summers on record. Almost three-quarters of England is designated as under drought, as is the entirety of Wales.

Scientists previously warned that a heavy downpour could cause more harm than good following the dry and hot summer, as it could lead to flash flooding in parts of the country.

The Environment Agency flood forecast for the next five days suggests that local flooding from surface water is “possible more widely on Wednesday”, which could bring a deluge to land, roads and some properties.

Health officials have issued an urgent appeal for blood donors to step forward following a "triple whammy" of surging demand, lower collection rates and the challenges posed by hot weather.

The NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT) division said increasing donor numbers will help ensure national blood reserves are in a stronger position to "withstand" routine summer "shocks" to the system.

It comes following various heatwaves in the UK - which directly affect eligibility, as even mildly warmer weather is capable of reducing a donor's iron levels.

NHSBT reported that donations can decrease by 10 per cent on ordinary warm days as a result.

Warm weather can also contribute to dehydration which will impact donors, while summer holidays, childcare responsibilities and deferrals for people returning from trips abroad continue to disrupt regular collection appointments.

open image in gallery The NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT) division has urged those able to donate to come forward ( AFP/Getty )

Meanwhile, some patients reliant on routine transfusions could require a higher volume of blood than usual due to warmer conditions. NHSBT said that it has seen higher demand from hospitals during the heatwaves in June and July.

Darren Bowen, assistant director for blood supply at NHSBT, said: “This summer has been a particularly challenging one for the blood service in England – with blood stocks hit by the triple whammy of hot weather, holidays and high demand from hospitals.

“With hot weather arriving earlier and lasting much longer than we have seen in recent years, it has resulted in lower collections along with increased demand from hospitals, with many patients reliant on regular transfusions for conditions like sickle cell needing more frequent treatment, or higher quantities of blood, than usual.

“We urge donors, especially those with B negative, O negative and the Ro subtype, as well as more donors of black heritage, to keep coming forward as we work to rebuild stocks.”

It comes as blood supply organisations across England, Canada and Australia have come together for the first time to launch an appeal for more blood donors across the three countries as a range of pressures have impacted blood supplies.

These include extreme weather and seasonal illness to changing donation patterns, NHSBT said.

The organisation has previously issued an urgent call for donors to fill 60,000 appointments over the summer period.

It has joined forces with Australian Red Cross Lifeblood and both Canadian Blood Services and Hema-Quebec in Canada to highlight the growing demand for blood because of ageing populations leading to more people living with conditions such as cancer and sickle cell that require regular blood transfusions for treatment.

Meanwhile, demand for medicines made from plasma to treat immune deficiencies, bleeding disorders and other conditions continues to rise, it said.

Across the three countries, blood supplies have dropped up to 30% in recent months, NHSBT added.

Gerry Gogarty, director of blood and plasma supply at NHS Blood and Transplant, said with millions globally depending on blood transfusions for surgeries, trauma, cancer treatment and chronic disease, disruption to regular donation is a challenge all three countries face.

“Blood collection systems are vulnerable to changing weather and climate, including heatwaves in summer and cold and flu outbreaks in winter, but regular donors are the foundation of a resilient supply,” Mr Gogarty said.

“By boosting the number of donors, particularly those with key blood types including O negative, B negative and the RO subtype needed to treat sickle cell, we can better withstand these shocks and ensure we are prepared for a future where events like this may happen more often.”

Mark Ronson has remembered the late Amy Winehouse and her music which "matter so deeply to so many people" as the 20th anniversary of her Back To Black album approaches.

The award-winning singer died in July 2011 at the age of 27.

Ronson, 50, began his working relationship with the star when producing several tracks for her hit 2006 record Back To Black, before she appeared on his 2007 version of ‘Valerie’.

The DJ produced a number of tracks on the album including ‘Rehab’, which picked up three Grammy Awards, ‘You Know I’m No Good’ and ‘Love Is a Losing Game’. He also holds a co-writing credit on the title track ‘Back To Black’.

To mark two decades since its release, the chart-topping album will be reissued this October in a range of special formats containing rare B-sides, unreleased demos and a recording from a live show in Amsterdam.

The formats will also feature previously unseen photographs from original album photographers Mischa Richter and Alex Lake, as well as new liner notes by producers and friends including Salaam Remi and Ronson.

open image in gallery Mark Ronson and Amy Winehouse ( Getty )

Ronson said: “It’s crazy that six songs made in a fit of furious musical infatuation would matter so deeply to so many people 20 years later.”

US record producer Remi, who has worked with artists including Alicia Keys, Doja Cat, Fergie, Nelly Furtado and Estelle, hailed Winehouse as a “one-of-a-kind soul”.

He said: “Amy was one of one.

“One-of-a-kind artist. One-of-a-kind spirit. One-of-a-kind soul.

“Experiencing that level of talent, passion, humour, honesty and love for what she created was a gift.”

The Grammy-winning musician first collaborated with Winehouse in 2003, producing key tracks from her debut album including ‘In My Bed ‘and ‘F*** Me Pumps’.

He worked with the music star on Back To Black, producing songs such as ‘Tears Dry on Their Own’ and ‘Me & Mr Jones’.

open image in gallery Mark Ronson began his working relationship with the star when producing several tracks for her hit 2006 record Back To Black , before she appeared on his 2007 version of ‘Valerie’.

Remi also released ‘Find My Love’ in 2019 – a collaborative posthumous single which featured rapper Nas and archival vocals from Winehouse.

Winehouse skyrocketed to global success after the release of her Back To Black record.

The singer, who was open about her struggles with drink and drug problems throughout her career, became one of the musicians associated with the so-called “27 club” after she died at that age.

Known for her signature beehive hair and heavy-winged eyeliner, the musician has remained an important figure in the industry since her death, with peers such as Adele and Lady Gaga among those who have acknowledged her lasting influence.

The upcoming special editions of Back To Black will be released on October 23, four days before its 20th anniversary.
