Sports.title: What makes Norris say “I don't have a car to fight for the championship”?
Sports.content:
The 2026 Formula 1 championship finds itself at a curious intersection where nobody is willing to entertain the idea that they have the best car.

Championship leader Kimi Antonelli said after finishing second to Lando Norris in the Dutch Grand Prix that Mercedes no longer has the best car – indeed, that it may only be the third best.

But Norris, now fourth in the standings with 159 points to Antonelli’s 242, was determined to play down talk of him staging a comeback in the final half of the season, despite winning two consecutive grands prix. "I don't have the car I need to fight for a championship," he said after his Dutch GP victory.

Many readers would be tempted to cite the so-called Mandy Rice-Davies principle – "Well they would say that, wouldn’t they?"

What’s clear, though, is that under the latest technical regulations there is still a difference in relative strengths between cars which complicates the competitive picture. In broad-brush terms the McLaren MCL40 thrives in fast corners, Ferrari’s SF-26 is strong in terms of carrying good speed into slow corners, while the Mercedes W17 is somewhere between the two. That makes the competitive balance heavily dependent on circuit layout.

Norris’s contention is that his car is insufficiently rounded to be dominant across the remaining rounds in the way last year’s McLaren was the car to beat at most tracks.

Norris played down the significance of his Dutch GP victory Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

"We have a strong car in certain areas," he said. "It's not like last year where we were pretty good everywhere. We're very, very strong in high speed. The place we've improved the car the most is high-speed performance.

"No one matches us in high speed. And that's a good thing. My pace advantage to Mercedes in Turn 7, Turn 8 was crazy.

"But their advantage that they have to us in slow speed is also crazy. And therefore I don't have the confidence to say, yeah, I can easily fight for a championship for the rest of the season. I know I've just won two races in a row and two poles in a row, but at the minute I don't have the car I need to fight for a championship.

"And I know that's quite a big comment, but I think last year I understood what is needed from a car and what was needed from me. And I know the level that I am now and what I can perform at. And I know just what I need from the car – and what tracks we have coming up where we're going to certainly struggle more."

The issue is more complex than simply saying a particular car is fast around a certain type of corner. This year’s cars are shorter, narrower and slightly lighter – and the chassis characteristics are more interconnected with power unit performance than ever before, given the influence of corner-entry speeds on energy harvesting.

McLaren's decision to run a short wheelbase, helping it save weight at the start of the season, has baked in certain shortcomings in terms of how much aerodynamic load the team can squeeze from the floor.

Performance is often hugely variable between tyre compounds. In Saturday’s sprint race, running mediums, Norris struggled with rear degradation and was overtaken by Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc in the closing stages. In the grand prix he took the restart on used softs, was passed by Antonelli at the start, and didn’t really get into the race until the hard-compound tyres went on.

Norris was able to pressure championship leader Antonelli later in the Zandvoort race Photo by: Andy Hone/ LAT Images via Getty Images

"We put on the hard tyres," he said. "We were a bit more aggressive with how we wanted to approach the stint. And we turned things around. I had that feeling in the car that I wanted. I went from just not feeling like I was going to win a race to at least we can force him [Antonelli] to make mistakes.

"When I get what I need from a car, when I have the front I want, when I get the confidence with the rear on entries – just when I get what I need to be able to know and predict every single corner, I'm going to win a race."

Norris has a driving style slightly more aligned to Max Verstappen than the likes of George Russell or even his own team-mate, Oscar Piastri. Rather than separating the throttle off/brake on and turning phases, he likes to blend the throttle and brakes and take a shallower approach angle. Essentially he is feeling for the point in the overlap where the front tyres begin to exert more lateral grip, which helps rotate the car and carry more speed into the corner, towards the apex.

This requires the car not only to have a 'strong' front end, but also to communicate what the front tyres are doing, which represents a tough engineering challenge. Modern F1 cars require a consistent ride height for the aerodynamics to function optimally, so the suspension geometry is designed to minimise dive and squat. A side of this is that it saps driver 'feel'.

Some can live with that, some can’t, which is why McLaren designed an alternate front suspension geometry with a revised kingpin angle for Norris when he was floundering at the beginning of last season. Once he has that feel he can be very adaptable in terms of his lines and the degree of overlap between throttle and brake, which is why he thrives in low-grip conditions.

But although he has a huge amount of adaptability within this range, he still needs that strong front end, good transmission of feel, and confidence that the rear axle will rotate predictably on cue.

"It's clear where our weaknesses are," Norris concluded. "Therefore we need to attack those things. And until we do that, it's still going to be a very tough end of the season."

Sports.title: FIA explains safety car formation lap after F1 driver criticism at Dutch GP
Sports.content:
The opening stages of the Formula 1 Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort descended into chaos after rain had started to fall during the grid procedure.

Max Verstappen crashed heavily on the exit of the final corner on the opening lap of the race. The Red Bull driver admitted that it was entirely his own mistake. The Dutchman thought he could get back on the throttle, but that part of the track was clearly still too wet.

Behind Verstappen, Gabriel Bortoleto also came close to crashing, although he miraculously managed to keep his Audi out of the wall, while it was even more remarkable that team-mate Nico Hulkenberg managed to avoid him.

The German immediately said over the radio that he feared he was going to T-bone Bortoleto.

"It was just that corner, if I'm very honest with you. It was full wets, that place. I think that's why Max lost it and it was the same for me," Bortoleto said in the media pen post-race.

"I was on the downside of the banking. I did a little reaction move to the left, I think, when I saw big smoke coming up ahead. And when I did that, I just went as well."

According to Gasly, F1 drivers would have been able to get their tyres up to temperature more effectively if the formation lap had been completed without the safety car Photo by: Clive Rose / Getty Images

Would a normal formation lap have been better?

According to the drivers, the rest of the track had already dried by that point, meaning it was simply a matter of surviving the final two corners. Starting on slicks therefore made sense, as did the FIA’s decision to opt for a standing start.

That said, several drivers were critical of how the start procedure was carried out at Zandvoort.

"If we would go the way we did with one lap behind the safety car and a standing start, then I would have preferred to just do a normal out-lap, so we would have pushed a bit faster,” Pierre Gasly said when asked by Motorsport.com.

"I thought the point was to go at least once through the last corner and the banking with the safety car before doing the normal race start. And yeah, it was damp."

According to the Alpine driver, the FIA would have been better off choosing between two conventional options: a rolling start behind the safety car or a standing start with a normal formation lap.

"I'm sure we'll review at the next race what the drivers' feedback was," Gasly continued. "But I think it was either no safety car and only one formation lap or with the safety car at least giving us one extra lap."

Red Bull stand-in Liam Lawson shared that view and added that he already knew before the start that the procedure would lead to chaos.

Lawson emphasises that he deliberately left more margin than his team-mate Verstappen in the final corner Photo by: Anni Graf - Formula 1 via Getty Images

"I don't know why we had the safety car. To do a standing start and also do a lap behind the safety car makes no sense," Lawson said when asked by Motorsport.com.

"I'm not sure what the reasoning of that was, but I feel like we could all see that coming. We were all probably saying the same thing before when we got the news, but we didn't have control over that."

FIA explains reasoning behind safety car formation lap

When asked by Motorsport.com, the FIA clarified that it acted on the information available at the time.

The race director first sent the medical car out for a reconnaissance lap, something an FIA spokesperson said does not normally happen.

The feedback from the medical car was that there was still standing water at Turns 2 and 3, with Turn 3 – the Hugenholtz corner – also being the first banked corner on the circuit. Based on that information, the FIA considered it safer to complete the formation lap behind the safety car.

The intention at that point was to have a standing start, but by completing the formation lap behind the safety car, race control kept both options open. If the standing water had been deemed too dangerous, it could still have opted for a rolling start.

Williams driver Carlos Sainz, however, felt the latter would not have been a solution and would not have prevented the chaos in the final corner.

Carlos Sainz, Williams Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

"I think, given it was towards the end of the lap, a non-standing start, a rolling start, would have ended up in the same result, because by that time we were all one by one," Sainz said. "So I don't think it would have changed much. It's an unfortunate situation with a lot of water in only one corner."

It therefore came down to the drivers’ own judgement, with Lawson stressing that he deliberately left more margin – considerably more than Verstappen, who was running ahead of him.

"It was just impossible. The whole first half of the lap was dry and then the last few corners were completely soaked. So, it was really easy to do that [what Max has done] when you have this much power on a slick tyre," he said.

"I really lifted out of it because honestly I had no confidence in how much grip we were going to have there and I think Max was probably trying to get closer and make an overtake, and just lost it."

Verstappen himself, however, did not want to blame any external factors and stressed that he had simply made a mistake.

Sports.title: Hamilton explains Dutch GP radio outburst over Ferrari team orders
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has urged Ferrari to be more like Mercedes with its efficiency after growing frustrated by a lack of team orders during the Formula 1 Dutch Grand Prix.

The Ferrari driver finished fourth in an action-packed contest at Zandvoort on Sunday, with his mid-race battle with stablemate Charles Leclerc arguably being Hamilton’s defining period.

Hamilton had just overtaken McLaren’s Oscar Piastri for fifth on lap 35 and was right behind a much slower Leclerc, so was therefore angling for team orders but they did not arrive.

“Great way of wasting time guys, good job,” complained a sarcastic Hamilton, who eventually took fourth when Leclerc pitted on lap 43 to end a very drawn-out process.

That is compared to Mercedes which swapped its cars with seven laps remaining, as George Russell gave second to Kimi Antonelli, who had fresher tyres so could attack Lando Norris.

Although the McLaren driver still took victory, it was a decision both Antonelli and Russell agreed with as they completed the podium ahead of Hamilton and fifth-placed Leclerc.

“I want to win,” Hamilton told F1 TV. “I want to win. I'm here to win and it is difficult when you're looking ahead and you see the two Mercedes drivers, they get the call and it's done - they execute straight away.

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Clive Rose / Formula 1 via Getty Images

“They let Kimi by and let him get on with the race. I was on a different strategy. It's not the same here and that's a little bit difficult, but we just have to take it.

“We'll take it offline, and when I go back now, I'll speak to them about it.”

Russell did well to take third though, as he feared that Mercedes had “lost a double podium”, because by letting Antonelli by, it put him under instant pressure from Hamilton.

The Mercedes driver held firm though, helped by the lap 70 virtual safety car for debris at Turn 5, and Hamilton reckons the earlier fiasco harmed his chances of overtaking his former team-mate.

When asked by Motorsport.com if the VSC stopped him from getting a podium, the seven-time world champion replied: “It felt like it was the closest opportunity I had.

“I think I'd come out of [Turn] 14 pretty close to him and I was just opening SM [Straight Line Mode] and just getting on the boost.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Michael Potts / LAT Images via Getty Images

“I don't know whether or not we would have got by because the Mercedes is just so quick. You saw the McLaren fly past just on power. We're losing like four tenths of a lap here just on straight lines.

“So that was a challenge, but I do think the time was lost when I was behind Charles, which ultimately meant I had a bigger distance to cover to try and catch up with George at the end.”

The result leaves Hamilton tied with Russell in second and 59 points behind Antonelli with 11 rounds remaining, a run where the Ferrari driver is hoping to add to his Barcelona victory.

But to do so Hamilton thinks the Italian marque must reduce its engine power deficit to Mercedes, despite various chassis upgrades it brought to the Netherlands.

“The one thing I'm definitely really proud of the team, they brought an upgrade here this weekend,” the 41-year-old added.

“We are getting closer to them but half the season we've been down in power. We really need to pick up the power if we're going to be anywhere near trying to fight for them and closing the gap to them.”

Sports.title: What caused Verstappen’s F1 Dutch GP crash
Sports.content:
Making mistakes may be uncharacteristic of Max Verstappen, but that’s exactly what the four-time world champion did on the first lap of his home Formula 1 race.

Starting the Dutch Grand Prix from seventh on the grid after feeling unwell all weekend, Verstappen took a decent getaway but found himself squeezed on the grass in a four-wide moment on the run to Turn 1. He was consequently challenged by Red Bull stand-in Liam Lawson in the following corners – which he didn’t mind: “We are allowed to race, so I think that's normal.”

Verstappen eventually held on to that seventh position, but a rain shower which occurred some 50 minutes before the start had dampened the track, and two drivers lost control in the banked final corner on lap one.

While Gabriel Bortoleto escaped from a 360-degree pirouette unscathed, Red Bull’s superstar couldn’t catch the RB22 and suffered a substantial crash, which caused a red flag.

“I think the start is just a consequence of what is happening on the right. It's OK, it can happen,” Verstappen commented regarding about the incident at lights out.

“Then, yeah, I got caught out. It was still quite wet in that corner, and as soon as I saw the dry patch coming, I was like, ‘Now you can accelerate’, but clearly that didn't work. So probably it was still a bit too early.”

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Photo by: Eric Le Galliot

Verstappen described the impact as “a decent hit” but clarified he’d “had worse”.

Red Bull eventually endured its worst grand prix since the April break results-wise, with Lawson its top car in seventh.

Verstappen did admit to “a disappointing weekend” in terms of pace as McLaren, Ferrari and Mercedes were out of reach, but this situation was no surprise to him.

“I wish for more, but you need to be realistic this season,” the Red Bull racer insisted. “We are the fourth-fastest team, so it's not like walking up to Zandvoort and suddenly we can do some magic things.

“It's just how it is, other teams have brought upgrades, we haven't. When you're already on the back foot, it puts you even more on the back foot. So, there's nothing surprising, it's just the reality that we live in.”

So Verstappen will now focus on resting ahead of the Italian Grand Prix, two weeks from now: “I've just not been feeling well. I'm just looking forward to a break where I can just recover also, because I really didn't feel good.”

Sports.title: F1 Dutch GP: Norris overhauls Antonelli for victory, Verstappen suffers heavy crash
Sports.content:
Formula 1 world champion Lando Norris produced a mega drive to win the Dutch Grand Prix from pole while home hero Max Verstappen caused a red flag by crashing out.

The McLaren driver crossed the line 11.5s ahead of runner-up Kimi Antonelli, with his Mercedes team-mate George Russell completing the podium at Zandvoort.

It came after Norris pipped sprint winner Russell for pole ahead of third-placed Antonelli and they all, like the rest of the grid, started on slicks despite rain an hour before lights out.

But the rain was on and off causing a wet-dry surface, the dangers of which emerged at the end of the opening lap once Norris had a perfect getaway while Antonelli overtook Russell at Turn 1.

That’s because Verstappen dipped a tyre onto the white line on the inside of the final corner, causing the Red Bull driver to spin into the barrier which spread debris on the circuit.

“Yeah that’s it - sorry!,” said the Dutchman via team radio, having brought out the red flag just as Gabriel Bortoleto also had a 360-degree spin at the banking but somehow avoided damage.

So another standing start followed - after Oliver Bearman suffered an engine failure on the formation tour - and much to Norris’ dismay this time, as Antonelli squeezed by at Turn 1 for the lead.

Start action Photo by: Clive Rose / Getty Images

That was despite softs on the McLaren compared to mediums for Antonelli, who essentially had a double delight as title rival Russell lost third to hard runner Oscar Piastri at Turn 7.

Russell just didn’t have the pace, soon being pressurised by Charles Leclerc as he reported balance problems, but the tight track allowed him to hold firm before swapping mediums for hards on lap 18.

McLaren responded the previous lap with Piastri, but this backfired as a slow 5.4s stop put him behind Russell just as Antonelli had streaked 2.2s clear of Norris out front.

That gap closed to a second once the pit window - where all the frontrunners chose hard tyres bar Leclerc on mediums - had passed, yet the reigning champion struggled to make inroads.

The wheel-to-wheel battles were more prevalent lower down: Yuki Tsunoda came out on top in a mega multi-car fight for the top 10, while Leclerc was constantly on Piastri’s tail.

That little battle finally ended on lap 34 when the Ferrari and McLaren went through the opening corners wheel-to-wheel, only for Leclerc to edge by for fourth around the outside of Turn 3.

There was yet more misery for Piastri as he was overtaken for fifth at Turn 1 on the following tour by Lewis Hamilton, who quickly closed in on team-mate Leclerc.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

The seven-time world champion was angling for team orders but they did not arrive and Hamilton sarcastically told his Ferrari squad: “Great way of wasting time guys, good job!”

Hamilton eventually moved by though once Leclerc made his second pitstop on lap 43, two tours after the Mercedes duo, and five before Norris came in for another set of hard tyres.

But Ferrari kept Hamilton out which left him with first on track, yet the battle for the net lead emerged behind as Norris rapidly closed on Antonelli, who complained about his rear Pirellis.

So come lap 54 Hamilton, Antonelli and Norris were all within a second and the reigning world champion made a sweeping move on Antonelli around the outside of Turn 1.

It was that same lap that Norris subsequently took the actual lead at Turn 11 from Hamilton, who dropped behind Antonelli at Turn 1 the following lap - just as Esteban Ocon caused a virtual safety car by stopping at Turn 4.

“Are you using me as a guinea pig,” complained Hamilton, wanting to pit, and that he finally did under the VSC by taking softs - likewise for Antonelli, while Norris and now second-placed Russell stayed out on hard rubber.

Norris admitted he was “worried” by that decision and had reasons to be so, as the advantage of the fresher tyre became evident with Antonelli quickly reducing his gap to Russell.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Clive Rose / Formula 1 via Getty Images

Mercedes eventually told the Briton to let his team-mate by with the swap occurring at Turn 1 on lap 65, but this left Russell vulnerable against Hamilton, claiming “we’ve lost a double podium”.

But Russell held firm, helped by a brief VSC on lap 70 for debris at Turn 5, to take the final podium spot, 4.3s behind Antonelli and 15.8s off Norris who took his second win of 2026.

Hamilton finished fourth, Leclerc took fifth and Piastri was sixth, while Red Bull stand-in Liam Lawson, Audi’s Nico Hulkenberg, Aston Martin’s Fernando Alonso and Alpine’s Pierre Gasly respectively completed the top 10.

The result has extended Antonelli’s championship advantage, as the 19-year-old leaves the Netherlands with a 59-point lead over both Russell and Hamilton in second.

Sports.title: Social Media: FIA defends stewards after Colapinto fans’ abuse | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The FIA has condemned abuse targeted at its stewards following the Dutch Grand Prix.

Although the governing body did not specify what the abuse related to, it received several hateful and abusive comments in relation to penalties issued to Franco Colapinto for failing to respond correctly to yellow flags. Two other drivers, Arvid Lindblad, and Liam Lawson, received the same penalties.

“Following the Dutch Grand Prix, FIA stewards were targeted with online abuse after applying sporting penalties in line with FIA regulations,” said the FIA in a statement.

“The United Against Online Abuse coalition condemns all forms of abuse and harassment. disagreement with decisions is part of sport, but it must never justify threats or personal attacks.

“In 2023, the FIA launched the United Against Online Abuse coalition after a steward faced targeted abuse following the United States Grand Prix.

“We urge everyone engaging with our sport to do so with respect and responsibility, online and offline.”

In addition to his penalty at the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix, Colapinto has been penalised three times this year for failing to respond correctly to yellow flags.

Sports.title: On This Day: Schumacher’s stunning debut ends early at Spa | Brief
Sports.content:
One of the most famous and consequential debuts in grand prix history came to a disappointingly early end 35 years ago today.

Michael Schumacher had already electrified the Formula 1 paddock at Spa-Francorchamps by putting Bertrand Gachot’s Jordan seventh on the grid. Unfortunately his clutch died as he pulled away from the grid, ending his race on the first lap.

The Jordans were quick at Spa – Schumacher’s team mate Andrea de Cesaris was closing on race leader Ayrton Senna until his Ford-Cosworth engine let him down. That left championship leader Senna to collect a valuable 10 points after title rival Nigel Mansell retired.

Sports.title: McLaren’s car is still “horrible to drive” despite consecutive wins, says Norris | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lando Norris may have won the last two grands prix in a row but he says McLaren’s car is still a handful to drive.

The world champion believes this is partly a consequence of the 2026 regulations.

“It’s tough to say, but I do think it’s a trickier car to drive this year in some ways,” said Norris. “I think you can see that because the gaps between team mates are often bigger this year, I would say, than it was last year.”

However Norris says he is doing better at communicating his needs to his team.

“I do believe I’m able to understand situations better, to understand the car in a better way,” he explained. “It’s still just horrible to drive, but I’m doing a better job at just understanding this, relaying this to my team, figuring stuff out.

“So, it’s not just that I’m driving better on track. I’m certainly eliminating my weaknesses on track, and I don’t have so many, but it’s also how I work off the track.”

He said the changes he made on his car between the sprint race and qualifying session in the Netherlands “is a perfect example of [how] the work we put in overnight transformed our race and gave me the opportunity to win.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Norris’s team mate Oscar Piastri also appeared to struggle with his car at times during Sunday’s race, where he finished sixth. At one stage he asked his race engineer Tom Stallard: “Please give me some help on how to drive this thing.”

Despite his wins in the last two rounds, Norris says McLaren must make significant improvements in their car’s low-speed cornering.

“We have a strong car in certain areas,” he said. “It’s not like last year where we were pretty good everywhere.

“We’re very, very strong in high speed, and that’s the place we’ve improved the car the most, is high-speed performance. No one matches us in high-speed, and that’s a good thing. My pace advantage to Mercedes in turn seven and eight was crazy, but the advantage that they have to us in slow speed is also crazy.

“Therefore, I don’t have the confidence to say, ‘Yeah, I can easily fight for a championship for the rest of the season.’ I know I’ve just won two races in a row and had two poles in a row, but at the minute I don’t have the car I need to fight for a championship.

“I know that’s quite a big comment, but I think last year I understood what is needed from a car and what was needed for myself. And I know the level that I am now and what I know I can perform at, and I know just what I need from the car and I know what tracks we have coming up where we’re going to certainly struggle more, and I don’t want to struggle more.

“So I’m just doing my part to make sure, as a team, we don’t relax, we don’t get complacent in any way, and we work more than we’ve ever done before, even more than the last two years when we’ve won championships. I need the guys and girls to work and focus better than ever before to improve on these areas. If we can improve on these slow speeds, I’m confident that I can win every race this season. If we don’t, then it’s much more difficult to believe so.”

Sports.title: Leclerc failed to obey two orders to pit while he held Hamilton up | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc was in no doubt Ferrari wanted him to pit when he was holding his team mate up during the Dutch Grand Prix.

The team originally hoped to bring Leclerc in on lap 41 but did not want him to follow George Russell’s Mercedes into the pit lane. Ferrari told their driver to pit “opposite” Russell, so when the Mercedes came in Leclerc followed his team’s order and did not pit as well.

Meanwhile Hamilton was gaining on Leclerc and becoming concerned his team mate would hold him up. Early on lap 42 Ferrari told Leclerc to come in.

However Leclerc disputed the order, telling Ferrari it would put him at a disadvantage to Russell, who had pitted earlier. After a period of silence, which was long enough for Leclerc to prompt his race engineer Bryan Bozzi for a reply, Ferrari gave the driver a second instruction to pit. But Leclerc did not come in.

Hamilton was becoming increasingly infuriated, telling the team “we’re just losing time.” After Leclerc finally pitted on the next lap, following another instruction from Ferrari, Hamilton sarcastically commented: “Big waste of time guys, good job.”

The Ferrari drivers finished the race behind Russell, with Hamilton fourth ahead of Leclerc.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur claimed after the race the team was willing to accept Hamilton losing some time at this stage in the race as they were attempting to reach the chequered flag without changing his tyres again.

“The story with Lewis was that at one stage we were trying to go to the end and I think it would have been a good call, also,” he told Sky. “Probably we lost one second with Charles. The target when you go to the end, it’s not this one, and for sure with what’s happened after, you can always rewrite the race.”

Sports.title: Stroll demanded penalties after Bearman and Bortoleto passed red pit exit light | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lance Stroll urged race control to penalise two of his rivals for leaving the pit lane while a red light was shown during the Dutch Grand Prix.

The incident occured as the field left the pits when the race resumed following the stoppage caused by Max Verstappen’s crash.

The pit lane exit lights were green as the field began to leave the pits. However after Fernando Alonso passed by the signal changed to a flashing red light.

Oliver Bearman and Gabriel Bortoleto both drove past the flashing red light. Neither acknowledged the pit lane exit had been closed and continued to the grid, though Bearman suffered a power unit failure before he got there.

Stroll, who was following the pair, noticed the light had changed and alerted his race engineer Gary Gannon:

Stroll The lights red, huh? Light’s red. Gannon Checking, I’m checking. Stroll I’m not going unless it’s green. Gannon Yeah, understood Lance. Stroll 10 seconds later

Tell me if I can go or not. Gannon Waiting to hear back from the FIA.

The signal changes to green and Stroll leaves the pit exit

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

He repeatedly called for the drivers who had passed the red signal to be penalised. Stroll correctly noted that Formula 1’s penalty guidelines state drivers who pass a red light at the pit lane exit during a race should receive 10-second stop-and-go penalties:

Stroll So everybody that went under a red should get a penalty. Gannon Yep, yep. Stroll Stop and go. Gannon Understood, we’ll report it. So the back of the pack… Stroll It’s the rules. Gannon …the back of the pack is in nine, so you can build temp. Good pushing to build temp

Stroll appeared to be under the impression that many more drivers than just the two immediately in front of him had driven past the red signal:

Stroll It’s clear that everyone went under red, then they all should get a penalty. Gannon We’re checking it now. Stroll Stop and go. Gannon Yeah, we’re checking now. Stroll Everybody. Gannon It started out green and then it went red and we’re checking who went through red and reporting it ASAP. Absolutely Lance.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

The Aston Martin driver continued to press his case on the formation lap, even when his race engineer was trying to warn him about Bearman’s stoppage ahead:

Gannon ‘Bearman is slow between 10-11. Yellow ahead for Bearman stopped. Bearman stopped between 10-11. Watch for Bearman… Stroll Those are the rules. Gannon …there, watch for Bearmen. Stroll The rules are: it’s red… Gannon Lance, we’ve reported it, we reported it. Now let’s get focused getting around to the grid, okay? We’ve reported and they will action it.

However the stewards chose instead to only reprimand the pair, pointing out that the incident occured before the race resumption and neither had gained an advantage.

“The pit exit light turned red when the driver was approaching the pit exit to join the track for the re-start of the race after a suspension,” they noted. “Such an infringement happening during the race normally requires a very significant penalty as the drivers are obliged to obey light signals at all times. However, in this case the infringement did not happen during a live race, but rather on the build-up before the re-start, although the race had technically already resumed in accordance with Article B5.15.2g.

“In addition to that, the stewards acknowledge that neither any advantage was gained nor any potentially dangerous or unsafe situation was created. Therefore a reprimand to the driver is deemed appropriate given the mitigating circumstances and the unique scenario.”

Sports.title: Matchroom Presses WBA To Force Teofimo Lopez vs. Jack Catterall
Sports.content:
“When I met Gilberto Mendoza in Egypt, I shook his hand and he gave me his word if I beat Giyasov, someone who was avoided and waited for his shot for two years, I will get my shot within 180 days regardless who has the belt. So I believe the WBA will do the correct thing,” Catterall posted.

That account removes much of the uncertainty about what the WBA intended. Its published resolution named Rolando Romero, but its president allegedly told Catterall that the commitment followed the title. Lopez still has a technical argument based on the written wording, yet the WBA would have to break Mendoza’s personal promise to let him move on.

The dispute began after Lopez openly denied that Catterall was his mandatory during Monday’s Inside the Ring show. Lopez plans to pursue the three additional titles he needs to become the undisputed welterweight champion, beginning with the winner of Ryan Garcia versus Conor Benn on September 12.

That pursuit leaves no place for Catterall, but the secondary WBA champion has rejected the easiest negotiated solution.

“There’s not $1 that can persuade me to step aside to allow a unification bout to happen. I’m here to fight,” Catterall said.

His refusal means Matchroom cannot be paid to wait while Lopez pursues the Garcia vs. Benn winner. The WBA must enforce the consolidation fight, permit a unification first, or allow its two welterweight champions to remain separated.

The 180-day period expires on November 19, based on Catterall’s May 23 victory over Shakhram Giyasov. That leaves less than three months to settle the dispute. The cut Lopez suffered over his right eyebrow against Rolando Romero places more strain on the schedule, although there has been no indication that it will keep him out for an extended period.

Teofimo may believe the WBA will permit a unification to take priority over its internal consolidation fight. Sanctioning bodies regularly move mandatory obligations aside when champions pursue another belt, giving his team a stronger argument than the wording omission alone.

Catterall brings tactical risk with little financial reward. His awkward southpaw style and sharp counterpunching deny opponents clean offensive opportunities. Ryan Garcia, Conor Benn and Devin Haney generate massive paydays. Catterall brings no comparable commercial appeal, only a genuine threat to expose Lopez inside the ring.

WBA Loophole Gives Teofimo Lopez Easy Out On Jack Catterall

A review of the WBA’s published rulings supports part of Teofimo Lopez’s argument. No public order currently names Jack Catterall as the mandatory challenger for Lopez’s newly acquired Super welterweight title.

The May 21 ruling required Rolando Romero to face the Catterall-Shakhram Giyasov winner within 180 days. Its language named Romero specifically. It did not say the obligation would transfer to Romero’s successor if the title changed hands.

That omission gives Lopez a technical basis for denying that Catterall has been formally assigned to him. The WBA would need to issue another ruling, clarify that the original order followed the championship, or designate Catterall as Lopez’s challenger.

Teofimo still goes too far by claiming Catterall was lied to. The WBA sanctioned the Giyasov bout and publicly stated that its winner would receive Romero within 180 days. Catterall’s expectation came directly from the organization, not from an invented promise by his team.

The real issue is poor wording from the WBA. It created two champions and ordered them to meet, yet attached the obligation to Romero by name rather than clearly attaching it to the Super title. Lopez is now using that opening to pursue the Garcia-Benn winner while Catterall waits for the WBA to explain what its own ruling means.

Teofimo Lopez Denies Jack Catterall Mandatory Status

Teofimo Lopez claims Jack Catterall is not his WBA mandatory and says the British contender was lied to about his right to challenge for the welterweight title.

During today’s Inside the Ring show, Catterall confronted the new WBA champion after Lopez discussed facing the Ryan Garcia vs. Conor Benn winner and eventually meeting Devin Haney for the undisputed championship.

“He’s not. He’s not my mandatory,” Lopez said when Catterall was identified as next in line. “By the sanctioning rules, he’s not my mandatory, and I think they lied. I think they lied to him.”

“It’s in the contract,” Catterall answered.

Teofimo’s denial conflicts with the WBA’s own published ruling. When the organization elevated Rolando Romero to Super champion in May, it sanctioned Catterall’s bout with Shakhram Giyasov for the vacant secondary title and stated that Romero had to face the winner within 180 days.

Catterall defeated Giyasov and now holds that belt. Lopez may argue that the ruling named Romero rather than whoever defeated him, or that no separate order has been issued since Saturday. Neither explanation supports his claim that Catterall was lied to. The WBA publicly connected the two titles and imposed a deadline for bringing them together.

The exchange became entertaining because Lopez tried to rewrite the situation while Catterall was on the screen looking directly at him. Rather than explain the supposed sanctioning rule, Teofimo declared that the obligation did not exist and blamed unnamed people for misleading Catterall.

After making that denial, the new champion returned to the familiar claim that he will face anyone.

“I’m always willing to fight anybody and everybody,” Lopez said.

“I’m glad you won on the weekend because I know you don’t duck nobody,” Catterall replied. “It would have been more difficult to get Rolly into the ring. I’m happy for you, but we’ve got to get it on.”

Catterall played the interaction perfectly. He congratulated Lopez, reminded him that Romero would have been harder to bring into the ring and declined to turn the conversation into a shouting match. That left Teofimo arguing against a contract he had not seen while Catterall calmly insisted the terms were already written down.

There was also some clever pressure inside Catterall’s praise. Telling Lopez, “I know you don’t duck nobody,” gave the champion little room to reject the fight without contradicting the reputation Catterall had just assigned to him.

The WBA now needs to explain the status of its own ruling. It can grant Lopez permission to pursue a unification, arrange a step-aside payment or order the title consolidation. What it cannot credibly do is remain silent while its new champion claims the other titleholder was fooled.

Lopez is clearly trying to look past the mandatory to chase the massive paydays against the Ryan Garcia vs. Conor Benn winner or a unification with Devin Haney. Catterall holds the regular belt after beating Shakhram Giyasov, which, in standard WBA procedure, makes him the direct mandatory to unify the titles.

Sports.title: Esteban De Jesús Shatters Roberto Durán’s Invincibility
Sports.content:
Durán had captured the WBA and Ring lightweight titles from Ken Buchanan five months earlier at the same arena. Two quick stoppages followed, and the 10-round meeting with De Jesús may have looked like another chance to stay active in New York.

His preparation was far from ideal. Durán had suffered an injured elbow and cuts to his lip in a car accident. Reports also described a young champion enjoying the rewards of his new position and treating the fight less seriously than De Jesús did.

Both boxers came in above the lightweight limit, with Durán at 137½ pounds and De Jesús at 138. That kept the championship belts out of reach, but the absence of titles did nothing to reduce the importance of what followed.

De Jesús was 22 years old and carried only one defeat on a record listed around 32-1 or 33-1. The former Puerto Rican lightweight champion possessed the timing, composure and left hook needed to punish Durán’s aggression.

Protecting his early advantage, De Jesús worked from range, used his jab and combinations, then caught Durán with the left hook when the champion tried to force his way inside.

The usual Durán pressure never fully arrived. He landed enough hard punches to remain dangerous, including a right hand during the eighth that forced De Jesús to clinch, but his attacks lacked their normal volume. Frustration showed in the fifth when referee Arthur Mercante warned him for hitting after the break and delivering a low blow. Both men continued punching after the bell in the eighth.

Ten rounds later, all three officials favored De Jesús before 9,144 spectators. Mercante gave him five rounds to Durán’s four, with one even. Harold Lederman scored six rounds for De Jesús and three for Durán, with one even, while Bill Recht gave De Jesús six rounds, Durán two, and scored two even. The $62,339 gate reflected the interest surrounding Durán’s New York return, but the night belonged to the Puerto Rican contender.

The defeat did not diminish Durán for long. It gave him a target.

Their second fight came in Panama in March 1974, this time with the WBA lightweight title at stake. De Jesús floored Durán again in the opening round, but the champion recovered and stopped him in the 11th.

The deciding meeting followed four years later in Las Vegas with the WBA and WBC championships on the line. Durán ended their rivalry by stopping De Jesús in the 12th round, completing his domination of the lightweight division before moving up in weight.

Competition eventually gave way to something deeper. In 1989, Durán visited De Jesús as his former opponent was dying from AIDS. He embraced and kissed him publicly during a period when fear and stigma surrounded the disease.

That 1972 upset remains one of the defining results of the decade. De Jesús did not catch an unknown prospect before his prime. He defeated the reigning lightweight champion, then forced one of boxing’s greatest fighters to spend the next six years proving that night would never happen again.

Sports.title: Joe Cordina Cannot Afford Another Wasted Year
Sports.content:
Stevenson withdrew after suffering a hand injury during training and underwent surgery. The cancellation cost Cordina a world title fight through no fault of his own, but Matchroom then needed nearly nine months to get him back into the ring.

Jaret Gonzalez Quiroz was a reasonable opponent for his lightweight return in July 2025. Coming back against a limited fighter made sense after the Cacace defeat, the Stevenson cancellation and more than a year outside the ring. The mistake was giving Cordina a second rebuilding fight five months later. Gabriel Flores Jr. carried a higher ranking and a recognizable name, but he presented little danger to a boxer with Cordina’s championship experience. One tune up should have been enough.

After defeating Flores by unanimous decision on December 13, Cordina became the WBO’s No. 1 lightweight contender. He then waited nearly seven months for a title fight against Abdullah Mason in Cleveland.

That date was lost when the United States embassy refused Cordina’s visa application. He had been charged following an alleged February incident in Cardiff and later pleaded not guilty to two counts of assault by beating. Cordina maintains that he acted in self defence, and his trial is scheduled for October 13.

The Stevenson cancellation was beyond Cordina’s control. The Mason situation cannot be treated in quite the same way. Whatever the trial ultimately decides, circumstances involving Cordina resulted in the visa refusal and removed him from the biggest fight available to him.

Matchroom should already have placed him on a UK card against a respectable lightweight, but Cordina also carries responsibility for demanding an active schedule. A 34 year old former champion cannot passively protect a No. 1 ranking while months of his career disappear. Even a 10 round bout would have kept him active and shown that he intended to remain a serious lightweight contender.

Since Cacace stopped him in May 2024, Cordina has fought only twice, and neither opponent showed how he would perform against a leading lightweight. His world championship experience means he does not require an extended rebuilding process.

Neither title fight took place, but the long periods surrounding them were avoidable. At 34, Cordina needs meaningful opposition, not another year spent waiting.

Sports.title: Lou DiBella Says Zuffa Will Seize U.S. Boxing Immediately
Sports.content:
The established companies had decades to reduce the number of titles, arrange the leading fights, and develop boxers into recognizable stars. Instead, promoters protected their champions as financial assets while the sanctioning bodies produced regular, interim, and super titles.

Becoming a champion consequently lost much of its value. DiBella argued that the average titleholder can walk through Times Square during rush hour without being recognized.

“We opened the door for Jake [Paul]. We opened the door for Turki Alalshikh. We opened the door for Zuffa and TKO. We opened the door for Dana and Nick. Anyone saying we didn’t open that door is a liar.”

Zuffa Boxing also has a clearer route to casual American viewers. Paramount already owns a large entertainment platform, while DAZN remains known primarily among dedicated boxing followers in the United States.

Hearn received particularly harsh criticism for his attempt to conquer the American market. DiBella described him as an effective self-promoter who can make individual events feel important, but said he returned to Britain “with his tail between his legs.”

His failure leaves Matchroom, Queensberry, Top Rank, and PBC facing a company with a stronger US television position and a centralized business model. British promoters have the best chance of remaining powerful because the UK is boxing’s strongest national market, DiBella believes, but he sees no traditional promotional company equipped to stop Zuffa in America.

The risk is that Zuffa replaces boxing’s fragmented system with a near-monopoly that controls fighters, championships, and matchmaking. DiBella dislikes that outcome, yet his larger argument is difficult to dismiss: the old guard had control of boxing and gave Zuffa every reason to believe it can run the business better.

Sports.title: PBC Prospect Joseph Brown Remains Unbeaten
Sports.content:
Normally, when you view a Joseph Brown bout, you see a boxer who establishes the range, uses his jab, his footwork, and lands sharp combinations. On the night of August 22nd, we saw a more aggressive version of Joseph Brown.

In the opening round of the bout, Brown stood in the pocket, threw the jab, and connected with shots in between his opponent’s shots. During the early part of the 2nd round, Wiggins changed the bout from boxing to grappling.

Despite the excessive clenching from his opponent, Brown was able to land solid shots to the body. Brown turned up his aggression in round three as he pressed forward, but Wiggins was able to sneak in a good right hand.

Joseph Brown responded by landing a sharp right to the body, and during the final seconds of the third round, Brown switched to southpaw and landed a double jab. In the fifth round of the bout, Brown started in the southpaw stance.

While in the southpaw stance, Brown connected with the jab, and when he switched to orthodox, he landed a couple of solid combinations. During the sixth and final round of the bout, Brown put his skills on display.

He landed the jab, the lead right hand, combination shots, and he did a little showboating in between. At the conclusion of the contest, Brown was declared the winner on all three judges’ cards by the identical score of (60-54).

With the victory, Joseph Brown improved his record to (8-0, 5 KOs). During a brief interview with Vince DWriter, Joseph Brown stated how he earned the win when he said, “I think my keys to victory were being smart with my shot selection, and pressing the action.”

Joseph Brown is a prospect who has no knowledge of losing because he never lost as an amateur, and he’s currently undefeated as a pro. As an amateur, Brown’s overall combat record was (67-0).

Between boxing and kickboxing, he won a total of six national titles, and he won a world championship in Muay Thai. Brown started his career with Mayweather Promotions, but he recently made a career-defining move.

During his interview, Joseph Brown spoke on his change of scenery and the challenges he faced leading up to fight night.

Sports.title: Tim Tszyu Reduced To Hunting Boxing’s Faded Names
Sports.content:
It is difficult to believe his career has been reduced to this so early. Consecutive losses to Sebastian Fundora and Bakhram Murtazaliev clearly changed the direction of his matchmaking.

Fundora took Tszyu’s title by split decision in March 2024 after an accidental elbow opened a severe cut. The defeat came with an excuse because Tszyu fought through blood pouring into his eyes. Murtazaliev removed any room for rationalization seven months later, dropping him repeatedly before getting a third-round stoppage.

Since then, Tszyu has gone from pursuing the strongest opponents available to hunting recognizable fighters coming off long inactivity spells. Spence had not competed in nearly three years before their fight. Charlo has fought once since May 2022 and has never boxed at middleweight.

The money for facing Spence must have been substantial because Tszyu seems eager to repeat the formula. Charlo offers an old storyline and far less certainty than an active contender in his prime. That may make financial sense, but it does little to establish Tszyu as a serious middleweight.

At 31, he should be targeting Yoenli Hernández, Denzel Bentley or WBA champion Erislandy Lara. His drawing power in Australia gives him enough leverage to pursue any of the four middleweight champions without spending years moving through eliminators.

Hernández and Bentley would show how Tszyu handles active, natural middleweights. Lara would give him an opportunity to win a title against a respected champion. Those fights carry genuine sporting value.

Crossing Spence off the shirt creates the image of a mission being completed. In reality, Tszyu defeated one faded name and immediately selected another. Charlo is at least attainable. Crawford and Canelo merely make an archaic list look important.

Sports.title: William Zepeda Owes Jadier Herrera The First Shot
Sports.content:
That decision was difficult to defend. Interim championships are supposed to protect a contender’s position when the full champion is unavailable. Herrera did exactly what the WBC asked, stopping Ricardo Núñez in the eighth round, only to watch Zepeda and Roach compete for the higher belt.

A March divisional update stated that the Zepeda-Roach winner must meet Herrera. Unless that instruction has changed, the WBC should now order the consolidation fight instead of approving a voluntary defense.

Herrera presents a far greater physical threat than Roach did. The 23-year-old southpaw is 5-foot-11 and has stopped 16 of his 18 opponents. Núñez dropped him early in their fight, but Herrera recovered and gradually broke down a much more experienced puncher.

Zepeda said after beating Roach that he wants to become undisputed rather than naming an opponent. That ambition gives his team a reason to pursue another champion instead of Herrera or Cruz, but it does not erase the WBC’s previous instruction. The organization already made Herrera wait while Zepeda fought for the vacant belt. Allowing a unification before the consolidation bout would extend that delay and reduce the interim championship to little more than a bargaining tool.

Andy Cruz has now created more uncertainty in the division by publicly targeting Zepeda.

“William Zepeda, I’m coming for you,” Cruz told reporters.

The WBC placed Cruz at No. 1 after his third-round stoppage of Abraham Montoya in July. His Olympic background and close loss to IBF champion Raymond Muratalla give him greater name recognition than Herrera, making Cruz the easier fight to sell.

That does not give him a stronger claim. Cruz was granted an IBF title opportunity in only his seventh professional bout and lost. Herrera won the WBC interim championship, then waited while Zepeda received another title fight immediately after losing to Shakur Stevenson.

Zepeda-Cruz would test the champion against an accurate counterpuncher capable of controlling him from long range. It is one of the best fights available at lightweight, but Herrera should not be discarded to make it happen.

If Zepeda wants Cruz next, Herrera must agree to step aside. Otherwise, the WBC needs to honor its own order and give its interim champion the position his belt was supposed to guarantee.

Sports.title: The Ring’s Welterweight Rankings Reward the Wrong Fighters
Sports.content:
The Ring previously excluded Romero because of inactivity. He returned Saturday night, fought with little urgency, surrendered his WBA title to Teofimo Lopez and was rewarded with a ranking. The panel effectively treated losing as a promotional achievement because Romero remains a recognizable name.

If inactivity made him unworthy before the fight, a poor performance followed by a defeat should not have restored him. Romero threw only 352 punches across 12 rounds and allowed Lopez to take control without producing anything close to an elite performance.

Lopez belongs in the top 10 after collecting the WBA belt, but placing him fifth is another triumph of name recognition over what happened inside the ring. He landed 124 punches, was hurt more than once and received a 114-114 score from one judge. Scraping past a reluctant, limited opponent does not instantly make Lopez one of the five best welterweights. The Ring’s treatment of Jack Catterall and Arnold Barboza Jr. is just as difficult to defend. Catterall is ranked third, while Barboza is excluded despite defeating him directly. Head-to-head results should provide the foundation for credible ratings. Ignoring that result leaves the panel ranking reputation instead of performance.

Keyshawn Davis, Liam Paro and Richardson Hitchins are also missing. Davis’s last two fights took place at light welterweight, but he operated at a higher level than virtually everyone on the published list. If divisional activity automatically disqualifies him, that rule should be applied consistently rather than abandoned whenever a famous fighter acquires a belt.

Paro owns the IBF championship, yet belt ownership did not protect him from removal. Hitchins entered at No. 9 after defeating Ricardo Salas in his welterweight debut, then vanished without losing. The Ring uses belts as hall passes for Haney and Lopez while ignoring one when it belongs to Paro.

Brian Norman Jr. remaining at No. 2 adds to the disorder. He looked terrible against Devin Haney, landing only 59 of 399 punches. Stopping little-known non-contender Josh Wagner afterward did not prove that Norman is the division’s second-best fighter.

Alexis Rocha, Raul Curiel, Rohan Polanco, Eimantas Stanionis and Romero should be removed. A list based on present ability would look closer to this:

Keyshawn Davis Richardson Hitchins Liam Paro Devin Haney Brian Norman Jr. Jack Catterall Arnold Barboza Jr. Teofimo Lopez Ryan Garcia

The tenth position should remain vacant until somebody earns it. The Ring has filled its list, but it has not identified the best welterweights.

Ghana News.title: Police arrest seven in Ashanti Region narcotics crackdown
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Police Service has arrested seven persons in separate intelligence-led operations targeting suspected narcotics-related activities in the Ashanti Region.

The operations were conducted by the Inspector-General of Police (IGP) Special Operations Team (SOT) at Ejisu, Abrepo Junction and Atimatim on Thursday, August 20, 2026.

According to a police statement issued by the Ashanti Regional Public Affairs Unit, the operations followed intelligence gathered on suspected narcotics activities in the three locations.

At Ejisu, the police arrested Nana Kwadwo Adu, 43, and Nana Kwame Fella, 48.

Four others were arrested at Abrepo Junction. They are Stephanie Anokye, 23; Roland Anokye, 20; Gideon Owusu, 30; and Grace Fosua, 27.

At Atimatim, the operation targeted Kofi Opoku, 27, who the police said was suspected of involvement in the peddling of narcotic substances and had reportedly evaded arrest on previous occasions.

The police said the operations led to the recovery of quantities of pill pouches containing dried leaves suspected to be narcotic substances.

Other items recovered included quantities of Tramaking 225mg and 250mg, Royal 255mg and Rophynol 100mg, as well as 860 tablets and capsules of Tramadol suspected to be unregistered drugs.

An unspecified amount of Ghanaian currency was also recovered during the operations.

The seven suspects are currently in police custody and are assisting with investigations.

The police said the ongoing investigations are aimed at establishing the source of the substances, determining the full extent of the suspects’ involvement and identifying other persons who may be connected to the suspected activities.

The Ashanti Regional Police Command has urged the public to continue providing credible information to assist the police in their efforts to maintain public safety and security.

The Command said further updates will be provided as and when necessary.

Ghana News.title: Turf Club condemns Accra Race Course demolition, calls for Prez Mahama’s intervention
Ghana News.content:
The Accra Turf Club has condemned the forceful entry, demolition and alleged takeover of its Race Course at Borteyman, describing the incident as “extremely serious.”

The Club is appealing for urgent government intervention following the incident on Saturday, August 22.

It says “about 200 armed men, led by persons identifying themselves as Clement Dzato and another person referred to as Azuma, forcefully entered the premises of the Accra Race Course.”

The Club says the group was accompanied by police officers and heavy-duty equipment and “proceeded to undertake total demolition and destruction of the Accra Race Course facilities.”

It alleges that about 100 horse stables were demolished, while horses were forcibly removed and jockeys ejected from their residential facilities.

The Club says it made several attempts to secure police intervention to stop the demolition, but the destruction continued.

“The Accra Turf Club therefore calls for urgent, lawful and decisive intervention to protect the Club’s property, restore its possession, safeguard its horses and personnel, and preserve Ghana’s horse racing heritage.”

“President of the Republic of Ghana, His Excellency John Dramani Mahama; the Minister for the Interior, Hon. Muntaka Mohammed-Mubarak; the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Hon. Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah; the Attorney-General and Minister for Justice, Dr. Dominic Akuritinga Ayine; the Inspector-General of Police, Christian Tetteh Yohuno; the National Security Coordinator, DCOP Abdul-Osman Razak to urgently intervene in this matter," The club said in a statement.

It is also demanding the immediate removal of what it describes as “land grabbers and encroachers” from the property.

The Club says the Race Course is an important part of Ghana’s sporting heritage and supports livelihoods within the equestrian sector.

“The Accra Race Course is not merely a piece of land… It represents the continuation of a long-standing Ghanaian sporting tradition whiles providing livelihood for more than 30,000 members in the equestrian fraternity, including jockeys, trainers, horse owners, groomers and others whose activities depends largely on horse racing.”

The Club says it will pursue all lawful means to protect its property, rights and Ghana’s horse racing heritage.

“We are confident that His Excellency the President will act swiftly and decisively to right this wrong, protect the integrity of the Government’s directives, and ensure that the rule of law is upheld in this matter.”

Ghana News.title: NPP alleges GoldBod gold purchases could be fuelling galamsey
Ghana News.content:
The New Patriotic Party (NPP) has raised concerns over the role of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) in the fight against illegal mining, alleging that its gold purchasing arrangements may be allowing illegally mined gold to enter the formal market.

Speaking at a media briefing on Tuesday, August 25, 2026, NPP National Organiser Henry Nana Boakye questioned the effectiveness of the mechanisms used by GoldBod and its licensed buyers to establish the origin of gold purchased from mining communities.

He argued that weaknesses in the gold supply chain could make it difficult to distinguish between gold produced by legally licensed miners and that obtained through illegal mining activities, popularly known as galamsey.

“GoldBod, I can tell you now, is the cause of the environmental destruction we are seeing. They are now responsible for galamsey,” Mr Boakye alleged.

According to him, the concerns go beyond the NPP, with stakeholders within the mining sector, including the Ghana Chamber of Mines and some Members of Parliament, also questioning the source of gold purchased through GoldBod’s network.

Mr Boakye challenged GoldBod to explain how it verifies the origin of gold before it is purchased and subsequently introduced into the formal trading system.

“If GoldBod is not buying galamsey gold, then who is?” he asked, insisting that the state-owned institution must provide greater clarity on its gold sourcing and traceability processes.

He also criticised what he described as repeated assurances that measures were being developed to strengthen traceability, arguing that the concerns surrounding the source of gold entering the formal market remain unresolved.

The NPP National Organiser is therefore calling for greater transparency in GoldBod’s operations, particularly in relation to the processes used by the institution and its licensed buyers to verify the source of gold purchased from miners.

The allegations come amid continuing national efforts to curb illegal mining, which has been blamed for widespread environmental degradation and the pollution of water bodies across the country.

Ghana News.title: Journalists cautioned against exposing cyber vulnerabilities, disrupting investigations
Ghana News.content:
Journalists have been cautioned against publishing unverified claims about cyber criminals or prematurely disclosing unresolved vulnerabilities in computer systems.

Alex Awere-Kyere, Senior Manager for Critical Information Infrastructure (CII) at the Cyber Security Authority (CSA), said that while the media had an important role to play in exposing cyber threats and educating the public, journalists needed to balance the public interest with the potential security implications of their reports.

“Sometimes, in our quest to do media enterprise, we may publish information that can disrupt investigations or give cybercriminals an indication of the next move of the security agencies,” he said.

Mr Awere-Kyere made the remarks during a training session for media practitioners under the National Community Media Cyber Capacity Building Project (NCMCCBP), aimed at strengthening journalists’ capacity to report responsibly on cybersecurity.

He explained that premature publication of information about vulnerabilities in computer systems could provide criminals with a roadmap to exploit those weaknesses before they were fixed.

He urged journalists who received sensitive information about cyber incidents to engage the CSA or other relevant security agencies before publication.

“Where the security agencies advise that we hold on to certain information, the media should heed that advice or engage the authority to determine which aspects of the information can safely be made public,” he said.

Mr Awere-Kyere noted that 13 sectors, including banking and finance, energy, water, and health, had been designated as Critical Information Infrastructure sectors due to their importance to national security and the economy.

A disruption to the operations of such institutions, he said, could have consequences far beyond the affected organisation and potentially affect the wider economy.

Mr Awere-Kyere also urged the public not to wait until they had lost money before reporting suspected mobile money fraud.

He said an early report to the CSA could allow the authority and the police to intervene before a fraudulent transaction was completed.

“Once the victim transfers the money to the fraudster and the money is withdrawn from the mobile money account. The prospects of recovering it become very slim,” he said.

He encouraged the public to report suspected mobile money fraud to the CSA through a toll-free number -292 before completing the transaction, where possible.

He said mobile money fraud involving stolen personal information was handled through the Joint Cybersecurity Committee established under Section 13 of the Cybersecurity Act, 2020 (Act 1038).

The Committee brings together the CSA, Bank of Ghana, National Communications Authority, Economic and Organised Crime Office, Ghana Army, and the Criminal Investigations Department of the Ghana Police Service.

Mr Awere-Kyere said tackling mobile money fraud required more than pursuing the perpetrators after money had been stolen, stressing the need to address how victims’ personal information got into the hands of fraudsters.

That, he said, required collaboration among the CSA, Data Protection Commission, telecommunications operators, and other members of the Joint Cybersecurity Committee.

The engagement formed part of a series of training sessions under the NCMCCBP, being implemented by the CSA, Africa Centre for Digital Transformation (ACDT), and the Government of the Czech Republic.

The project was launched in Accra on August 3, 2026, to build the capacity of journalists and media practitioners to understand cybersecurity issues and report on them accurately and responsibly.

The programme is scheduled to move to Kumasi in September.

The training comes at a time when cyber-related incidents are becoming increasingly relevant to everyday life, making the media’s role in informing the public critical.

Mr Awere-Kyere said responsible cyber reporting should help the public stay safe without inadvertently handing cybercriminals the information they need to strike.

Ghana News.title: African Political Parties Summit to convene in Addis Ababa in November
Ghana News.content:
The second edition of the African Political Parties Summit (APPS) will be held in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, from November 5 to 7, 2026, with political leaders expected to deliberate on the role of political parties in driving Africa’s economic transformation.

The summit is being convened by the Africa Governance Centre (AGC) in collaboration with the Ethiopian government under the high patronage of Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali.

This year’s summit is themed “Governing for Growth: Political Parties as Architects of Africa’s Economic Future.”

Organisers say the gathering will focus on how political leadership can contribute to industrialisation, sustainable development, regional integration and the creation of resilient African economies.

The 2026 summit builds on the inaugural edition held in Accra, Ghana, in August 2025, which brought together more than 100 representatives of political parties from across the continent.

That meeting ended with the adoption of the Accra Declaration, a 10-point commitment aimed at promoting good governance, regional integration and inclusive development.

The Africa Governance Centre says the Addis Ababa summit comes at a defining moment for the continent as African countries seek to accelerate economic transformation while dealing with complex socio-economic challenges.

Discussions are expected to examine how political parties can help strengthen accountable institutions and advance development priorities in line with the African Union’s Agenda 2063.

Two flagship platforms will form part of the 2026 summit — the African Youth in Politics Forum (AYPF) and the Africa Women Political Leadership Summit (AWPLS).

The platforms are expected to provide dedicated spaces for discussions on youth and women’s participation in political leadership and ways of improving their representation in Africa’s political systems.

Organisers say recommendations from the two platforms will feed into the Addis Ababa Declaration, which is expected to capture shared priorities and commitments on strengthening development-oriented political institutions across the continent.

The summit will bring together political party representatives and other stakeholders to examine how political leadership can support Africa’s economic ambitions and contribute to sustainable development.

Ghana News.title: We will explore all options including legal on Tarkwa mine lease renewal – Gold Fields
Ghana News.content:
GoldFields

Gold Fields has revealed that it is open to exploring all options and avenues including legal , on fresh proposals for the renewal of the Tarkwa mine lease.

According to the mining giant, this is to ensure that it gets a fair and equitable treatment on the consideration lease renewal of the Tarkwa mines by the Government of Ghana.

The Chief Executive of Gold Fields, Mike Fraser, disclosed this to Journalists around the world through a conference call from South Africa today, August 25 2026.

Mr. Fraser stated his outfit is looking this way, because of the uncertainty and delays on taking decision on issue, adding that “this is why this option is being considered”.

“We remain hopeful that the engagement that we are having and will be sensible consideration of our application”, the Group CEO of Gold Fields added.

He also stated that after working in the Ghana mining sector for more than 20 years, “we believe that we are in a better place to deliver value to Ghanaians as well as operate it safely”.

The Group CEO of Gold Fields disclosed that this plan to alert their investors on the options available when it comes to the lease agreement for the Takwa mines in Ghana.

Mr. Freser went ahead to state that Gold Fields is, however, hopeful to get to the level where this legal option may have to be exercise.

“What we are saying here is that this is consideration, so treat us fairly ,when it comes to our lease agreement” he stated.

The Group CEO continued that “This is the last option that we will pursue, but we needed to make it very ​clear to our shareholders that if required, we certainly would take those pathways in order to try and protect value”

Tarkwa Lease Renewal

Speaking to Journalists via Teleconference from South African, Mr. Fraser also disclosed that in July this year, the mining firm formally submitted a commercial proposal to the Government of Ghana on the renewal of the Tarkwa Mining leases.

This, Mr. Fraser says was coming after it submitted an initial request in November 2025 to the government.

Gold Fields says it is looking for a 25 years lease renewal of the Tarkwa mines as it targets fresh US$6 billion investment on deposits pegged at 7.4 million ounces.

The current mining lease for Tarkwa mines, expires in April 2027, and the Group CEO says an early decision on these issues will be appropriate.

The Government of Ghana on the other hand has maintained that it is open to discussions with Gold Fields, but has ruled out an automatic renewal of the lease.

Gold Fields said its proposal sought to boost local participation, expand community benefits and procurement opportunities, and increase the mine’s long-term economic contribution.

Gold Fields submitted a formal lease renewal application in November 2025 and is awaiting a government decision, it added.

The company said its financial strength, technical expertise and capacity to fund major reinvestment and mine-life-extension projects make it best placed to lead. Tarkwa through its next phase.

It added that continued operatorship would safeguard jobs, support local suppliers and sustain government revenues.

Tarkwa was Gold Fields' second-largest gold producer in the first half of 2026, behind Salares Norte in Chile, with its 192,000 ounces accounting for about 15% ​of the group's total output.

Xenophobic Attacks

The Group CEO admitted that recent developments in south Africa in terms of xenophobic attacks, has affected current discussions with government of Ghana.

But the Chief Executive,was quick to add that as a mining firm it has moved to condemn the attacks, through other association and business interest groups that it is currently a member.

“I want to describe it as unfortunate, when it comes these xenophobic attacks” Mr. Freser added.

Arbitration Hearing with E&P

On the arbitration hearing between Gold Fields and Engineers & Planners Company Limited, which an Accra High Court has ordered Gold Fields, to provide US$60 million bank guarantee, the Group Chief Executive, noted that it finds the ruling interesting and surprising.

He however says tha his outfit will study the ruling stating that “we believe that everything has been paid to E&P when it comes to serves rendered”.

An Accra High Court has ordered Abosso Goldfields Limited which many of us refer to as Gold Fields to provide a US$60 million bank guarantee to secure any eventual arbitral award that may be made in favour of Engineers & Planners Company Limited, in a significant ruling arising from a mining-services dispute whose underlying claim exceeds US$100 million.

The July 29, 2026 judgment, delivered by Justice Emmanuel Kofi Diaba of the High Court’s General Jurisdiction Court 5 in Accra, therefore turns on a simple question with major commercial consequences: what is an arbitration victory worth if, by the time it is obtained, there are insufficient assets against which to enforce it?

The dispute stems from a Mining Services Agreement between E&P and Goldf Fields in what is now known as the Damang Mine.

According to the court, the agreement was connected to a mining lease granted to Goldfields by the Government of Ghana.

That lease expired in April 2026 and was not renewed. E&P subsequently initiated arbitration proceedings at the Ghana Arbitration Centre against Gold Fields.

Before that arbitration could properly commence, however, E&P went to the High Court seeking security for any award that might ultimately be made in its favour. Its estimated arbitration claim is in excess of US$100 million.

Ghana News.title: High Court declines bid to adjourn Adu Boahene trial pending SC review on legal vacation ruling
Ghana News.content:
Adu Boahene

The Accra High Court has dismissed an application by former Signals Bureau Director-General Kwadwo Adu Boahene seeking to adjourn his trial pending the Supreme Court’s determination of a review application filed by Ofoase-Ayirebi MP Kojo Oppong Nkrumah over the continuation of selected criminal cases during the legal vacation.

Counsel for Mr Adu Boahene, Samuel Atta Akyea, had asked the court to adjourn the proceedings until September 2, when a three-member panel of the Supreme Court is expected to hear Mr Oppong Nkrumah’s review application.

He argued that the outcome of the application could have a bearing on the ongoing trial and that it was therefore appropriate for the High Court to await the Supreme Court’s decision.

However, Deputy Attorney-General and Minister for Justice Justice Srem-Sai opposed the application, pointing out that the prosecution had only one more day to close its case.

He argued that the Supreme Court had already determined the substantive interlocutory application concerning the legal vacation and that the mere filing of a review application did not automatically suspend proceedings.

Justice Francis Apanga Achibonga, after hearing arguments from both sides, said he had not identified any rule requiring the trial to be suspended in the circumstances.

The judge noted that although the earlier Supreme Court decision had been delivered by a single judge, it remained binding until it was set aside or reversed by a subsequent decision.

He therefore dismissed the defence’s request for an adjournment.

Adu Boahene trial

Mr Adu Boahene is standing trial alongside his wife, Angela Adjei Boateng, Mildred Donkor and Advantage Solutions Limited on 11 charges, including conspiracy, stealing, using public office for profit, money laundering and causing financial loss to the state.

All the accused persons have pleaded not guilty and are currently on bail.

The latest disagreement follows earlier disputes between the defence and prosecution over the pace and conduct of the trial.

In July 2025, the High Court rejected a defence application seeking further disclosure of National Security operational account records dating back to 1992.

The defence argued that the documents could contain information relevant to the accused persons’ case.

Following the ruling, Mr Atta Akyea sought time to study the decision and consider further legal options, including an appeal or an application for a stay of proceedings.

The prosecution opposed the request, insisting that the trial should proceed without unnecessary delays.

At the time, Mr Atta Akyea accused the prosecution of withholding documents and said: “I won’t accept any ambulance trial.”

He has maintained that his approach is intended to protect due process and ensure that his client receives a fair trial, arguing that the justice system should not create an accelerated track for selected cases while other matters continue under the ordinary rules.
