World.title: Your load shedding schedule might already be watching the Pacific Ocean
World.content:
A strengthening El Niño could add fresh strain on Eskom's reserve margin this summer, according to new reporting: Image ChatGPT

South Africa’s strengthening El Niño isn’t just a story about heat and drought anymore.

According to Cape Town Today, it could also put real pressure on Eskom’s already thin power reserves this summer.

Why hotter weather means more strain on the grid

As El Niño drives temperatures up over the 2026/27 summer, more households and businesses will likely lean harder on air conditioning and cooling, according to Cape Town Today.



The publication reports this could inflate national electricity demand by 8–10%.

That would shrink Eskom’s reserve margin to around 1 500 MW, a buffer that’s already stretched thin in normal years.

The bigger picture behind the numbers

This sits alongside a wider set of El Niño pressures already confirmed by multiple sources: the World Meteorological Organization’s forecast of a strong event developing through October, above-normal temperatures expected from August through December, and increased drought and veld fire risk across the summer rainfall regions.



Add rising electricity demand into that mix, and the strain compounds across water, food, and now power all at once.

Why this one’s worth watching closely

Unlike the heat or drought angles, this is the first sign that El Niño’s reach could extend all the way to your load shedding schedule, something that touches daily life more directly than a dry dam or a hot afternoon.

Hectic to think our lights could be caught in the crossfire of all this too. I’ll be keeping an eye on whether Eskom or other sources confirm these numbers as summer gets closer. I am not looking forward to this.



Do you think load shedding could make a comeback this summer because of El Niño, or is the grid in better shape than that?

Let us know in the comments below, Mzansi…

World.title: Here’s how the Springboks can regain the No 1 ranking on Saturday
World.content:
Seven days is a long time in rugby and the good news is that the Springboks can regain their No 1 World Rugby rankings spot on Saturday. Image: Charmaine Visser

The Springboks lost the first ‘Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry’ Test to the All Blacks at Ellis Park in Johannesburg last Saturday.

Their 33-16 defeat not only saw Rassie Erasmus’s men go 1-0 down in the four-Test series, it also saw them lose their No 1 World Rugby ranking to New Zealand.

EXCLUSIVE | Will Pieter-Steph du Toit break the Springbok centurion curse against the All Blacks?



However, seven days is a long time in rugby and the good news is that the Springboks can regain that coveted No 1 spot on Saturday in Cape Town.

How?

By beating the All Blacks – by any margin.

EXCLUSIVE | Springbok team to face All Blacks in Cape Town attended these SCHOOLS

What needs to be done?

Heading into the match at the Cape Town Stadium, the All Blacks have 94.03 points, with the Springboks 1.82 points adrift on 92.21.

A win by the Springboks by 15 points or fewer will give them 1.18 points (and see the All Blacks lose 1.18 points). That would be enough for South Africa to move back to No 1 in the world.



A win by 16 points or more by the Springboks would see them pick up 1.77 points (and see the All Blacks lose 1.77 points). That would open a sizeable gap between the two sides in the rankings.

A draw (by any score), would see South Africa gain 0.18 points (and see the All Blacks lose 0.18 points), but that wouldn’t be enough to alter the standings.

A win by New Zealand by 15 points or fewer will give them 0.82 points (and see the Springboks lose the equivalent number of points), retaining the No 1 spot for the Kiwis.

Back-to-back 16-point wins or more by the All Blacks would see them gain a further 1.23 points (and the Springboks lose 1.23 points).

But that’s not going to happen, right?

World.title: These Western Cape towns are attracting young families in search of a quieter life
World.content:
From mountain trails to vineyards and family-friendly communities, these Boland towns are attracting a new wave of property buyers. Image: canva

The idea of moving to the countryside is no longer just limited to retirees looking for a quieter pace of life.

Across the Boland towns of Robertson, McGregor and Montagu, a growing number of younger buyers and families are purchasing homes in search of space, nature and a slower lifestyle – without giving up access to everyday amenities.

The towns, all popular destinations along the Western Cape’s scenic Route 62 corridor, are increasingly attracting buyers who see them as more than holiday destinations.



According to property experts, the area’s combination of mountains, vineyards, agriculture and community life is proving attractive across generations.

Young families are joining the market

Property data has shown that Robertson, in particular, has become a hub for the wider Bonnievale, Ashton and Robertson (BAR) valley, as well as neighbouring Montagu and McGregor.

Situated along the Breede River and Route 62, Robertson is picturesque, surrounded by vineyards, mountains and open countryside. The area also offers hiking, mountain biking and horse trails, as well as numerous wine farms with restaurants and tasting rooms.



Data reveals that recent buyers are largely split between the 30-to-50 and 55-to-70 age groups, with fewer younger singles entering the market.

In Robertson, freestanding homes range from around R1.6 million to R5.5 million, while sectional-title units range from R1.5 million to R3 million. Estate homes generally cost between R2.5 million and R7 million.

While lifestyle estates remain particularly popular with retirees, younger families are increasingly buying older homes closer to schools and renovating them.



Winelands in Robertson, Western Cape. Image: canva

Aerial view over McGregor, Western Cape. Image: canva

Church in Montagu, Western Cape. Image: canva

Property prices are climbing in these Western Cape towns

And the growing demand is reflected in prices.

In Montagu, data shows the median property price increased from R1.6 million in 2021 to R2.65 million in 2026 – a rise of 65.6%.

McGregor has seen an even bigger jump, with prices increasing from just under R1 million in 2019 to around R2.9 million in 2026, an increase of roughly 113%.



Vacant land prices have also risen in both towns.

Robertson is also seeing more development as demand increases. Just over 10% of homes in the town are currently situated in estates, but this is expected to grow.

The new Western Cape lifestyle destination?

For buyers priced out of some of the Western Cape’s better-known lifestyle towns, Robertson, McGregor and Montagu are becoming increasingly attractive alternatives.



They offer vineyards, mountains, outdoor activities and a strong sense of community, while property prices remain comparatively lower than in many other parts of the province.

For young families in particular, the attraction may be less about escaping to the countryside and more about finding a place where space, schools, nature and community can all fit into the same address.

World.title: Who are Maswanganyi’s new club Al Khaldiya?
World.content:
Patrick Maswanganyi has moved to Al Khaldiya in Bahrain. Image: @orlandopirates/X

Orlando Pirates officially announced the transfer of Patrick “Tito” Maswanganyi to Bahrain-based outfit Al Khaldiya on Monday.

Bahrain is a small Asian country found between Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, and it not as big when it comes to football.

However, the league itself have some competitive clubs, and Al Khaldiya is one of them despite being a relatively new club.



Also read: Orlando Pirates star Maswanganyi moves overseas

WHO ARE MASWANGANYI’S NEW CLUB AND BAHRAIN AL KHALDIYA?

Al Khaldiya were formed on 27 October 2020, and they are nicknamed the Lions of Bahrain.

They played in the second division of Bahrain’s football for a season before winning promotion to the top flight.



Al Khaldiya won the Bahraini Premier League for the first time in history in 2023, and this was just three years after their formation.

They successfully defended their league crown during the 2023-24 season following some impressive runs in between.

Maswanganyi’s new club then finished season at the end of the 2024–25 campaign.



To date, Al Khaldiya already boast two league titles, four Super Cup titles and two King’s Cup titles.

And that is an impressive record given that they are just a team that has only been existing for six years.

Also read: Molefi Ntseki could return as Bafana Bafana coach… for now



WAS THIS THE BEST MOVE?

Let us know in the comment section…

World.title: Who was Zolani Tete? Inside the SA boxer’s remarkable career
World.content:
Zolani Tete was shot dead outside his home. Image via Facebook: Zolani Tete Official

The late Zolani “Last Born” Tete was shot dead outside his home in Mdantsane on Friday, 21 August.

He was one of South Africa’s most accomplished boxers, celebrated for his power, precision, and resilience in the ring.

ZOLANI TETE SHOT DEAD OUTSIDE HIS HOME

South Africans were left in shock and heartbreak following the killing of former two-division boxing world champion Zolani Tete.



As previously reported by The South African, Eastern Cape police have arrested three more suspects in connection with the killing of former two-division boxing world champion Zolani Tete, bringing the total number of people in police custody to four.

WHO WAS ZOLANI TETE?

Zolani was born on 8 March 1988 in Mdantsane, Eastern Cape, a township famous for producing boxing talent.

He began his training at the age of eight and went on to enjoy an extraordinary amateur career with more than 400 fights, losing only three.



He turned professional in 2006 and quickly rose through the ranks, becoming a two-weight world champion.

Tete first captured the IBF junior-bantamweight title in 2014, defeating Teiru Kinoshita in Japan and defending it successfully against Britain’s Paul Butler.

He later moved up to bantamweight, where he won the WBO title in 2017, initially as interim champion against Arthur Villanueva before being elevated to full champion.



His most iconic moment came in Belfast in November 2017, when he knocked out fellow South African Siboniso Gonya in just 11 seconds, setting a Guinness World Record for the fastest knockout in a world title fight.

Over his professional career, he fought 34 times, winning 29 bouts, 22 of them by knockout.

CAREER SETBACKS

Despite his success, Tete’s career faced setbacks. In 2022, he tested positive for the banned substance stanozolol after a victory in London, leading to a four-year suspension.



He denied deliberately using performance-enhancing drugs and was preparing for a comeback when his suspension ended in July 2026.

Tete was also admired for his humility and devotion to family. The boxer famously used his earnings to buy a prosthetic leg for his mother, fulfilling a promise he had made as a child.

He remained deeply connected to Mdantsane, inspiring young fighters in a community with a proud boxing tradition.



Tete is an icon and his legacy spreads further than his titles and record-breaking knockout but also in his role as a symbol of resilience and pride for South African boxing.

His journey from Mdantsane’s gyms to the world stage ensured his place among the country’s greatest fighters, and his memory continues to inspire future generations.

World.title: A passion for sports cars: How Matlala and Maumela's friendship blossomed
World.content:
PRETORIA - Alleged underworld figure Vusimuzi “Cat” Matlala has detailed his relationship with Hangwani Maumela, a central figure in the alleged looting of Tembisa Hospital.

Matlala told the Madlanga Commission that their shared passion for luxury sports cars brought them together in 2015 or 2016.

“We both have a passion for sports cars,” he told the Madlanga Commission.

“There is a restaurant in Sandton that we both frequented. We used to meet each other there. I liked his car, and that’s how we started our relationship.”

He conceded that he and Maumela were friends and said they later entered a joint business venture, pooling funds and sharing profits from government tenders they secured.

Asked by evidence leader Advocate Sello Mahlape SC whether they had any other relationship that allowed them to benefit financially, Matlala said they did.

He told the commission that they were involved in a joint business venture in which they invested money and shared profits from government tenders they successfully secured.

Matlala did not list the projects they had secured, saying there were many.

World.title: Customary marriage registration deadline fast approaching
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Couples married in terms of customary law who have not yet registered their marriages have until 31 August to do so.

Under the Recognition of Customary Marriages Act, customary marriages have the same legal recognition and protection as civil marriages.

Couples whose marriages were concluded before 2000, as well as those married after 2000, are required to register them.

Sanlam Trust’s Adv Sankie Morata says registration is important when it comes to proving the existence of a marriage during a life-changing event.

"In the past it has become difficult to prove the existence of a particular marriage in a death or divorce," he said.

Morata says couples who have not yet registered their marriage should visit their nearest Home Affairs office.

Who must register?

World.title: LIVESTREAM | 'Cat' Matlala back for more grilling
World.content:
PRETORIA - Alleged underworld figure Vusimuzi "Cat" Matlala returns to the stand at the Madlanga Commission on Tuesday.

Matlala resumed his testimony on Monday after proceedings were delayed by his legal team.

READ | Matlala denies close ties with other cartel suspects

During his testimony, the tender don denied having a close relationship with suspended deputy police commissioner General Shadrack Sibiya.

He told the Commission that Sibiya was not his friend, but simply “someone that I knew”.

He also insisted that he had no personal or professional relationship with alleged Big 5 Cartel member Ignatius Mothakathi.

World.title: WATCH: Ramaphosa delivers keynote address at SIDSSA 2026
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - President Cyril Ramaphosa will deliver a keynote address at the Infrastructure Symposium.

Delegates are meeting in Cape Town to find ways of accelerating investment and improve delivery across the continent.

The gathering has brought together government, business and investors to unlock infrastructure funding for major projects.

World.title: Six months into Iran war, Hormuz traffic way down, sailors stranded
World.content:
LONDON - Six months since the start of the Middle East war, the strategic Strait of Hormuz remains largely paralysed, with thousands of sailors still stranded in the Gulf and commodity carrier traffic way below its normal level.

- Only a few transits per day -

Before Iran blocked the strait in response to joint US-Israeli strikes in February, around one fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas exports passed through the waterway.

Iran's Guards have also warned of a "danger zone" covering 1,400 square kilometres where mines may be present.

World.title: Trump veers from boredom to denial after six months of Iran war
World.content:
WASHINGTON - At an impromptu press conference last week, US President Donald Trump waxed lyrical about his helipad, his ballroom and his granite paving stones.

The one thing he barely mentioned? The Iran war.

Six months after launching what he expected to be a lightning offensive, Trump appears bored or even in denial about the conflict as it puts a drag on his second presidency.

"Right now, the situation is so good," Trump replied when asked about Iran, after leading reporters on a tour of the White House's South Lawn to show off his latest renovations.

During the 36-minute event, Trump used the word "granite" 13 times and the word "Iran" just three.

But the war, in which at least 18 US service members have died and more than 750 were wounded, according to Pentagon figures, has become a millstone around Trump's neck. Thousands more have died in Iran and Lebanon.

US voters are angry about the war's knock-on effect on the cost of living and crucial midterm elections are around the corner.

Even his MAGA fans are questioning why the man who vowed to start no new foreign wars has got America into another quagmire with no apparent plan to get out of it.

"Is there a rabbit in the hat? No, I think the hat is empty," William Galston, senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, told AFP.

- 'Very boring' -

World.title: Cool Japan: Human fridge chills workers in extreme heat
World.content:
TOKYO - Feeling dizzy and unwell after cycling to work in Japan's punishing summer heat, warehouse worker Isao Tabuchi headed for his company's newest acquisition: a refrigerator for humans.

The phonebooth-sized machine, where jets of chilled air ensure ice-cold comfort, only launched this year but has proved popular in a country that seems to be getting inexorably warmer.

"I was really able to recover thanks to that. Once you use it, it's very, very cool," Tabuchi, 51, told AFP in the western industrial city of Higashiosaka.

Tokyo-based industrial equipment distributor Trusco Nakayama said it has sold more than 300 units of the "Do Hiemon Box" since April, priced at 1.5 million yen ($9,400).

Customers include construction sites, factories and warehouses, and will expand in the future to golf courses, said company sales agent China Yamamoto. Baseball stadiums may also be interested.

Some within the company had been sceptical, she added.

"It's large, it's expensive, and it's not the kind of product where you can just explain it in words and have customers say, 'Okay, let's buy one.' So there were a lot of uncertainties," she told AFP.

- 'Cruelly hot' -

Scientists say human-induced climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme heat events around the world.

In 2025, Japan saw its hottest summer on record.

This year, the weather office began using a new word -- "kokushobi" or "cruelly hot day" -- when temperatures hit 40C (104F), urging the public to treat extreme heat like a natural disaster.

World.title: Federer looks forward to brief return to Arthur Ashe stadium
World.content:
NEW YORK - Roger Federer said he is looking forward to this week's celebratory return to Arthur Ashe Stadium to play for the first time since his final US Open in 2019.

The exhibition Tuesday night during "fan week" ahead of Sunday's start of the tournament features doubles with former rivals Andy Roddick and Andre Agassi, along with John McEnroe, another giant of the sport.

The group collectively has won a dozen mens' singles titles at the US Open.

"It really gives me a true opportunity to say thank you," Federer said at a news conference Monday previewing the match and his upcoming induction to the International Tennis Hall of Fame later this week in Newport.

New York fans of Federer were deprived of a true sendoff for the 20-time Grand Slam champion as marked by Agassi, Serena Williams and some other champions.

When Federer lost in the 2019 quarterfinals to Grigor Dimitrov of Bulgaria, he had planned to keep playing. And while he did continue to compete, injuries prevented participation in the US Open in either 2020 or 2021 ahead of his last match at the Laver Cup in September 2022.

While Federer has played some other exhibitions since retiring, he said Monday that the time had only seemed to fall into place for a New York match this year ahead of the Newport ceremony.

"The kids are getting older," he said of his four children, two sets of twins now 12 and 17. "So they can also maybe enjoy a little bit seeing, their dad play."

Federer expects a "respectful" match with a not-too-intense level of competition.

"We're not playing best of five," he said "I hope it's going to be a lot of fun for us and the same for the fans to just see us back out playing."

But Federer quickly shot down any questions about a tennis comeback, saying "no" at least nine times to a question on whether he was interested in a wildcard.

"There's just way too many obstacles, and I'm too busy," he said. "All good and just just a fan now, just enjoying watching."

World.title: Masengeli: Police to flag 'unfit' aspirants ahead of 2027 elections
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Deputy Inspector General of Police Eliud Masengeli. [File, Standard]

The National Police Service will recommend to the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) individuals it considers unfit to run for elective office based on their track records, Deputy Inspector General of Police Eliud Masengeli has said.

Masengeli said the police would use their surveillance and security mandate to identify individuals whose conduct could pose a threat to peaceful elections.

“We will recommend to IEBC individuals who are not fit to run for office based on their track records,” Masengeli said.

He said police would also step up surveillance, crime prevention and arrests targeting individuals involved in politically instigated violence.

“We will deal with goons and their sponsors,” he said.

The Deputy IG was speaking on Tuesday, August 25, during the launch of the National Cohesion and Integration Commission’s (NCIC) Roadmap to a Violence-Free 2027 General Elections.

His remarks come as Kenya prepares for the August 10, 2027 General Election, with the IEBC having activated the Electoral Code of Conduct and the Election Offences Act for the election period.

The NCIC roadmap seeks to strengthen early warning and response mechanisms, address conflict triggers, counter hate speech and disinformation, and promote dialogue ahead of the polls.

The commission has raised concerns over growing political intolerance, hate speech, ethnic contempt, disinformation and divisive rhetoric as the country moves closer to the 2027 elections.

The focus on political violence comes amid renewed concern over the use of organised groups during political campaigns. The IEBC has identified political goonism among the threats to peaceful elections.

NCIC Chairman Bishop Kepha Nyamweya said the roadmap was designed to ensure violence prevention begins early, rather than after political tensions have already escalated

"As the National Cohesion and Integration Commission, we reaffirm our commitment to working with all stakeholders to promote national unity, peaceful coexistence and social cohesion throughout the electoral cycle. We will continue to strengthen our efforts in monitoring and responding to hate speech and ethnic contempt, facilitating dialogue, supporting peace structures and promoting responsible leadership and citizenship," said Nyamweya.

"Every leader must choose responsible speech over inflammatory rhetoric. Every political party must place the interests of the country above vested political interests. Every citizen must reject incitement, violence and manipulation."

World.title: Relief for schools as government releases Sh18.5b capitation
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Education CS Julius Ogamba. [File, Standard]

The government has released Sh18.5 billion in capitation to support operations in public basic education institutions during the third term of 2026, as schools reopened across the country on Monday.

Education Cabinet Secretary Julius Ogamba said the funds have already been released and will support learners in pre-primary, primary, junior and senior schools.

The allocation is intended to facilitate smooth school operations and ensure learning activities continue without disruption.

The Sh18.5 billion has been distributed across three major capitation programmes, with Free Day Secondary Education (FDSE) allocated Sh10.963 billion, accounting for the biggest portion of the Term Three capitation.

The money will support operations in public day and secondary schools and comes as institutions prepare learners for a busy academic term.

Free Day Junior School Education has received Sh6.1 billion, to support learners in the second tier of basic education and help institutions meet operational requirements as the Competency-Based Education system continues to expand.

Meanwhile, Free Primary Education has been allocated Sh1.4 billion to support learning in public primary schools.

The funds come as a relief to school heads who had raised concerns on the insufficient funds disbursed to schools this year.

However, Ogamba said the disbursement demonstrates the Government's commitment to ensuring that learners have access to free and compulsory basic education as provided for under Article 53(1)(b) of the Constitution.

“The Government affirms its commitment to fulfil its duty to learners and educational institutions,” said the CS.

Ogamba also warned school heads and principals against misuse of the funds, directing them to ensure the money is spent prudently and for the benefit of learners.

School administrators have further been cautioned against imposing unauthorised levies on parents and learners.

Ogamba said the Ministry would take firm action against institutions found to have misappropriated public resources or imposed illegal charges.

“We will deal firmly with any verified cases of misappropriation of resources and the imposition of unauthorised levies,” he said.

The warning comes as schools reopen for the third term, a period that is expected to be particularly demanding for institutions and learners because of the academic activities and assessments scheduled for the school calendar.

The Ministry has maintained that capitation is meant to ease the financial burden on families and enable schools to provide essential services without passing prohibited costs to parents.

Ogamba reiterated that school administrators must remain accountable for the public funds entrusted to them, warning that verified cases of misuse will attract action from the Ministry.

The Government has also reaffirmed that every child is entitled to free and compulsory basic education, placing the responsibility on education officials and school managers to ensure capitation achieves its intended purpose.

World.title: Ndindi Nyoro begins nationwide political mobilisation ahead of 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro after attending service at Gathuki-ini ACK Church on August 23, 2026. [Boniface Gikandi, Standard]

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro has said he will take his campaign for national transformation across Kenya as he positions himself for the 2027 presidential race.

Ndindi said he was interested in leadership committed to addressing concerns in education, health, youth and unemployment, among other needs.

Nyoro, who is the People’s Party of Kenya leader, spoke at St Michael Gathuki-ini ACK Church in Kiharu on Sunday, where he called for respect and political maturity.

Addressing residents in Kiria-ini (Mathioya) and Gakira (Kangema), he urged politicians to engage in a responsible manner.

“I trust in God that after next year Kenya will be able to have leadership that will be responsible for improving citizens' standards of living,” he said.

He regretted that hundreds of university graduates in the area were yet to secure employment.

“I plead with Kenyans to support my course that is geared to transform the nation and ensure equality and transparency,” said the PPK leader.

Nyoro said that after engaging Murang'a residents, he will take his transformation campaigns to all parts of the country.

Speaking at Kiria-ini market, he said he would engage the people to seek their blessings.

“All along had been feeling the urge to lead the country, thus the need to come out in the open and fight for position,” he said.

On Monday, the MP announced his exit from the ruling United Democratic Alliance (UDA), declaring that he will join the opposition ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Nyoro, an economist serving his second term as Kiharu MP, said he will work with opposition leaders to push for what he termed real change in Kenya.

The legislator said all opposition presidential aspirants are welcome at rallies organised by the PPK.

His move marks a significant political shift as parties and leaders begin positioning themselves ahead of the 2027 polls.

World.title: City Hall in rush to expand drainage system ahead of El Nino
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja during an inspection tour of the ongoing drainage system expansion. [GPS]

Nairobi County has embarked on drainage expansion works aimed at mitigating floodwaters ahead of El Nino rains.

Governor Johnson Sakaja, while calling on city residents to remain alert and proactive, said City Hall has intensified preparations and accelerated identification of hotspots.

The governor on Friday said his administration is taking early and coordinated action to minimise the impact of heavy rains, urging residents to stay calm, pay attention to official information and follow guidance from the multi-agency team established to coordinate the city’s preparedness and emergency response.

“We are working proactively to address the challenges of flooding before El Nino hits the ground. We urge our people not to panic but to be alert and get information from our multi-agency team,” said Sakaja.

The Governor spoke during an inspection tour of several flood-prone areas in Nairobi, including the Mombasa Road-Bunyala Junction corridor and Globe Roundabout, which experienced significant flooding during previous heavy rains.

Sakaja said drainage works are already underway in the affected areas, with teams working to open up and deepen drainage channels, clear obstructions, and improve storm-water flow to prevent a repeat of the flooding witnessed previously.

His remarks come as weatherman warned of increased rainfall in the coming months, with Nairobi among the urban areas requiring heightened preparedness because of its exposure to flooding and the impact of heavy rainfall on roads, settlements and other critical infrastructure.

Sakaja said the county has so far brought together the disaster management teams, Kenya Red Cross, Kenya Urban Roads Authority (KURA) and Kenya National Highways Authority (KeNHA) under a coordinated programme worth Sh2.4 billion to strengthen Nairobi’s flood resilience.

Of the amount, Sh2 billion has been set aside for drainage and flood-mitigation works targeting 19 roads in flood-prone areas.

The projects are at an advanced stage, with tenders awarded and contractors expected to commence implementation after completion of the necessary processes.

Sakaja reiterated that the programme will complement ongoing county interventions under the Nairobi Regeneration Programme, which includes the rehabilitation and upgrading of critical infrastructure across the city.

“The Sh2 billion will support a comprehensive drainage overhaul that complements the ongoing Nairobi Regeneration Programme. Our goal is to permanently address the flooding challenges that have affected the city for many years,” Sakaja said.

He said the focus is not only on responding to floods after they occur, but on addressing the infrastructure weaknesses that have historically made Nairobi vulnerable to flooding.

To strengthen preparedness, the county has established five specialised sub-committees under the multi-agency framework.

The committees include Infrastructure and Drainage; Emergency Response and Evacuation; Shelter and Relief; Security and Traffic and Communication.

While the Infrastructure and Drainage committee will coordinate the clearing and improvement of drainage systems, rivers and other critical infrastructure, the Emergency Response and Evacuation committee will oversee rapid response, rescue and evacuation operations whenever emergencies occur.

The Shelter and Relief committee will prepare safe shelters and coordinate the provision of food, water, medical assistance and other essential support to affected residents.

The Security and Traffic committee will coordinate security, traffic management and emergency access, while the Communication committee will strengthen early-warning systems, public alerts and timely dissemination of information.

Sakaja said the county is also mobilising personnel, equipment and other resources to clear blocked drains, remove silt and waste and strengthen emergency response systems in areas identified as vulnerable.

He urged residents and their associations, businesses and other stakeholders to play an active role in flood preparedness by keeping drainage areas clear and paying attention to official warnings.

The county chief said residents in high-risk areas will be provided with timely information on emerging weather conditions and the actions they should take when heavy rains occur.

“We don’t want people to panic. We want people to be proactive, to listen to information and to work with us. The multi-agency team is in place, and we are preparing before the rains intensify,” Sakaja said.

According to him, the multi-agency approach will also help eliminate jurisdictional gaps by bringing together national and county agencies to operate as one coordinated team.

He said the combination of drainage upgrades, emergency preparedness, early-warning systems and coordinated response would strengthen Nairobi’s resilience and reduce disruption caused by heavy rains.

The multi-agency team is expected to meet next week to review progress, coordinate ongoing works and further push the city’s El Niño preparedness agenda.

World.title: Public officers eyeing elective posts to resign by February 10 - IEBC
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon addressing the press at a past press conference. [File, Standard]

Public officers seeking to contest elective positions in the 2027 General Election have until February 10, 2027, to resign from office, the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) has announced.

IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon said the deadline falls exactly six months before the August 10, 2027, General Election, which the Commission has confirmed will be held on a Tuesday.

“Any public officer who intends to contest in this election must resign from public office by Wednesday, 10th February 2027, which is exactly six months before the election,” Ethekon said.

The IEBC said adherence to the timelines will be non-negotiable, noting that they are legally binding and essential to ensuring an orderly electoral process.

Under the timetable, political parties must submit their membership lists and details of candidates participating in party primaries by March 16, 2027.

Party primaries and any related disputes must be concluded by May 8, while independent candidates are also required to meet their legal obligations by the same date.

Presidential aspirants will have until May 24 to submit lists of supporting voters drawn from a majority of Kenya’s counties.

Candidate registration will begin on May 29, with specific deadlines applying to the various elective positions.

The official campaign period will commence after candidates are registered, but not earlier than May 29, 2027.

Ethekon warned political parties, candidates and their supporters against breaching the prescribed campaign period, saying any electioneering outside the legal window will be unlawful.

The restrictions cover campaign posters, billboards, political caravans and other forms of campaigning.

Campaigning will close on August 7, 2027, 48 hours before Kenyans head to the polls.

“The law prescribes when election campaigns may commence,” Ethekon said, urging political parties, candidates and their supporters to strictly comply with electoral laws and regulations.

The deadline is among key milestones unveiled by the electoral commission as political parties, aspirants and other stakeholders begin preparations for the next General Election.

World.title: Schools will open on August 24 as scheduled, Ogamba says
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Students heading home during recent demonstrations. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The Ministry of Education said the official academic calendar remains unchanged.

In a statement issued on Wednesday, August 19, Education Cabinet Secretary Julius Ogamba insists that learners will return to school on Monday, August 24, 2026.

The CS has dismissed reports circulating on social media claiming that the reopening of schools for the third term has been postponed, warning parents, teachers, learners and education stakeholders against relying on unauthorised online notices.

“We wish to clarify that the academic calendar for Basic Education institutions and Teacher Training Colleges remains unchanged,” the CS said.

The clarification comes two days before the scheduled reopening of schools, amid reports circulating on social media platforms suggesting that the government had pushed back the start of Term III.

"Our attention has been drawn to misleading information circulating on various social media platforms, purporting that the academic calendar for basic education institutions and Teachers Training Colleges has been changed," he stated.

The Ministry termed the reports “FALSE” and urged members of the public to completely disregard them.

Ogamba said the Ministry had directed Regional Directors of Education, County Directors of Education and Sub-County Directors of Education to ensure strict compliance with the approved academic calendar contained in a circular dated October 9, 2025.

According to the Ministry, pre-primary, primary, junior, senior and secondary schools will begin Term III on Monday, August 24. The term will run for nine weeks and end on October 23, 2026.

The reopening marks the final academic term of the school year, with schools expected to implement the approved programmes as they prepare learners for the end-of-year national assessments and examinations.

Diploma Teachers Training Colleges will also resume academic operations on August 24, with their third term scheduled to conclude on November 6, 2026.

The Ministry further confirmed that the national assessment and examination calendar has not been altered for KPSEA, KILEA, KJSEA, KPLEA and KCSE are scheduled to begin from October 26, 2026, as earlier announced.

The Ministry also reminded schools that extracurricular activities and visits to secondary schools will remain banned during Term III.

The latest clarification is part of efforts by the government to prevent confusion among parents, learners and teachers as schools prepare to reopen.

Ogamba urged education stakeholders to obtain information through official Ministry communication channels, rather than social media posts whose authenticity cannot be established.

“Parents, teachers and learners and members of the public are advised to strictly rely on the Ministry's official communication channels and field officers for accurate information," he said.

World.title: Ruto denies Sh104bn SHA technology contract
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto has dismissed claims that the government entered into a controversial Sh104 billion contract with Safaricom and Apeiro Limited for the Social Health Authority (SHA) technology system.

Speaking on Tuesday evening at the Presidential Townhall held during the National Health Summit at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC) in Nairobi, Ruto defended the government's investment in digital health, saying the technology was designed to improve transparency and accountability in the management of SHA services.

“There is no Sh104 billion contract. What we have done is design a digital system to make sure that everything is visible. Every treatment must be traceable, and every payment must be accounted for,” Ruto said.

He explained that the government had not purchased the technology outright but had engaged investors who own the equipment, with the State paying for the services provided.

His remarks were echoed by Digital Health Agency Chief Executive Anthony Lenaiyara, who rejected claims that SHA had committed Sh104 billion to technology upgrades.

“It is not correct or true that SHA has undertaken any upgrade or invested Sh104 billion in technology upgrades. What we did is build a digital superhighway comprising 43 systems to support Universal Health Coverage,” Lenaiyara said.

Lenaiyara said the technology infrastructure had been rolled out without requiring health facilities to purchase the devices, adding that the system had transformed the processing and accountability of SHA claims.

He contrasted the new system with the former National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF) model, where claims were processed using physical files that moved between different offices for verification and approval.

Ruto also addressed other government programmes, saying the State had mobilised resources to construct 23,000 additional classrooms to ease pressure caused by shortages of learning spaces.

World.title: 'That was not healthcare, it was theft'- Ruto on old health system
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during the official opening of the Kenya Health Summit at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC), Nairobi, August 18,2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has accused the defunct National Health Insurance Fund (NHIF) system of enabling theft from sick Kenyans, citing claims for procedures that never happened.

Speaking on Tuesday, August 18, at the opening of the Kenya Health Summit at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC) in Nairobi, Ruto described the old system as opaque and vulnerable to abuse.

"We heard of claims for procedures that never happened, fictitious patients and inflated bills. That was not healthcare, it was theft, and theft from sick Kenyans," said Ruto.

He called digital health systems the backbone holding the reforms together and said they would close loopholes that let people profit from the system's weaknesses.

Ruto ranked Universal Health Coverage (UHC) alongside the Affordable Housing Programme as one of the government's most consequential social transformation efforts, crediting collaboration between national and county governments for changes in how healthcare is financed, delivered and accounted for.

The two-day summit, themed "Reforms Delivered, Health as a Right," has drawn more than 5,000 delegates to audit progress under the Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda (BETA) and set priorities for the remainder of Ruto's term, according to Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale.

Ruto said 32.3 million Kenyans are now registered with the Social Health Authority (SHA), which replaced NHIF in October 2024.

Eight million have received treatment, more than 1.2 million mothers have been supported to deliver safely and more than 500,000 surgical procedures have been supported, he added.

He put Kenyans' previous annual out-of-pocket health spending at Sh150 billion ($1.16 billion), saying families had borrowed, sold assets or organised harambees to cover medical costs before the reforms.

"Millions paid out of pocket, borrowed, sold assets, organised harambees or stayed away from hospital because they could not afford care," said Ruto.

Since October 2024, SHA has received more than Sh209 billion ($1.62 billion) and paid more than Sh178 billion ($1.38 billion) to contracted facilities across all 47 counties, Ruto added.

He credited 107,800 Community Health Promoters, deployed under a shared financing arrangement between national and county governments, with reaching more than nine million households and referring over 750,000 people for further treatment.

On supply chains, Ruto said the Kenya Medical Supplies Authority's (KEMSA) fill rate had risen from about 40 per cent to 91 per cent, helped by a Sh1.5 billion ($11.6 million) recapitalisation and a Sh10 billion ($77.4 million) credit line.

The reforms rest on four laws Ruto signed on 19 October 2023: the Primary Health Care Act, the Social Health Insurance Act, the Digital Health Act and the Facilities Improvement Financing Act.

Ruto acknowledged gaps remained in registration, benefit clarity, claims processing and digital systems.

"The ultimate measure of reform is not the laws we pass or the numbers we register, but the experience of the patient in terms of dependable, affordable and dignified care," said Ruto.

Deputy President Kithure Kindiki, Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi, National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula, Duale and Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja attended the opening session, alongside county governors, principal secretaries, members of Parliament and development partners.

The summit runs through Wednesday.

World.title: PM follows up with CBE governor on joint coordination efforts in several economic files
World.content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly affirmed full coordination between the government and the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) as part of preparations for the National Economic Transformation Program, based on an integrated vision reflecting the state’s economic priorities for the coming period.

This is being carried out in implementation of President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s directives and aims to ensure the integration of economic, fiscal, monetary, and sectoral policies and measures, while achieving a tangible impact on the national economy.

Madbouly made the remarks during a meeting on Monday, August 24, 2026, with CBE Governor Hassan Abdalla at the government headquarters in New Alamein City.

The meeting was held as part of regular coordination between the government and CBE to follow up on priority economic issues and discuss mechanisms for strengthening financial and monetary stability.

The meeting reviewed several issues related to the performance of the Egyptian economy during the current period, including coordination efforts to continue reducing inflation rates, efforts to increase dollar inflows, indicators related to strengthening the state’s foreign currency reserves, and economic and structural reforms.

The meeting also confirmed that Egypt has safe levels of foreign currency reserves capable of securing the country’s strategic needs for essential commodities.

Continuous efforts are being made to strengthen strategic stocks of various commodities through ongoing coordination between the government and the Central Bank in this regard.

For his part, Abdalla said that the CBE Board of Directors had approved the regulations governing services under the Digital Financial Identity System, which enables banks to identify customers and electronically verify their identities.

The move comes as part of the bank’s ongoing efforts to support digital transformation and promote financial inclusion, in line with the Egyptian state’s vision of transitioning to digital financial services.

He explained that the regulations establish an integrated regulatory framework for services under the Digital Financial Identity System, covering governance of the system and defining the roles and responsibilities of all participating parties, as well as technical and operational requirements, data protection controls, and cybersecurity measures.

This is intended to ensure that services are delivered according to the highest standards of security and efficiency and in line with international best practices.

World.title: Egypt, Mongolia discuss cooperation in water resources management
World.content:
Minister of Irrigation and Water Resources Hani Sewilam discussed with Mongolian Minister of Food, Agriculture and Light Industry Tsagaankhuugiin Iderbat ways to enhance cooperation and exchange expertise in water resources management, amid growing challenges facing the water and agriculture sectors and the importance of sound water resources management in supporting food security and sustainable development.

The meeting was held on the sidelines of Sewilam’s participation in the 17th session of the Conference of the Parties to the UN Convention to Combat Desertification (COP17) in Mongolia.

Sewilam outlined the Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation’s vision for implementing the second generation of Egypt’s water management system (2.0), which seeks to develop water management through integrating engineering and technological solutions, improving water-use efficiency and expanding reliance on modern technologies in managing water resources.

The two sides also underscored the importance of maximizing the return on each unit of water and improving water-use efficiency, particularly in agriculture.

World.title: Egypt overtakes Spain, France, Croatia, Serbia in Taranto 2026 medal standings
World.content:
Egyptian teams competing at the Mediterranean Games in Taranto continued their strong performances, winning medals and propelling Egypt past Spain, France, Croatia and Serbia in the overall medal standings.

In sport, some athletes compete simply to make up the numbers, while others seek to leave their mark in the history books.

In Taranto, Egypt is not merely competing for numbers, it is showcasing a new philosophy: what matters is not how many athletes a delegation brings, but how many champions can carry their country’s flag to the podium.

This has been the story of Egypt at the Mediterranean Games, where the Pharaohs have climbed to fifth place in the medal table with 13 medals, surpassing major sporting powers including Spain, France, Croatia and Serbia.

Egypt has also maintained its position at the top of the Arab medal standings, five medals ahead of Tunisia.

Perhaps the most significant figure, however, is not the 13 medals but the number that preceded it: 196. That is the number of Egyptian athletes competing at the Games, compared with much larger delegations numbering more than 300 or even 400 athletes.

Italy has 498 athletes, Turkey 334, France 330, Greece 281, Algeria 268 and Spain 249.

So far, Egypt’s medals have come from three main sports, swimming, fencing and wrestling, highlighting the depth and diversity of Egyptian sport and its ability to produce champions across multiple disciplines.

Behind this performance is close coordination among Olympic champion and Minister of Youth and Sports Gohar Nabil, Egyptian Olympic Committee President Yasser Idris, and the national sports federations, based on a simple but challenging principle: Egypt does not need the largest delegation; it needs the strongest delegation.

Minister Gohar Nabil was keen to be present alongside the athletes, providing support and encouragement during his attendance at the opening ceremony.

Meanwhile, Yasser Idris overcame his grief following the death of his mother, which coincided with the start of the competitions and caused him to arrive in Italy later than planned, in order to support the Egyptian delegation and follow its performances.

Egypt’s 13 medals have placed the country firmly among the leading nations and kept it at the top of the Arab standings, with four gold, four silver and five bronze medals, as follows:

Swimming

Gold: Abdelrahman Sameh — 50m butterfly

Bronze: Farida Osman — 50m butterfly

Bronze: Youssef Ramadan — 100m butterfly

Fencing

Gold: Mohamed al-Sayed — épée

Gold: Mohamed Hamza — foil

Silver: Sara Hosny — foil

Silver: Youssef Shamel — épée

Bronze: Abdelrahman Tolba — foil

Wrestling

Gold: Mohamed Hassan — 67kg

Silver: Mahmoud Farag — 60kg

Silver: Abdelrahman Haitham — 125kg

Bronze: Mostafa Hussein — 77kg

Bronze: Shehab al-Din Abdel-Raouf — 65kg

World.title: Irrigation minister: Egypt pursuing an integrated approach to maximize efficient use of available water resources
World.content:
Minister of Water Resources and Irrigation Hani Sewilam affirmed that Egypt is pursuing an integrated approach to maximize the efficient use of its available water resources by improving water-use efficiency, expanding the reuse of agricultural drainage water and optimizing the use of every drop of water, particularly in light of the country’s limited water resources and growing demand.

Sewilam made the remarks during a lecture titled “Innovations in Water Resources Management,” delivered on the sidelines of his participation in the 17th Session of the Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (COP17), being held in Mongolia.

During the lecture, the minister outlined the main features of Egypt’s water resources system and reviewed the country’s water resources and needs, as well as measures being implemented to strengthen water security and ensure sustainable management of available resources.

Sewilam also highlighted Egypt’s efforts to deepen cooperation with Nile Basin countries and other African nations, stressing that Egypt attaches great importance to regional cooperation as a means of advancing sustainable development and promoting the exchange of expertise and knowledge in water resources management, in a manner that serves the common interests of African peoples.

The minister outlined the main pillars of the second generation of Egypt’s water management system (Water 2.0), with a particular focus on rehabilitating and upgrading water infrastructure and deploying advanced technologies to enhance the management and operation of the water system.

He noted that the ministry is expanding the use of satellite imagery and unmanned aerial vehicles (drones) for monitoring and surveillance, enabling the collection of accurate, real-time data and enhancing decision-making capabilities.

Sewilam also presented Egypt’s digital twin project for the Ismailia Canal as a pioneering example of applying advanced technology to water management.

The project represents a significant step toward the digital transformation of the water system by integrating data and modern technologies into the monitoring and management of water resources and improving operational efficiency.

The minister further reviewed the state’s efforts to treat and reuse agricultural drainage water, describing the initiative as a key component of Egypt’s strategy to maximize the use of available water resources.

He also highlighted ongoing efforts to protect Egypt’s coastlines through environmentally friendly materials and nature-based solutions, helping mitigate the increasing impacts of climate change and safeguard vulnerable coastal areas.

Sewilam underscored the importance of good governance and institutional capacity-building in water resources management.

He pointed to the ministry’s efforts to strengthen the participation of water users through the establishment and support of Water User Associations, while also enhancing communication with members of the House of Representatives and the Senate.

These efforts, he said, promote greater coordination among the ministry, water users and legislative institutions in addressing water-related challenges.

The minister also highlighted a pioneering initiative launched by the Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation to train rural women in using water hyacinth to produce handicrafts. The initiative seeks to turn an environmental challenge into an opportunity for economic empowerment, income generation and job creation.

Sewilam affirmed that Egypt will continue to modernize and strengthen its water management system by integrating modern infrastructure, advanced technology, water reuse, nature-based solutions, sound governance and community participation under the second generation of the national water management system.

This integrated approach, he stressed, is essential to ensuring the long-term sustainability of Egypt’s water resources, strengthening water security and supporting the country’s broader development objectives.

World.title: Kim Jong Un’s powerful sister says she is ‘completely unaware’ if he contacted Trump
World.content:
Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, said she is “completely unaware” whether her brother communicated with US President Donald Trump, as Trump claimed this week.

Kim, one of North Korea’s top officials, acknowledged that her brother has a “great relationship” with Trump and “personally has good memories and feelings” for him. But in a statement released on state media Wednesday, she stopped short of confirming Trump’s claim of recent contact.

Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korea’s leader Kim Jong Un, attends a reception in the Great Hall of People following a military parade marking the 80th anniversary of victory over Japan and the end of World War II, in Beijing on September 3, 2025. Jade Gao/AFP/Getty Images

Trump told reporters Monday that Kim Jong Un had responded to his request for a conversation, shortly after the president demanded a sudden reduction in joint military drills with South Korea, a close and long-standing US ally.

Trump did not elaborate on the contact. He added Wednesday that he intends to meet Kim later this year, but he didn’t offer details and would not say whether he has exchanged any letters with North Korea’s leader.

In her statement, Kim Yo Jong said of the reported “communication” between Trump and her brother: “I am not aware of it at all, and perhaps it may be the only thing I do not know as regards the foreign policy of our supreme leadership.”

Kim’s statement is illuminating because she is one of her brother’s top lieutenants and a close confidant, routinely pictured alongside the North Korean leader and someone who often delivers important statements on behalf of the often secretive and opaque rgime.

Joint military drills have long irritated North Korea, and Kim Yo Jong said reducing them does not change “the provocative and offensive nature of them,” even though the US and South Korea frequently emphasize their defensive nature. Scaling the drills back should not be seen as “measure of goodwill,” Kim added.

Kim Jong Un and President Donald Trump met three times during Trump’s first term. KCNA VIA KNS/AFP/Getty Images

The annual joint exercises are usually scheduled to run for 10 days, but this year’s will last only five, at Washington’s request. They are designed to adapt to North Korea’s evolving capabilities and incorporate training to counter drones, GPS disruption and cyberattacks, a spokesperson for US Forces Korea said last week.

Sudden scale down of drills

Analysts have warned that by scaling down war games with South Korea, Trump risks working against his own stated goal of having Seoul assume more responsibility for its own defense.

Contained within the military exercises is training to give South Korea something it hasn’t had since the Korean War began in 1950: wartime operational control of the combined South Korea-US forces on the peninsula, analysts point out.

It’s a key goal for both countries. Once Seoul shows it can take on that burden, Washington can take a backseat in any future conflict, providing some firepower but letting South Korea assume most of the responsibility and cost of its defense.

Trump’s demand to scale back the drills – which were months in planning – came on the first day they joint exercises began.

Publicly, South Korea’s President Lee Jae Myung has welcomed Trump’s request, and reiterated that he supports dialogue with North Korea and wants to take more responsibility for its own defense.

“We sympathize with President Trump’s determination and effort to create conditions for dialogue to establish peace regime on the Korean Peninsula, even if it means scaling back the recent South Korea-US joint military exercise and field training exercises, and we pay tribute to that decision.” Lee said on X late Wednesday.

He added he “fully agrees” with Trump that South Korea “should take responsibility itself of security on the Korean Peninsula while building sufficient capability to independently defend the peninsula by rapidly increasing defense spending to achieve a defense expenditure of 3.5 percent of GDP.”

When calling for these exercises to be reduced, Trump cited his positive relationship with Kim Jong Un, a longtime US adversary, as well as Seoul’s lack of assistance for the war in Iran.

“I get along with him,” Trump told reporters Wednesday. “And you know what? The fact that I get along with him — that’s a good thing.”

Trump met with Kim three times for denuclearization talks during his first term, but those talks were ultimately unsuccessful, and North Korea’s nuclear weapons program has only grown since.

On Thursday, South Korea defense minister said he estimates North Korea now possesses between 80 and 120 nuclear warheads, a range significantly higher than Trump’s recent assertion that Pyongyang has ​57 nuclear weapons.

Trump took similar steps to scale back joint operations with South Korea during his first term. In March 2019, the two countries announced that their annual large-scale exercises would be reconfigured and take a reduced form.

This post has been updated with additional developments.

World.title: Trump criticism leads to rare criminal charges for Air Force officer who called for impeachment
World.content:
A US airman who was arrested twice, once on the steps of the US Capitol while calling for the impeachment of President Donald Trump, was officially criminally charged Monday for his comments, according to a charging document his attorney shared with CNN.

Maj. Jason Watson faces the following charges under the Uniform Code of Military Justice, according to the document: three violations of Article 88 for alleged “contemptuous” remarks about Trump, five violations of Article 92 for allegedly disobeying orders and two violations of Article 133 for alleged conduct unbecoming an officer.

The rare Article 88 charges are connected to the Air Force officer’s June interview with the Defenders of our Republic Substack newsletter, his July 1 protest in uniform at the US Capitol, and an August 17 CNN interview.

It can be considered a violation of the Uniform Code of Military Justice to participate in uniform in any overtly partisan activity, such as a political protest, or to use “contemptuous words” against the president and other high-ranking civilian officials. Many low-level offenses of these rules are resolved informally, but Watson’s violations were unusually high-profile.

Watson was first arrested in July while protesting in uniform at the US Capitol, and he was then arrested again last week just days after criticizing Trump again during a CNN interview. One of his attorneys, Chris Mutimer, told CNN that his client was ordered to remain in “pre-trial confinement” — an action analogous to a denial of bond in civilian court — pending legal action against him.

“Not only is (Trump) a failure as president, he is flagrantly violating the Constitution, breaking the law, engaged in rampant corruption, and is killing Americans,” Watson told CNN’s Erin Burnett during the interview. “And that is unacceptable to me.”

In July, Air Force Secretary Troy Meink said in a social media post that he expected all airmen to “comply with all laws and policies government personal conduct, political participation, and the wear of the uniform.”

“Americans place their trust in us,” Meink said. “We cannot, and will not, compromise the trust of the nation.”

The disobeying orders charges against Watson allege that he violated Defense Department regulations barring troops from speaking out in favor of partisan causes; “wrongfully” wore his uniform at a Capitol press conference; broke leave regulations by traveling to Washington, DC; and refused to wear his uniform to work the morning after his CNN interview.

Air Force prosecutors also alleged that Watson’s Capitol protest and CNN interview constituted “conduct unbecoming an officer.”

Mutimer, Watson’s attorney, told CNN’s Erin Burnett on “OutFront” that he spoke with his client Monday and “he is basically in solitary confinement for his safety.”

Mutimer said, “He truly believes in everything about our constitution and what it represents, and the oath that he swore, and he stands by the fact that he did this so others wouldn’t have to, and to share that to anyone who’s scared and feels alone.”

The founder of the organization that organized the protest in July, Jessica Denson of the Removal Coalition, told CNN at the time that Watson was aware of the risks of what he was doing and had reached out to them via email.

“We started having conversations and took this desire that he had to come out very seriously and thought about the best way to make his sacrifice worth it,” Denson said.

Military courts-martial leading to “contempt of officials” charges are rare — a CNN review only identified two such convictions that have occurred since the modern Uniform Code of Military Justice was enacted in 1951.

In 1965, an Army lieutenant was convicted of the charge after he participated in an off-base protest against the Vietnam War in El Paso, Texas. Lt. Henry Howe was sentenced to a dismissal from the service — the equivalent of a dishonorable discharge for an officer — and a year in the military prison at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas. Defense Secretary Robert McNamara ultimately granted parole to Howe, ending his sentence early.

The most recent Article 88 conviction came in 2021, when former Marine Corps Lt. Col. Stuart Scheller pleaded guilty to contempt of officials and other charges linked to a series of social media videos he published criticizing the Biden administration’s handling of the US military’s withdrawal from Afghanistan. Scheller, who was confined to the brig for a period of time before his trial, was sentenced to a $5,000 pay forfeiture and resigned from the Marine Corps sans-pension as part of a plea agreement.

The Trump administration has since appointed Scheller to serve as a senior adviser to the Pentagon’s undersecretary for personnel and readiness.

Frank Rosenblatt, a retired Army judge advocate and associate law professor at Mississippi Christian University, said to CNN that the standard for “contemptuous” words is “less than precise” in guidance provided to military judges and panel members (similar to jurors).

Rosenblatt said that “contemptuous” remarks under Article 88 must be “insulting, rude, and disdainful conduct, or otherwise disrespectfully attributing to another a quality of meanness, disreputableness, or worthlessness.”

He suggested that a pretrial hearing known as an Article 32 proceeding may be required to assess whether Watson’s remarks instead “are true or are fair criticisms” of the president.

It remains to be seen whether Watson’s case will be referred to trial, and whether that trial will be considered a special or general court-martial. Special courts-martial are roughly equivalent to misdemeanor trials, and general courts-martial are analogous to felony trials and can hand down more severe sentences.

The Air Force did not immediately respond to a request for comment sent on Monday. In an August 19 statement to CNN, an Air Force spokesperson said that Watson “is presumed innocent” and said that that Air Force District of Washington will oversee his trial “if (his) case is referred to a General Court-Martial.”

This story has been updated with additional details.

CNN’s Piper Hudspeth Blackburn, Carmen Conte Widman and Francesca Giuliani Hoffman contributed to this report.

Davis Winkie’s work at CNN is supported by a partnership between Outrider Foundation and Journalism Funding Partners (JFP). CNN retains full editorial control of the reporting.

World.title: As elections near, Netanyahu casts Turkey as Israel’s latest enemy
World.content:
Jerusalem —

The giant billboard on Tel Aviv’s main highway placed Turkey squarely at the center of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s election campaign. The image showed its president, Recep Tayyip Erdogan, alongside the leaders of Iran, Hezbollah and the mayor of New York City as adversaries of Israel under the slogan, “They want Netanyahu to lose. Don’t let them win.”

Just a few days later, Turkey became the center of Israel’s latest military confrontation as well.

Israeli jets struck the Abu al-Dahar airbase in northern Syria, targeting what officials said was an emerging Turkish military buildup that Israel viewed as a significant threat.

But with elections just over two months away, the strike’s proximity to Netanyahu’s campaign messaging has fueled a debate in Israel and abroad: is Netanyahu preempting a genuine strategic threat or amplifying one to boost his ballot-box standing?

Throughout much of his decades-long political career, Netanyahu has portrayed himself as “Mr. Security,” equipped to confront any threats facing Israel. He is also a shrewd political operator with a long record of turning crises to his advantage.

Tom Barrack, US President Donald Trump’s envoy to Syria and ambassador to Turkey, issued a rare public rebuke to Israel over the strike, calling it an “unnecessary escalation.” In an interview with podcaster Mario Nawfal, Barrack suggested a political motive, floating a “theory” that Israel “simply tried to bait Turkey.” He called it “a very aggressive move, but one that might play well going into elections.”

Officially, Israel has framed the attack as a pure operational necessity: Netanyahu and his Defense Minister Israel Katz have both said Israeli intelligence indicated Turkey was preparing to install forces and equipment at the airbase.

An Israeli military source told CNN the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) had gathered intelligence on Turkey’s plans to deploy personnel, drones and air-defense systems at the site. Such a deployment, the source said, could constrain Israel’s freedom of action in Syrian airspace and alter the strategic balance in the area. The intelligence, a second source said, was shared with the Trump administration and with Syria’s President Ahmed Al-Sharaa. Israel and Syria have held deconfliction talks over the past year, reaching what Netanyahu has described as a “status quo in security matters.”

Abu al-Duhur airbase following strikes, in Syria, on August 18, 2026. Reuters

On Sunday, Roman Goffman, the chief of Israel’s Mossad intelligence agency, met again with Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani in Jordan to ease the latest tensions, according to the Syrian state news agency.

Still, Turkey, the US and some of Netanyahu’s domestic political rivals pointed to the timing. Rejecting the Israeli account as “untenable,” Turkey accused Netanyahu of “pursuing expansionist and destabilizing policies in the region” ahead of the October vote. The Turkish government said it would continue to cooperate with the Syrian government “on a legitimate basis for the establishment of peace, stability, and prosperity.”

Netanyahu brands Erdogan an ‘antisemitic tyrant’

Netanyahu and Katz have pushed back on the political motivation narrative, warning instead of an impending Turkish footprint in Syria. “We will not tolerate a military Turkish presence taking root in Syria and threatening Israel,” Netanyahu said last week.

Meanwhile, the Israeli prime minister also sharpened his already-combative rhetoric against Erdogan. On Friday, Netanyahu’s office branded Erdogan in an X post as an “antisemitic tyrant who oppresses his own people.”

Netanyahu and Erdogan have a long-running public feud, which intensified dramatically during the wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. Erdogan has called Netanyahu a war criminal and repeatedly accused Israel of atrocities in Gaza; Netanyahu has accused Erdogan of supporting Hamas. Recently, Netanyahu came out against the sale of US F-35 fighter jets to Ankara, warning of Erdogan’s “aggressive ambitions” in the region.

Amos Harel, a senior security analyst for the leftwing Haaretz newspaper, says that both the security and political explanations are relevant. “There are indeed indications that Erdogan’s approach toward Israel is very hostile, and that Turkey is undertaking various military moves in Syria, some of which concern the IDF – including at that specific airport,” he said, citing intelligence on Turkish plans to deploy advisers, drones, and air-defense systems.

At the same time, Harel told CNN, “it is also completely clear Netanyahu is pursuing a new and aggressive line,” one he frames as a lesson from the October 7, 2023 attack on Israel: strike first, on every front, while establishing security buffer zones along Israel’s borders in Gaza, Lebanon, and Syria. The Israeli military seized a 400 square kilometer buffer zone inside Syria after the 2024 collapse of the Assad regime and has occupied it since.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, (C-R), and his wife, Sara, (C-L) cast their ballot at his party Likud’s main polling station during primary elections ahead of Israel’s general election in October in Jerusalem on August 17, 2026. Ohard Zwigenberg/Pool/AFP/Getty Images

But the political context of the latest war of words has only deepened the suspicions of some of Netanyahu’s critics. Opposition leader Yair Lapid, who defended the operation itself as justified, criticized the triumphant Israeli statements that followed. “In the Middle East, striking when necessary is important. But if you struck, stay quiet,” he said.

Yair Golan, leader of the leftwing Democrats party, called the operation “provocative and dangerous.” Former prime minister Ehud Barak went further, writing on social media that the escalation “strongly reeks of a political intention to go into elections amid a series of security tensions designed to alarm the public.”

With Netanyahu and his political bloc currently trailing in the polls, his critics are concerned that a new security crisis could fundamentally shift the political landscape and help him control the campaign agenda.

“Netanyahu is known to believe that a security emergency is a last-resort option that could reshuffle the deck and improve his chances of surviving these elections,” Harel said. And with Trump constraining Israel’s war on Iran and limiting its military actions in Gaza and Lebanon, he said, “Turkey-Syria becomes a potential front. This raises, at the very least, a strong suspicion that political considerations are involved as well.”

World.title: Secret Service aware of Iranian state media video threatening life of Barron Trump
World.content:
The US Secret Service says it’s aware of a video aired by Iran’s state broadcaster appearing to threaten the life of Barron Trump, the youngest son of President Donald Trump.

Hardline Iranian media have repeatedly featured content threatening the life of President Trump and his family following the assassination of its former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and many of his family members at the outset of the US-Israeli war with Iran in February.

While there have previously been threats to first lady Melania Trump, this appears to be the first time their son Barron has been publicly singled out.

“The US Secret Service is aware of the video and investigates anything that can be perceived as a threat toward our protectees,” Secret Service spokesperson Nate Herring told CNN in a statement. “Out of concern for operational security, we do not discuss matters of protective intelligence.”

The nearly three-minute video begins with an English language graphic reading: “Where to kill Barron Trump?!,” and features stylized graphics showing locations where the younger Trump is publicly known to spend time, including Trump Tower in New York.

Towards the end of the video, the narrator suggested people were “eagerly waiting to receive our $10 million reward.”

The video was broadcast over the weekend by Iranian broadcaster IRIB, a state media outlet considered to be aligned with hardliners in the Iranian regime. The head of the broadcaster is directly appointed by Iran’s supreme leader.

A federal law enforcement source told CNN that the video is part of a campaign of videos from Iran targeting the Trump family and Trump himself. Some of the videos have included movement details and suggestions for killing members of the president’s family.

US First Lady Melania Trump, left, and US President Donald Trump arrive for a Fostering the Future event in the Rose Garden of the White House in Washington, DC, US, on Thursday, August 20, 2026. Yuri Gripas/Abaca/Bloomberg/Getty Images

The source said that protective operations are constantly moved and adjusted based on an array of security information from the Secret Service, other agencies, police and other countries.

CNN has reached out to the White House for comment.

President Trump has publicly discussed the Iranian threats on his life, saying in July: “I’m on whatever list… so far, I guess I’ve been a bit lucky, but maybe that doesn’t last very long. These are evil, sick people.”

He made those comment at the NATO summit in Turkey, before he secretly slipped out of the country on an alternate military plane, which he boarded while hidden inside a catering truck, as part of an elaborate ruse prompted by an Iranian threat.

A person familiar with the matter told CNN that threat involved a shoulder-fired missile and was a specific enough threat that officials feared Trump’s life would be at enormous risk if he flew on either version of Air Force One.

The US government has long warned that Iran may try to kill Trump, ever since the 2020 drone strike he ordered which killed top Iranian general Qasem Soleimani.

During the dayslong funeral events for the late Khamenei in July, regime loyalists were seen holding posters with the words “Kill Trump” and offering a bounty for whoever avenged their leader’s death.

Anti-American displays, including chants of “Death to America” and flag burnings, have been a constant of state-organized rallies in Iran since the Islamic Revolution brought the theocratic regime to power in 1979.

World.title: Liberia: How Five European Outcasts Flew Under the Radar In a Bid to Make Liberia a Narco State
World.content:
Two Croatians. A Ukrainian. A Serbian and a Spaniard, charged earlier in the same sprawling case. Long before anyone in Monrovia knew their names, these five men had already made themselves at home — in government offices, in run-down neighborhoods, in the easy, ordinary friendships that make a foreigner stop being a stranger. It was, investigators say, exactly the kind of access a narco state is built on.

By Rodney D. Sieh | [email protected]

MONROVIA — In the years before anyone in this country had reason to say the words “US$319 million” in the same breath as Monrovia, three men were already comfortable here. Nikola Ivancic, Mihovil Vrovac and Taras Zadereiko did not slip into Liberia as strangers passing through on false papers and quick exits. They arrived, they stayed, and they built lives — learning the rhythms of Liberian life, making friends in low places and in high ones, until the line between “foreign businessman” and “fixture of the community” had all but disappeared. By the time investigators finally traced a multimillion-dollar cocaine operation running along the airport highway near Duazon and Roberts International Airport — a case that would produce multiple arrests, an indictment of 12 individuals, and court proceedings still unfolding today — these European outcasts had already done the hard part. They had made themselves at home.

A FrontPageAfrica investigation has found that all three men also carry Ghanaian passports — a small detail that says almost as much about how easily the region’s documentation systems can be bent as it does about the men themselves.
