World.title: Netanyahu got his Iran war, but maybe not his desired result
World.content:
Jerusalem – After decades of urging the United States to attack Iran, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu finally got his wish. But after six months of inconclusive hostilities, Israel may ultimately find itself in a worse position than it was before the war.

The Islamic republic, which Netanyahu has long cast as an existential threat, has not only survived but appears emboldened.

Underlying Netanyahu’s dilemma have been the wild swings in the approach of US President Donald Trump, who joined Israel in launching the conflict in late February, but by April abruptly called a ceasefire and sought a negotiated settlement in the face of souring public opinion and soaring oil prices.

“It’s a colossal failure of Israeli strategy regarding Iran,” said Danny Citrinowicz, a former top Israeli intelligence analyst on Iran who is now at the Tel Aviv-based Institute for National Security Studies.

“Yes, we had operational achievements, but strategically we’ve failed.”

Israel on the very first day killed Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, the supreme leader who ruthlessly suppressed dissent in Iran, including mass protests earlier this year, and backed virulently anti-Israeli groups like Hamas, which led the October 7, 2023 attacks.

But Khamenei was also seen as holding back on full-blown pursuit of nuclear weapons, a reluctance that could now end if the Islamic republic feels it has lost its conventional deterrents.

While Trump has recently declared economic warfare on Iran and periodically ordered new strikes, he has voiced support for a deal that would see sanctions relief.

Netanyahu had adamantly rejected a 2015 nuclear deal negotiated by then-president Barack Obama.

Citrinowicz said Israel now had a choice between accepting a new nuclear deal that would strengthen Iran, or trying to weaken it further and increasing the risk that it will seek a nuclear weapon.

“Israel is trying to do both but it’s not going to work,” he said.

– Degrading vs toppling –

An extraordinary 92 percent of Israelis believe Iran won or gained more from the conflict, according to a June survey by the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in collaboration with the Agam Institute — a warning sign for Netanyahu ahead of October 27 elections.

Netanyahu had said he was hoping to “create conditions for regime change” but did not explicitly make toppling the Islamic republic his goal.

Instead, some see Netanyahu following an Israeli playbook witnessed in Gaza, Lebanon and Syria — inflict overwhelming damage that will allow Israel to return and attack later as it sees fit, a strategy the country euphemistically calls “mowing the grass”.

“Netanyahu doesn’t see this as a loss. He has the United States directly at war with Iran, with Israel for now on the sidelines,” one foreign diplomat based in Israel told AFP on condition of anonymity.

Iranian counter-strikes killed 25 people in Israel and four in the occupied West Bank, but Iran has focused its fire more recently on Gulf Arab states that provide bases for US troops.

Alex Grinberg, a senior fellow focused on Iran at the Turan Research Center, said the war set back Iran significantly by eliminating infrastructure and people in the nuclear programme and imposing massive economic damage.

“I think Israel did achieve its strategic goals, meaning denying the Iranian regime the strategic capacity to threaten Israel,” he said, while casting doubt on the prospects for a favourable US-Iran deal.

– Risking public opinion –

The war has already complicated Israel’s relationship with its most crucial ally, and may preclude any possibility of a future reconciliation with the Iranian people.

The increasingly unpopular conflict triggered a surge of criticism of Israel in the United States, where its war against Hamas in Gaza had already dealt a heavy blow to its standing in the public eye.

Public perceptions of Israel inside Iran are difficult to gauge, as polling is difficult, but the two countries were allies before the Islamic revolution, and protests before the war indicated noticeable public opposition to the clerical government.

And while Netanyahu and Trump have both publicly professed to support the Iranian people, the US and Israel have issued apocalyptic threats over the course of the war that appeared to make little distinction between the Islamic republic and its citizens, and their strikes have destroyed infrastructure including top universities.

There is “a real possibility of lasting hostility towards Israel and the United States, particularly if the war is remembered through civilian casualties and damage to the country rather than solely through the removal of senior regime figures”, said Liora Hendelman-Baavur, a senior research fellow at the Alliance Center for Iranian Studies at Tel Aviv University.

“That hostility would not necessarily restore the Islamic republic’s legitimacy, but it could complicate future relations long after the present leadership has changed.”

World.title: Iraq, Qatar provide oil for loading inside Hormuz via bids
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Trade sources reported on Monday that Iraq’s national oil marketer, SOMO, and QatarEnergy are presenting crude oil through unusual bids that mandate purchasers to load cargoes within the Strait of Hormuz.

SOMO announced that it is offering Basrah Medium and Basrah Heavy crude for loading in September from either the Basrah oil port or a single point mooring, along with the necessary supporting facilities, as reported by Reuters.

QatarEnergy provided free-on-board oil loading at al-Shaheen, Qatar Marine, and Qatar Land ports in September and October.

Earlier, SOMO provided substantial discounts on Basrah crude in August to entice customers to load shipments from the Strait of Hormuz.

SOMO asked potential term purchasers to designate contractual volumes of Basrah Medium or Basrah Heavy crude for complimentary onboard delivery from the Basrah Oil Terminal or other port-related infrastructure.

Iraq’s oil marketer provided discounts ranging between $25 and $27 per barrel on Basrah Medium, according to the loading period. It provided discounts of $27.80 to $29.80 a barrel for Basrah Heavy.

Maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz decreased due to ongoing military operations in the region and heightened shipping security risks.

The significant price reduction aims to compensate for rising maritime insurance costs and freight expenses by transferring transit risk to purchasers.

World.title: Iraq to introduce new banknotes with three zeros removed
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq intends to remove three zeros from its currency to modernize financial transactions, reduce physical cash circulation, and return stockpiled funds to the official banking system.

Under the suggestion, a 25,000-Iraqi dinar note would become 25 Iraqi dinars, but the currency’s purchasing power and true financial value would stay unaffected.

According to Jamal Kocher, a Kurdish member of the Iraqi parliament’s finance committee, Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has asked for the removal of zeros from invoices.

Kocher told The New Region that if the plan is implemented, 1,000 Iraqi dinars would be converted to one dinar, while 25,000 dinars would be equivalent to 25 dinars.

Earlier in August, Communications Minister Mustafa Sanad acknowledged the plan to eliminate the zeros and modify the currency.

The redenomination strategy aims to bring undeclared cash, estimated to be between 8 and 10 trillion Iraqi dinars that are currently held outside banks, back into official channels. This initiative seeks to combat crime, corruption, and money laundering.

According to the idea, everyday prices, incomes, and savings will alter correspondingly, resulting in a direct mathematical shift rather than a change in actual wealth.

Iraq has sought printing partners in the United Kingdom and Australia, as well as its traditional suppliers in France and Germany, to create an estimated 7.5 billion new banknotes.

While government officials such as the Communications Minister and Finance Committee members have emphasized the importance of an official implementation date, the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) has yet to present a formal draft bill to parliament.

World.title: FSSAI crackdown: Food companies withdraw ‘100%’ and health claims after notices
World.content:
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (

) on Tuesday said several major food business operators (FBOs) had taken corrective action following notices issued over misleading labels, claims and other regulatory violations.

In a post on X, the food regulator said the measures included withdrawal of misleading label claims and changes to product packaging to ensure consumer safety and regulatory compliance.

Among the companies named by FSSAI were Amway India Enterprises, Juza Foods, Mondelez India Foods and Sapiens Labs, while another case involved a product marketed by Vichi Agro Products and processed and packed by J J Foods.

Amway removes 'Energy Drink' and '100%' claims

FSSAI said Amway India Enterprises Pvt Ltd had accepted its directions and removed the term "Energy Drink" from its XS product range.

According to the regulator, the product was a caffeinated beverage licensed under food category 14.1, but carried the term "Energy Drink". Amway confirmed that it had removed the word "Energy" from its product artwork, website and promotional materials.

FSSAI said Amway had clarified that the descriptor was originally adopted in good faith following an FSSAI advisory issued in March 2024. The company said revised packaging would take effect from the next production cycle in August 2026.





Amway also requested permission to sell existing stock carrying the earlier artwork until the inventory was exhausted in the ordinary course of trade, while the revised packaging is introduced.

In a separate case, FSSAI said Amway had also removed the term "100%" from its product name "100% Pure Coconut Oil", citing violations related to food labelling and advertising claims.

The company submitted a compliance response confirming that it had removed the claim from its packaging and promotional material and discontinued old stock from sales channels.

Revised packaging has been finalised and is in production, with the new packaging expected to be rolled out progressively from September-October 2026, along with updated website listings.

Juza Foods agrees to remove baby food claims

FSSAI also highlighted action taken by Juza Foods, Malappuram, Kerala, over multiple claims made for its baby food products.

The regulator listed claims including "pure", "natural", "traditional", "no artificial colours, flavours or preservatives" and "Your baby's 1st taste of Real Nutrition".

It also flagged health claims such as products being "ideal for sensitive babies", "easy to digest", offering "better absorption", and helping to "boost immunity" and "support stronger bones".

FSSAI also cited claims including "100% Ragi", "100% vegan", "100% Kerala Banana powder" and "100% sweet potato powder", along with comparative claims that the products contained "10X the calcium of wheat and rice" and "3X the calcium of Milk".

The regulator further said the company had been conducting its food business through an online website without having e-commerce listed as a Kind of Business in its licence.

Juza Foods acknowledged the violations and agreed to remove the misleading claims, FSSAI said. Its selling website has been shut down until the rectification is completed, while the company has applied for modification of its licence and for an e-commerce category.

Products delisted, s withdrawn

In another case, FSSAI said a product marketed by Vichi Agro Products Pvt Ltd and processed and packed by J J Foods was flagged over a misleading trade name.

A response received from Flipkart stated that the food business operator had delisted the product from the platform.

FSSAI also said Mondelez India Foods Pvt Ltd had withdrawn claims and s from e-commerce platforms following action over misleading health claims and nutrient comparative claims.

Sapiens Labs similarly submitted a response and withdrew all claims and s after FSSAI flagged a misleading claim on its own initiative.

Action comes amid wider FSSAI enforcement drive

The latest update comes amid a broader FSSAI enforcement drive against misleading s, false claims and labelling violations.

World.title: China's Xi Jinping to visit India with 400-member delegation for Brics: Report
World.content:
Chinese President Xi Jinping is likely to attend next monthâs BRICS summit in New Delhi with a large delegation, more than double the Chinese contingent that accompanied him on his last India visit in 2019.

Xiâs expected visit on September 12-13 with 400 officials, marking his first trip to India in seven years and comes as the two countries work to stabilise ties after years of tensions over their disputed border, reported Reuters, citing sources.

Two Indian sources said Xi was likely to be accompanied by around 400 officials, compared with fewer than 200 during his 2019 visit. âChinese officials are busy finalising hotels and security protocols,â one Indian source with direct knowledge told Reuters.

Xiâs final travel plans and the agenda for any possible bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi are yet to be finalised, the sources said.

The Chinese foreign ministry said, âChina attaches great importance to and actively participates in BRICS cooperation, and supports India, the current chair, in successfully hosting this year's BRICS summit.â

âWe currently have no information available to provideâ about Xiâs visit, it added.





The expected visit comes as India and China continue high-level efforts to improve ties. National Security Advisor Ajit Doval on Tuesday met Chinese Vice President Han Zheng in Beijing, with the two sides discussing ways to maintain peace and tranquillity along the border and strengthen relations across economic, political and multilateral platforms.

âOn 25 August, NSA and Special Representative on the India-China Boundary Question, Ajit Doval called on Han Zheng, Vice President of the People's Republic of China,â the Embassy of India in China said.



The two sides discussed strengthening peace and tranquillity in the border areas and improving bilateral ties âacross economic, political and multilateral foraâ, the embassy said.

Doval is in Beijing for the 25th round of Special Representatives talks on the India-China boundary question with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi. The talks are expected to cover the border dispute as well as bilateral, regional and international issues.

India-China ties were badly strained after the 2020 Galwan Valley clash, in which 20 Indian and four Chinese soldiers were killed. The confrontation led to a prolonged military stand-off along the Line of Actual Control before the two sides reached a disengagement agreement in October 2024.

Relations have improved gradually since then, with a series of high-level engagements between Modi and Xi. Their possible meeting in New Delhi during the BRICS summit could give fresh momentum to those efforts.

World.title: India mulls annual dope tests on all commercial pilots on a random basis
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Commercial pilots in India could soon be subjected to annual dope tests that may be conducted at random for the surprise factor. After the pilot in command of Air Indiaâs Aug 4 Phuket-Delhi flight had reportedly tested positive, govt had directed the Directorate General of Civil Aviation to review the existing rules for these tests.

âThe DGCA is having stakeholder consultation right now on what the current regulation says and how do we ensure there is a strict policy around this (drug tests for pilots) in the future. This consultation is going on right now. There are multiple ways of approaching this dope test. So right now the rule says 10% across the overall pilot network but just like I said DGCA is engaging and one of the opinions from our side is that everyone has to go through it in the year at a random time,â Union aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu said Tuesday.

âWe have to see how all the stakeholders are going to respond to this because one is the safety aspect of to ensure safety intact and the second is the operational impact. That also has to be taken into consideration.. We are going to balance both. If we do 100%, if every pilot has to go through the dope test once a year, then what can happen, what can be the impact of that, that is what DGCA is looking at,â Naidu added.

World.title: BPSC exam row, 'dogs bark' remark: What has triggered fresh student protests in Bihar
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Chaotic scenes unfolded in Biharâs Patna on Tuesday as protesting students clashed with police during a massive protest over alleged irregularities in the 70th BPSC examination.

The protest was met with a heavy police deployment, with barricades erected to stop the students from marching.

Police also used water cannons as protesters attempted to push past the barricades.

Later, the Samrat Choudhary-led government claimed it had addressed âalmost all issuesâ raised by the students. The protesters, however, said several long-standing demands remained unresolved and continued their agitation.

The students marched from Gandhi Maidan towards Raj Bhavan.

The protesting students also broke the barricades in bid to gherao chief minister's residence.

The protest has also brought into focus delays in recruitment examinations, the proposed format of the Teacher Recruitment Examination-4 (TRE-4), alleged paper leaks and demands for greater transparency in Bihar's recruitment system.

Govt says students' issues have been addressed

Bihar education minister Mithilesh Tiwari said the government had resolved the issues raised by the students and maintained that its doors remained open for further dialogue.





"All the issues over which the students were staging a sit-in have been resolved. It is not as if the student agitation was the sole reason for this; it is the government's very intent to resolve the problems faced by our youth in a timely manner. We have addressed every issue raised by the youth. I was surprised to hear a person who has never even taken a board exam offering suggestions on examinations. That is why I would say to

to enroll in a Bihar government school, pass the tenth-grade exam, and then come back to offer us suggestions on examinations," Tiwari said.

The minister said that almost all the demands had been met and invited students to approach the government with any remaining concerns.

"We have met almost all the students' demands. For any students who wish to convey further points to the government, the doors for dialogue remain wide open. Let the students come, talk, and get their issues resolved; the government belongs to them," he said.

However, the protesters said their concerns had not been fully addressed and that problems related to the education system, examination paper leaks and delayed recruitment continued.

'Do you need 1,800 years?' Students question recruitment delays

Protester Vikas Bhatt said the students were demanding improvements in Bihar's education system and action against repeated examination paper leaks.

"Our demand is that the education system in Bihar be improved. We are raising issues regarding the frequent exam paper leaks in the state. Look at the recruitment for librarians, it hasn't happened for 18 years; do you need 1,800 years? Whenever we stage a protest, they simply offer assurances and leave it at that.

How can things go on like this? Three recruitment drives were announced through the BSSC, but it has been three years.

We have repeatedly besieged the BSSC commission, demanding that the exam dates be announced. Despite this, they keep asking for 15 days' time. Apart from the BPSC, there isn't a single commission in Bihar that issues an annual calendar," Bhatt said.

The students are demanding the cancellation of the 70th BPSC examination over allegations of irregularities and paper leaks.

The agitation has also centred on the proposed TRE-4 examination. Students have opposed the proposal to conduct the examination in two phases across Bihar and are demanding that it be held in a single phase.

They have also sought the immediate release of the official TRE-4 .

Students break through barricades during Raj Bhavan march

As the protest continued, students marched from Gandhi Maidan towards Raj Bhavan. Some protesters broke through police barricades and attempted to move towards the restricted area.

Police used water cannons to disperse the crowd, while several protesters were detained.

DSP Kamakhya Narayan Singh said the police would not allow the protesters to enter the restricted area, although he expressed hope that the ongoing talks between students and senior officials would lead to a resolution.

"We will stop them; we won't let them proceed further. However, the dialogue has been positive, and we hope the students will agree.

They have raised several issues with the senior officials, and the outcome has been positive. So, I expect the turnout to be lower and that they will agree. If they don't, we will stop them right here. We won't allow them to enter the restricted area," Singh said.

Congress leader Sushil Kumar, who was present at the protest site, said the government had failed to give assurances on several key demands.

"We want to state clearly that a single-stage examination must be implemented for TRE 4.0 at all costs, and negative marking should be abolished.

There are numerous other issues as well, regarding the BPSC, BSSC, Sub-Inspector recruitment. The government has offered no assurances on any of these points. We have urged the Chief Minister to hold a dialogue; he should invite our delegation for talks. We have been on a hunger strike for nine days, yet no one is willing to listen to us.

Just imagine, had the government engaged in dialogue, this situation would not have arisen.

We are heading towards the Chief Minister's residence; the Chief Minister should hold talks, and our delegation will go there for the discussion," Kumar told news agency ANI.

JD(U) says govt is serious about students' concerns

JD(U) leader Shravan Kumar said the Bihar government was taking the concerns of students and job seekers seriously and was acting according to established rules and legal provisions.

"The government is taking the demands and concerns of students and job seekers seriously.

Everything is being done for them in accordance with established rules, laws, and provisions. Bihar is the first state in the country to have made such large-scale recruitments across government departments," Kumar said.

He also pointed to the government's employment target for the 2025-2030 period and urged young people not to be influenced by the opposition.

"It is Nitish Kumar's resolve to provide 10 million (1 crore) jobs and employment opportunities to the people of Bihar between 2025 and 2030.

Recruitments are taking place in every sector, and vacancies are being announced in every department. I urge our youth to exercise patience and not fall for the opposition's ploys; they are not going to provide jobs. They merely intend to exploit your hard work and sweat to further their own political interests.

Beware of them," he added.

Tejashwi writes to Samrat Choudhary

Meanwhile, Bihar leader of opposition Tejashwi Yadav has written to chief minister Samrat Choudhary over the ongoing BPSC row, urging the government not to ignore the students' demands and to hold talks for an early resolution.

Tejashwi has demanded that TRE-4 be conducted as a single examination across the state. He has also sought an end to what he described as discrimination against Hindi-speaking candidates in the BPSC Civil Services Main Examination and interview.

The RJD leader has further demanded complete transparency in all competitive examinations, including those for Sub-Inspector, Constable, BSSC and BPSC recruitments.

Among his other demands are a high-level independent inquiry into alleged irregularities in past examinations, strict action against recruitment mafias and time-bound schedules for all pending tests.

He has specifically called for clear timelines for the BSSC Intermediate, CGL, ASO, BSO, Librarian and Accountant recruitment examinations.

RJD scion Tejashwi remark also followed BPSC official's "dog-barking" remark.

Bihar LoP also called for action for his remark referring to students.

Bihar launches monthly student support camps

Amid the continuing protests, the Bihar government on Tuesday launched the monthly 'Vidyarthi Sahyog Shivir' or student support camps to address students' grievances.

The camps will be organised at educational institutions on the fourth Tuesday of every month, chief minister Samrat Choudhary said in a social media post.

"The Bihar government is launching Vidyarthi Sahyog Shivir starting today to ensure prompt resolution of students' grievances.

These camps will be organised at educational institutions on the fourth Tuesday of every month," Choudhary wrote.

The camps will allow students to raise their grievances directly with the concerned government officials. Students will also be able to register complaints online and track their status through the portal and Helpline 1100.

World.title: Delhi HC abates Sajjan Kumar’s appeal against conviction in 1984 riots case following his death
World.content:
Following his death last week, the Delhi High Court on Tuesday (August 25, 2026) closed an appeal by former Congress MP Sajjan Kumar challenging his conviction in a murder case arising from the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.

Sajjan Kumar, who was serving two life sentences in Tihar jail in connection with the 1984 riots, died on August 20.

"In view thereof, the present appeal would abate," a bench of justices Prathiba M Singh and Vikas Mahajan said.

This case was about the killings of Jaswant Singh and his son Tarundeep Singh in Saraswati Vihar on November 1, 1984.

Anti-Sikh riots broke out in Delhi after the assassination of the then prime minister Indira Gandhi on October 31, 1984, by her Sikh bodyguards.

Kumar was awarded life imprisonment in the case on February 25, 2025, by a trial court here after his conviction on February 12, 2025.

The trial court had said though the killings of "two innocent persons" were no less an offence, it was not a "rarest of rare case" warranting the imposition of the death penalty.

The trial court awarded life imprisonment to Kumar for being part of the mob which set afire the house of the victims and "brutally killed" the two victims besides looting their belongings.

It had also imposed a fine of around ₹2.4 lakh on Kumar.

Earlier, Kumar was sentenced to life imprisonment by the Delhi High Court on December 17, 2018, in another case related to the killing of five Sikhs and the burning of a gurdwara during the anti-Sikh riots.

Wearing a headscarf has not been established as an ‘essential religious practice’ for women in Islam: Allahabad HC
World.content:
The AllahabadHigh Court recently held that wearing a headscarf could not be established as an “essential religious practice” of Islam. The observation was made in a case involving a Muslim student’s demand to wear a hijab with her school uniform.

Also read | Allahabad HC asks for two adult sisters to be brought before it in religious conversion and marriage case

A Division Bench of Justices J.J. Munir and Indrajeet Shukla, in an order of August 21, 2026, dismissed the petition filed by a Class 11 student seeking permission to wear a headscarf along with the prescribed uniform at the Tagore Public School in Prayagraj.

In her plea, the student had argued that wearing the scarf was an essential religious practice protected by her fundamental rights under Articles 14 and 19(1)(a) of the Constitution. She had worn a headscarf at the same school from Class 6 onwards without objection, she said.

The fact that the student had worn the scarf for several years did not create an enforceable right to compel the school to relax or alter its uniform policy, the High Court said.

“We have perused the photographs from various classes relating to the petitioner. Except for her, no other girl student is donning the headscarf, even those belonging to the same religious community as the petitioner. Wherever this issue has arisen, the High Courts have been unanimous in opinion that wearing a headscarf is not essential part of the Islamic faith for a woman to don, in the absence of which faith would be jeopardized,” the HC said.

No factual foundation had been laid nor material placed on record to establish a case that the donning of a headscarf was an essential part of religion for a Muslim female, forsaking which would oust the girl or woman concerned from the faith that she professed and practised, the High Court said.

The Allahabad High Court relied on earlier judgments by the Bombay High Court and Karnataka High Court concerning hijab. The Bombay High Court held that not wearing a head covering in an all-girls section did not violate essential Islamic practices. A Karnataka Full Bench similarly found the hijab was not an essential religious practice, while noting the Supreme Court’s split verdict.

The Allahabad HC concluded that the dispute was principally about compliance with an institutional dress code rather than interference with the student’s freedom of faith.

“The school in this case does not seek to curtail the petitioner’s freedom of faith at all. All that they require is conformity to institutional discipline, of which a uniform is an essential part. In the event individual students were permitted to aid or depart even a little bit from the prescribed uniform on subjective grounds, it would militate against the idea of a uniform. It would transfer the authority to determine school discipline from the institution to individual students,” the High Court said.
